options.name: O1. Serving fix: enable prefix caching with sub-block matching (--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 16)
options.description: The current run has prefix caching DISABLED (log: enable_prefix_caching=False; /metrics: vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total = 0), so the 0.0% hit rate is not only the 4176-token block problem. The installed vLLM 0.26.0 already has --prefix-match-unit ('the finest token boundary a prefix-cache hit can land on ... can be set finer than the physical KV cache block sizes (e.g. 32 vs a 1024-token hybrid-model block) as long as every KV cache group's block_size is divisible by it'). 4176 = 16 x 261, so 16 is a legal unit. nemotron_h.py in the installed vLLM declares SupportsMambaPrefixCaching.
options.how_it_applies_here: Every LLM call re-prefills the 2,710-token static system prompt (measured with /tokenize: schema 815 + rules 304 + 11 few-shots 1,591) and the 504-token answer system prompt. With sub-block caching both become cache hits after the first request; only the ~40-token question and the rows are prefilled. Requires a relaunch of the 'llm' label via ZRT (team decision; ~4 min with cached FlashInfer kernels).
options.expected_token_effect: Billed/reported prompt tokens unchanged (usage still counts them); computed prefill drops from ~3,600 to ~900 tokens per LLM question (rows + question only).
options.expected_latency_effect: About -0.5 to -0.7 s per LLM question (2,710 tokens at the measured ~5.5k tok/s prefill is ~0.5 s per call A; call B's 504-token system prompt ~0.1 s). Decode (45 tok/s) is the real bottleneck, so this is a ~10% wall-time gain, not a 2x.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: None (bit-identical semantics; caching is transparent).
options.effort: 1-2 hours: change the zrt launch --extra flags, relaunch, verify vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total > 0 and re-run the benchmark.
options.risks: PR #46384 (merged 2026-07-12) was demonstrated on Qwen3.5; behaviour with NemotronH FP8 + Mamba2 on sm_121a in 0.26.0 is unverified. Issue #39809 reports crashes combining Mamba prefix caching with MTP speculative decoding (0.19.0), so caching may preclude future speculative decoding. The shared GPU also serves the vision model; a relaunch briefly interrupts the team's LLM.

evidence.claim: Current run: enable_prefix_caching=False, speculative_config=None; attention block size set to 4176 tokens 'to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size'; /metrics prefix_cache_queries_total = 0.0
--prefix-match-unit exists in installed vLLM 0.26.0 (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py, vllm/config/cache.py, vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py); help text quoted above

PR 'support partial prefix cache hit for hybrid model' introduces prefix_match_unit; example: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 16; merged 2026-07-12
Without sub-block matching, hybrid models get ~0% hit below one block and 95.4% once a full block is shared (479 tokens: 0%, 552 tokens: 95.4%); QPS dropped from 200 to <100 across the threshold
Mamba prefix caching + MTP speculative decoding crashes on startup for NemotronH (vLLM 0.19.0); workaround is to disable MTP when prefix caching is on

options.name: O2. Schema-specialised grammar-constrained Cypher decoding (EBNF generated from the Neo4j schema, decoded with xgrammar)
options.description: Instead of a generic Cypher grammar, auto-generate an EBNF from schema.cypher + DATA_MODEL: labels, relationship types WITH their legal direction and endpoint labels baked into the pattern rules, property names per label, enumerated status/source values, $now, a bounded clause set (MATCH/OPTIONAL MATCH/WHERE/WITH/RETURN/ORDER BY/LIMIT, a whitelist of functions). Property hallucination, wrong labels, reversed ABOUT/AFFECTS direction and write clauses become unrepresentable; the existing regex guard stays as defence in depth.
options.how_it_applies_here: The adversarial review found ~1/3 of non-templated questions fail on invented property names, reversed direction and over-filtering. Two of those three classes are structural and a schema-grammar removes them by construction (over-filtering is semantic and needs O3/O4). The schema is fixed and tiny (~30 properties, ~10 rel types), which is exactly when a hand-checkable grammar is feasible. EBNF structured outputs via xgrammar already work on this endpoint (stated in the task context).
options.expected_token_effect: Neutral on the first call; fewer repair rounds (each repair re-sends ~2.7k prompt + ~120 completion tokens). Completion tokens can be capped tighter because the grammar disallows prose.
options.expected_latency_effect: xgrammar mask overhead is near-zero per token; net effect is positive whenever a repair round (~3 s) is avoided. Grammar compile is cached by vLLM after the first request.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Structural error classes -> ~0. Literature: GraphRAFT +5.4 Hit@1 (35.71 -> 41.07) from constrained decoding at 10% training data; CYGNET measures 0.6-19.3% of generated Cypher as structurally invalid across five models. Caveat: an incomplete grammar can cost accuracy (Qwen2.5-7B Spider: unconstrained greedy 0.643 vs grammar-constrained 0.600), so the grammar must be tested against every gold query in the benchmark (coverage = 100% by construction).
options.effort: 1.5-2 days: grammar generator from the schema (~200 lines), coverage test over gold Cypher, ablation runs (no grammar / generic Cypher grammar / schema grammar).
options.risks: Grammar-coverage gaps silently push the model into awkward but legal queries; constrained decoding can distort the distribution; combining EBNF with n>1 sampling in vLLM 0.26 is unverified; Cypher features like list comprehensions and reduce() (used in the danger few-shot) must be included or those questions get worse.

evidence.claim: Grammar constraints help most when training data is scarce: with 10% data, 41.07% Hit@1 with constraints vs 35.71% without; zero-shot + constraints alone 14.73%

Qwen2.5-Instruct on Spider dev: grammar-constrained greedy 0.600 (7B) vs unconstrained greedy 0.643; cause attributed to incomplete grammar coverage, not distribution distortion; beam search beats sample+vote in 11/16 constrained configs
Across five models on CypherBench, 0.6% to 19.3% of generated queries are structurally invalid; a validation gate runs in 5.6 ms median with zero false positives on 1,135 queries
PICARD: schema-aware incremental parsing rejects inadmissible tokens (e.g., non-existent columns) and turned passable T5 models into SOTA on Spider/CoSQL
Neo4j's own guide: LLMs 'mainly struggle with recent syntax, relationship-direction and unknown attribute types or values'

options.name: O3. Execution-grounded best-of-N selection using vLLM n-sampling (shared prefill) + validator + logprob confidence
options.description: Request n=4 candidates in ONE call at temperature ~0.7-1.0, filter by the read-only guard/grammar, execute all survivors in read transactions, then select by (a) agreement of execution results (cluster by result set), (b) mean token logprob confidence, (c) non-empty result preference. Measured on this box: n=4 took 9.47 s vs 6.07 s for n=1 (538 vs 176 completion tokens) because prefill is shared and decode is batched (aggregate ~175-180 tok/s at 8-16 streams).
options.how_it_applies_here: The rows are tiny (graph has 30 nodes/36 rels) so executing 4 candidates costs milliseconds. Greedy decoding is not even deterministic here (two T=0 calls on the same prompt returned 160- and 176-token variants, one adding spurious n.since <= $now filters), so sampling+selection replaces luck with a measured criterion. Logprobs work on the endpoint (measured mean token logprob -0.072 on a good query).
options.expected_token_effect: Completion tokens ~x3-4 per call A (120 -> ~450-540); prompt tokens counted once per request. Per LLM question: ~3,600+215 -> ~3,600+600 without O4; with O4's shorter prompt the total stays below today's.
options.expected_latency_effect: +~50% on call A (measured 6.1 s -> 9.5 s at n=4, 160-180 completion tokens each); net per-question effect depends on how many repair rounds it removes (each ~3 s).
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Literature on 7B-class models: Query-and-Conquer 44.1% -> 54.8% EX on BIRD (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, 30 samples; gains visible from 3 samples); Ozsoy 2026 confidence-only selection 77.6% -> 85.4% execution success (Gemma-2-9B, 789 Text2Cypher questions), 63.8% -> 83.7% under very-diverse sampling; plain majority vote alone is weak (+1.28% at n=4 for 7B in CSC-SQL). Expect the largest gains on over-filtering (candidates without the extra WHERE win by non-empty result agreement).
options.effort: 1 day: n-sampling in llm_openai_compat, candidate scoring in text2cypher.run, benchmark ablation of selection signals.
options.risks: Correlated errors are not fixed: all 5 live candidates for 'which buildings have a unit assigned' used NEAR instead of ASSIGNED_TO. Execution agreement can prefer a popular wrong answer; tuning temperature/top-p matters (Dessi & Ozsoy: instruction-tuned models lack diversity, reasoning models produce syntax errors). n>1 with json_schema/EBNF on vLLM 0.26 unverified.

evidence.claim: Measured on the live endpoint: n=1 greedy 6.07 s / 176 completion tokens; n=4 T=0.7 9.47 s / 538 completion tokens, 2,770 prompt tokens counted once; two greedy calls differed (160 vs 176 tokens)
Execution-guided selection: Qwen 2.5 Coder 7B 44.1% (greedy) -> 54.8% (30 samples) on BIRD; improvements visible with as few as three samples; 15 samples a strong balance

Confidence-based candidate selection (Gemma-2-9B, 789 test questions): base 77.6% -> 85.4% execution success; very-diverse sampling 63.8% -> 83.7%; adding grammar filtering 86.7% but empty predictions rise (1 -> 24)
CSC-SQL: for 7B without RL, corrective self-consistency beats plain SC by +1.28% (n=4) to +4.25% (n=64); 32B: +1.06% to +2.02%

Adaptive trace budgeting + selective execution-guided refinement: Gemma-2-9B 84.0% -> 92.6% execution success with refinement; adaptive budget cuts traces 30.7% and wall-clock 21-25% for 0.2-0.5% loss
Aggregate decode throughput ~175-180 tok/s at 8-16 streams vs ~45-48 tok/s single stream (2026-09-24 measurements)

options.name: O4. Compact schema + dynamic kNN few-shot retrieval from a synthetic, execution-validated question bank
options.description: Replace the 1,591-token static block of 11 few-shots with the 3-4 most similar (masked-question embedding or BM25) examples drawn from a bank of ~200-500 schema-grounded Q/Cypher pairs generated by templates + LLM paraphrase and validated by execution (SyntheT2C / SynthCypher / PIPE-Cypher recipe, at toy scale). Rewrite the 815-token schema as a 380-token compact form (measured).
options.how_it_applies_here: Schema is fixed and small, so the bank can cover every operational question family (status, provenance, temporal, NEAR, routes, aggregation, conflicts, assignments, refusals). The bank is also the benchmark's training half (held-out test split is mandatory). No embeddings endpoint is served; a ~130 MB local sentence embedder or plain BM25 works offline.
options.expected_token_effect: Call A prompt 2,770 -> ~1,150 tokens (380 schema + 304 rules + ~450 for 3-4 examples + question). Per LLM question ~3,600 -> ~2,000 prompt tokens.
options.expected_latency_effect: -0.3 s per call A without prefix caching; near zero once O1 is on (the retrieved examples then break the cached prefix, so put them AFTER the static block).
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Strongest known lever for small models on a fixed schema: PIPE-Cypher 11-model mean EX 0.036 zero-shot -> 0.200 schema-specific few-shot -> 0.269 same-category demonstrations; ZOGRASCOPE dynamic ICL takes Llama-3.2-3B from 3.4% to 97.0% iid; DAIL-SQL masked-question similarity 79.5% -> 82.0% EX vs random (GPT-4, 5-shot). Expect the 'invented property' and 'wrong relationship type' errors to drop when a near-identical example is present.
options.effort: 1 day: generator (templates over schema + entity names, LLM paraphrases with thinking off, execute + dedupe), retriever, prompt assembly, benchmark split.
options.risks: Test-set leakage inflates numbers if the bank and questions.json overlap (ZOGRASCOPE compositional split falls to 71-75% vs 98% iid, length split 20-26%); retrieval misses on novel phrasings; paraphrases generated by the same model bias toward its own vocabulary.

evidence.claim: Measured with the server tokenizer: SCHEMA_TEXT 2,710 tokens = schema 815 + rules 304 + examples 1,591; ANSWER_SYSTEM 504; compact schema sketch 380

PIPE-Cypher: zero-shot transfer across 11 models mean EX 0.036 (0.000-0.203); few-shot with schema-specific examples 0.200; same-category ordered demonstrations 0.269; Qwen3.5-9B failure mix: answer mismatch 52.1%, execution failed 32.9%, schema invalid 10.4%, parse invalid 4.6%

ZOGRASCOPE (11 classes, 32 properties, 17 relation types): fine-tuned Llama-3.2-3B 97.9% iid / 71.0% compositional / 25.9% length; dynamic ICL Llama-3.2-3B 97.0% iid; zero-shot GPT-4o 41.7%, Llama-3.2-3B 3.4%
DAIL-SQL (GPT-4, 5-shot, Spider-dev EX): random 79.5%, question similarity 79.9%, masked question similarity 82.0%, DAIL selection 82.4%; zero-shot 72.3%
SyntheT2C: 3,000 synthetic pairs via LLM prompting + template filling with five validators; execution accuracy 27.83% -> 39.65% after SFT of 7-8B models
'The Death of Schema Linking': adding schema linking to models that see the full schema costs 2.72-4.77 EX points on BIRD (e.g., ft:GPT-4o 67.35 -> 62.58); aggressive linking keeps only 77.44% recall

options.name: O5. Template-first routing upgrade (TeCoD-style): embedding/NLI matcher over 20-30 parameterised Cypher templates, LLM only fills slots via json_schema (or tool calling)
options.description: Generalise the current 7-intent regex router: mine templates from the question bank (mask literals), match incoming questions with an embedding/NLI classifier, and let the model emit only the slot values (~30 tokens, json_schema-constrained, or native tool calls). Free-form text-to-Cypher (O2-O4) remains the fallback for unmatched questions. This is the 'Cypher templates / dynamic Cypher' pattern Neo4j itself recommends over free text2cypher for reliability, and what Aura Agent combines with a fine-tuned text2cypher tool.
options.how_it_applies_here: Operational questions in an EOC are highly recurrent; a 3-way benchmark split (templated / templated-paraphrase / free) will show how much traffic the templates absorb. Tool calling on the endpoint needs --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder (relaunch), but json_schema slot filling works today.
options.expected_token_effect: Matched questions: ~600 prompt + ~30 completion tokens (vs ~3,600 + ~215).
options.expected_latency_effect: Matched questions ~1 s (TeCoD reports 2.2x lower latency on matched queries); unmatched unchanged.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: TeCoD: matched-query accuracy from ~60% (ICL) to ~90%; BIRD overall 38-48% -> 86-92% across 1B-14B models. Nemotron's BFCL v4 tool-calling score is 53.2 (FP8 card), so slot filling should use json_schema with enumerated ids rather than free tool calls.
options.effort: 1 day for the matcher + 10 more templates; templates already exist for 7 intents.
options.risks: Coverage ceiling (novel questions still need O2-O4); a mis-routed template returns a confidently wrong shape (must keep the confidence >= 0.6 gate); templates duplicate the few-shot bank unless both are generated from one source of truth.

evidence.claim: TeCoD: NLI template matching 73% -> 91%; matched queries ~60% -> ~90% accuracy; BIRD unconstrained 38-48% vs TeCoD 86-92% (CodeS 1B/15B, Granite 2B/8B, Llama-3.1-8B, XiYanSQL 7B/14B, Arctic-R1-7B); 2.2x lower latency on matched queries; unmatched fall back to standard generation
GraphRAG.com pattern catalogue: Cypher templates = limited flexibility, high reliability; Text2Cypher = 'most flexible, but also the most unreliable'
Neo4j Aura Agent pairs a fine-tuned Text2Cypher tool with Cypher templates for 'more precise queries'
Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8 card: BFCL v4 53.2, IFBench 72.2, LiveCodeBench 67.6; recommended flags include --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser nano_v3

options.name: O6. Shrink or skip call B (answer composition): deterministic renderer for row-shaped results, 60-word cap otherwise
options.description: Call B costs ~850 prompt + ~100 completion tokens and ~2.5 s of the 5.5 s. For result shapes the templates already know (status rows, event lists, routes) render the answer deterministically from rows (the fallback path already does this and is fact-check-proof); otherwise keep the json_schema compose call with a 60-word answer cap and the compact system prompt.
options.how_it_applies_here: Grounding is enforced by regex fact-check today with one regeneration (another ~2.5 s). A deterministic renderer has grounded_rate = 1.0 by construction and no highlight-id drift; the model is only used for prose on genuinely novel row shapes.
options.expected_token_effect: -900 to -1,000 tokens per question when rendered deterministically; ~-40% completion tokens when capped.
options.expected_latency_effect: -2.5 s when skipped; -1 s when capped (decode-bound at 45 tok/s).
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Grounded rate up (no fabricated times/confidences), fluency and EOC phrasing down on the deterministic path; unchanged exec_acc.
options.effort: 0.5 day; renderer already exists as QAEngine._rows_summary and the fallback templates.
options.risks: Stilted answers in the demo; renderer must handle nested collect() rows; keep the model path for 'why/explain' questions.

evidence.claim: Baseline per LLM question: call A ~2,765 prompt/~120 completion/~3.0 s; call B ~800-900 prompt/~100 completion/~2.5 s; ~5.5 s wall (task context measurements 2026-09-25)
Single-stream decode ~45-48 tok/s, prefill ~5.5-6.4k tok/s on this box

options.name: O7. Cheaper, gated execution-feedback repair (keep, but only when a validator fires)
options.description: The pipeline already does up to 2 error repairs + 1 zero-row retry, each a full ~3 s call. Gate repairs on a deterministic validator (schema/direction/property check, LangChain-style CypherQueryCorrector for direction, CyVer-style property validation) and feed a structured error vocabulary instead of raw Neo4j messages; auto-fix direction without a model call.
options.how_it_applies_here: With O2 most structural errors never occur, so repair rounds become rare; the zero-row retry stays valuable for over-filtering but should be replaced by O3's non-empty-result preference.
options.expected_token_effect: Removes ~2.9k tokens per avoided repair round.
options.expected_latency_effect: -3 s per avoided round; direction auto-correction is ~0 ms.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Correction is worth +3.4 EX points in the Death-of-Schema-Linking ablation (Llama-405B); Multi-Agent GraphRAG's execution-feedback loop lifts CypherBench EX 56.07 -> 62.86 (GPT-4o) and 45.73 -> 53.40 (Qwen3 Coder); RAMPART corrector repairs 81-95% of structurally invalid queries (mean 89%).
options.effort: 0.5 day (direction corrector + structured error messages).
options.risks: Deterministic direction flipping is unsafe for CONNECTS_TO (undirected by convention) and must be schema-aware; mis-repairs (MapleDoctor reports 9.4%).

evidence.claim: Multi-Agent GraphRAG on CypherBench (5 domains, 150 Q each): single-pass -> agentic average 56.07% -> 62.86% (GPT-4o), 67.00% -> 77.23% (Gemini 2.5 Pro), 45.73% -> 53.40% (Qwen3 Coder); no token/latency numbers reported
Removing the correction stage costs 3.40 points (Llama 3.1-405b), selection 2.72 (Gemini), augmentation 2.72 (ft:GPT-4o) on BIRD
RAMPART corrector: 81-95% repair success across five models (mean 89%); first attempt 66.7%, second attempt +19.4%

Real-world ICL text-to-SQL errors (4,602 wrong queries from MAC-SQL, DIN-SQL, CHESS, DEA-SQL): schema errors dominate execution failures at 81.2%; repair tool 727 fixes with 75 mis-repairs (9.4%), ~1.2 s per query
LangChain CypherQueryCorrector deterministically corrects relationship direction from the schema; it addresses only direction

options.name: O8. Fine-tuning: LoRA on Nemotron (or a specialist small text2cypher model) with schema-grounded synthetic data
options.description: Generate 2-5k schema-grounded Q/Cypher pairs (O4's bank scaled up, CYQUARK/SynthCypher-style: pattern enumeration over the real graph, proto-NL, LLM paraphrase, execution + semantic filtering) and LoRA-tune. Two variants: (a) LoRA on Nemotron itself (vLLM nemotron_h.py declares SupportsLoRA; --enable-lora and --enable-mixed-moe-lora-format exist in 0.26.0), (b) add Neo4j's text-to-cypher-Gemma-3-4B (BF16 ~8 GB, fits in the 19 GB free) or fine-tune it further.
options.how_it_applies_here: Post-demo only. Unsloth documents ~60 GB VRAM for 16-bit LoRA of Nemotron 3 Nano; with ~19 GB free while Nemotron (48 GB) + Qwen3-VL (26 GB) are resident, training needs the vision model stopped or QLoRA. A fine-tuned model would let the few-shots be dropped entirely (prompt ~400 tokens) and is the classic resume item, but the literature shows few-shot retrieval (O4) already reaches ~97% iid on fixed small schemas, so the marginal gain must be measured on the compositional split.
options.expected_token_effect: Prompt 2,770 -> ~400-500 tokens (schema only); completion unchanged.
options.expected_latency_effect: -0.4 s prefill per call A; Gemma-3-4B as a separate specialist would decode ~2-3x faster than the 30B-A3B (unverified on GB10) but adds a second model and VRAM.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: SyntheT2C: execution accuracy 27.83% -> 39.65% (7-8B, +11.8); SynthCypher: Llama-3.1-8B 30.9% -> 71.4% on its test set; CYQUARK-4B reaches 85.38% EX on CypherBench vs GPT-5.5 88.79%; Neo4j fine-tunes gained ~+0.11 exact match (Llama-3.1-8B) and ~+0.07 (Gemma-2-9B) on the 2024 dataset. Domain fine-tunes generalise poorly out of distribution (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B tuned on Spider+BIRD: 43.8%/31.4% on ScienceBenchmark/EHRSQL).
options.effort: 3-5 days (data generation 1-2, training 1, serving/eval 1); requires GPU memory the demo setup does not have.
options.risks: LoRA serving on the FP8 NemotronH MoE checkpoint is unverified in 0.26.0; Unsloth issue #3854 reports LoRA merge failures for Nemotron 3 Nano; Neo4j's Gemma-3 model cards publish no accuracy numbers; overfitting to the paraphrase style of the generator; adding a model is a team decision.

evidence.claim: 16-bit LoRA fine-tuning of Nemotron 3 Nano uses around 60 GB VRAM; router layer training disabled by default; keep >=75% reasoning data to preserve reasoning
Installed vLLM 0.26.0 nemotron_h.py declares SupportsLoRA and SupportsMambaPrefixCaching; --enable-lora and --enable-mixed-moe-lora-format flags exist
SynthCypher (29,838 train / 2,000 test, 109 taxonomies, 528 domains): Llama-3.1-8B 30.9% -> 71.4%, Mistral-7B 31.1% -> 69.4%, Qwen-2-7B 14.6% -> 67.1% (GPT-4o-judged execution match)
CYQUARK-4B (Qwen3.5-4B, KG-grounded synthetic data): 85.38% EX on CypherBench vs GPT-5.5 88.79% / Claude Opus 88.58%; 78.47% on Zograscope vs GPT-5.5 65.68%

Neo4j Text2Cypher (2024) dataset: 44,387 instances (39,554 train / 4,833 test); fine-tuning deltas: Llama-3.1-8B ~+0.14 GBLEU/~+0.11 EM, Gemma-2-9B ~+0.13/~+0.07, GPT-4o ~+0.18/~+0.01; absolute values only in figures
Neo4j text2cypher-2025v1 dataset: 40,384 rows (35.9k train / 4.44k test); released models text-to-cypher-Gemma-3-4B/27B-Instruct-2025.04.0 (model cards carry no evaluation numbers)
Neo4j gemma-2-9b 2024 model: LoRA r=64, 1 epoch, 4-bit nf4, 1x A100; prompt 'Generate Cypher statement ... Use only the provided relationship types and properties in the schema'

OmniSQL-7B (2.5M synthetic samples): BIRD dev 63.9% greedy / 66.1% majority vote, Spider test 87.9% (> GPT-4o 83.2%); Qwen2.5-Coder-7B tuned only on Spider+BIRD drops to 43.8%/31.4% on ScienceBenchmark/EHRSQL

options.name: O9. 'LLM-only' alternative: serialise the whole graph into the prompt and answer without Cypher (keep only as an ablation baseline)
options.description: The graph is small enough to fit: the baseline snapshot (30 nodes, 36 rels, trimmed props) serialises to 8,931 tokens. The model would answer directly from the serialised graph. This is the 'just use the LLM' option the developer asked about.
options.how_it_applies_here: It violates the product contract (answers must be grounded in query rows with provenance; evidence/cypher fields in QA_CONTRACT) and scales badly: 100-500 Event nodes push the prompt to 30-100k tokens, above max-model-len 32,768. Useful only as the 'no-KG-query' baseline row in the benchmark table to show why text-to-Cypher is needed.
options.expected_token_effect: ~9k prompt tokens per question today (vs ~3.6k), growing with every event.
options.expected_latency_effect: ~1.6 s prefill at 5.5k tok/s plus decode; prefix caching helps only between graph changes.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Unknown for this task; graph-encoding choice alone swings LLM graph-reasoning accuracy by 4.8-61.8% (Talk like a Graph); no provenance guarantee and no fact-check possible against rows.
options.effort: 0.5 day as a benchmark baseline.
options.risks: Fabrication risk already confirmed for this model (invents incidents for presupposed places 6/6); grows beyond context.

evidence.claim: Measured: whole graph (30 nodes + 36 rels, trimmed) = 8,931 tokens with the server tokenizer
Choice of graph-to-text encoder changes LLM graph reasoning accuracy by 4.8% to 61.8% depending on task
Nemotron fabricates cited incidents for made-up places when the question presupposes them (6/6 with presupposing phrasing)

options.name: O10. Not recommended: DIN-SQL/MAC-SQL/CHESS-style decomposition and schema linking/pruning
options.description: Multi-call decomposition pipelines (schema linking, classification, sub-question generation, self-correction) were built for large schemas and frontier APIs.
options.how_it_applies_here: Schema is 815 tokens (380 compact) and fully fits; CHESS's 5x token saving is over BIRD-scale schemas; DIN-SQL costs 12.8k-21.6k tokens and ~60 s per question with GPT-4, i.e. 4-8 sequential calls at 45 tok/s locally. The 'Death of Schema Linking' result shows linking hurts when the schema fits.
options.expected_token_effect: +3-6x tokens per question.
options.expected_latency_effect: +10-20 s per question on this box.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Negative to neutral for a fitting schema (-2.7 to -4.8 EX from adding linking on BIRD).
options.effort: n/a
options.risks: n/a

evidence.claim: DIN-SQL: 85.3 EX on Spider, 55.9% on BIRD; ~12.8k/21.6k tokens per case and ~$0.50 / 60 s per question with GPT-4
CHESS: 71.10% on BIRD test, schema pruning reduces LLM tokens by x5, ~83% fewer LLM calls than proprietary leaders
MAC-SQL: 59.39% / 59.59% EX on BIRD dev/test via multi-agent decomposition

options.name: O11. Not available now: speculative decoding (MTP / ngram)
options.description: Decode speed is the bottleneck (~45 tok/s). MTP would help most, but the FP8 Nano checkpoint's config.json contains no MTP keys, the Nano paper does not mention MTP, and ngram prompt-lookup was tried and reverted on this box.
options.how_it_applies_here: vLLM 0.26.0 ships nemotron_h_mtp.py (NemotronHMTPModel registered) but that needs MTP weights in the checkpoint; only Nemotron 3 Super/Ultra/3.5 Lightning document MTP. Prefix caching + MTP is also reported to crash on NemotronH (0.19.0).
options.expected_token_effect: none

Live measurement (thinking off): n=1 greedy 6.07 s for 176 completion tokens; n=4 at T=0.7 9.47 s for 538 completion tokens with 2,770 prompt tokens counted once, i.e. 4 candidates for ~1.5x the wall time. Two greedy (T=0) calls on the same prompt produced different queries (160 vs 176 tokens), so benchmark runs must be repeated.

Live failure example: for 'Which buildings have a unit assigned to them right now?' all 5 candidates used (:Team)-[:NEAR]->(:Building) instead of ASSIGNED_TO, and one greedy variant added spurious n.since <= $now / n.last_confirmed <= $now filters (over-filtering). Voting cannot fix a unanimous semantic misread.

CypherBench (11 graphs, 7.8M entities, >10k questions): GPT-4o 60.18% EX, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 61.58%, Gemini 1.5 Pro 39.95%, Qwen2.5-72B 41.87%, Llama-3.1-70B 38.84%, Llama-3.1-8B 18.82%, Gemma2-9B 18.61%; errors span 10 categories incl. reversed direction, entity linking and pattern misalignment; Llama-3.1-8B shows far more schema violations.

ZOGRASCOPE shows the fixed-small-schema regime is far easier than CypherBench: fine-tuned 3B-7B models reach 97.9-98.0% iid but 71-75% compositional and 20-26% length splits; dynamic ICL gives Llama-3.2-3B 97.0% iid; zero-shot GPT-4o only 41.7%.

PIPE-Cypher (enterprise schema, 11 models): zero-shot mean EX 0.036 -> 0.200 with schema-specific few-shots -> 0.269 with same-category demonstrations; local Qwen3.5-9B: 0.963 parse validity, 0.916 schema validity, 0.189 EX; failure mix 52.1% answer mismatch / 32.9% execution failed / 10.4% schema invalid / 4.6% parse invalid.

Confidence-based candidate selection for Text2Cypher (Gemma-2-9B, 789 questions): 77.6% -> 85.4% execution success; grammar (ANTLR) filtering 86.7% but empty predictions 1 -> 24; schema filtering 84.0% with 36 empties.

Adaptive test-time inference for Text2Cypher (Sept 2026): fixed budget 84.0% -> 92.6% execution success with execution-guided refinement (Gemma-2-9B); adaptive trace budgeting cuts traces 30.7% and wall-clock 21-25% for 0.2-0.5% loss.

Grammar constraints are not free: Qwen2.5-7B Spider EX 0.643 unconstrained vs 0.600 grammar-constrained greedy (incomplete grammar coverage); beam search beats sample+vote in 11/16 constrained settings; inference-time compute cannot compensate a 7B -> 3B downgrade.
Template-constrained decoding (TeCoD): matched queries ~60% -> ~90%; BIRD 38-48% -> 86-92% across 1B-14B models; 2.2x lower latency on matched queries; unmatched fall back to standard generation.
Execution-guided selection lifts Qwen2.5-Coder-7B from 44.1% to 54.8% EX on BIRD with 30 samples, gains visible from 3 samples; 14B/32B gain only 1.5-3.5 points.

SynthCypher fine-tuning: Llama-3.1-8B 30.9% -> 71.4%, Qwen-2-7B 14.6% -> 67.1% (GPT-4o-judged execution match); SyntheT2C: 27.83% -> 39.65% execution accuracy; CYQUARK-4B: 85.38% EX on CypherBench vs GPT-5.5 88.79%.

Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8: 52 layers (23 Mamba-2, 23 MoE, 6 attention), 3.5B active, BFCL v4 53.2, IFBench 72.2, LiveCodeBench 67.6; the checkpoint config has no MTP keys and the paper does not mention MTP; LoRA of the 30B needs ~60 GB VRAM (Unsloth).

Neo4j's Text2Cypher assets: text2cypher-2024v1 (44,387 pairs) and text2cypher-2025v1 (40,384 pairs); fine-tuned gemma-2-9b (2024, LoRA r=64, 1 epoch) and text-to-cypher-Gemma-3-4B/27B-Instruct-2025.04.0 (cards publish no accuracy numbers); the 2024 paper reports only deltas (Llama-3.1-8B ~+0.11 EM, Gemma-2-9B ~+0.07 EM, GPT-4o ~+0.01 EM).

Schema linking is counter-productive when the schema fits in context: adding TCSL linking costs 4.77 (ft:GPT-4o), 4.76 (Gemini 1.5 Pro) and 2.72 (Llama-405B) EX points on BIRD; aggressive linking keeps only 77.44% column recall; correction stage worth +3.40.

Multi-agent decomposition costs: DIN-SQL 12.8k-21.6k tokens and ~60 s / $0.50 per question with GPT-4 (85.3 Spider / 55.9 BIRD); Multi-Agent GraphRAG's execution-feedback loop gives +6.8 (GPT-4o) and +7.7 (Qwen3 Coder) EX on CypherBench with no token/latency numbers reported.

A deterministic Cypher validation gate (regex + ANTLR + EXPLAIN + mirror execution) detects 100% of parse/constraint/labeled-path schema errors with zero false positives on 1,135 queries at 5.6 ms median; LLM correctors repair 81-95% of flagged queries.

Real-world ICL text-to-SQL error study (4,602 wrong queries): schema errors dominate execution failures (81.2%), function hallucination >40% of syntax errors; semantic errors 36.1% on BIRD; repair tool mis-repairs 9.4%.

recommendations: Step 0 (before any change, ~2-3 h): make the baseline real and recoverable. Commit bench/run_bench.py; write bench/questions.json with ~80-100 questions across the categories in the task (status, provenance, temporal, NEAR, routes with blocked/conflicted roads, aggregations, conflicts, assignments, unanswerable/out-of-scope, mutation/dispatch refusals) each with gold_cypher, compare keys, must_mention/must_not_mention; tag each question with a split (router-covered / paraphrase-of-router / free / compositional). Run --mode llm and --mode auto 3x each (T=0 is non-deterministic here), commit results, then scripts/snapshot_state.sh baseline-v1 so the code, graph dump and results are one tag. Record the server config (vllm-llm.json, vllm version 0.26.0, model id, prompt token counts) inside the results JSON.

Step 1 (pre-demo, low risk, in this order, each as its own tagged experiment): (a) O1 prefix caching relaunch if the team agrees (zero accuracy risk, verify prefix_cache_hits_total > 0); (b) O4 compact schema + kNN few-shots (3-4 examples) from an execution-validated bank, placed after the static block so the cached prefix survives; (c) O3 best-of-4 with guard/grammar filter -> execute -> non-empty-result agreement + mean logprob; (d) O6 deterministic answer rendering for row shapes the templates know, 60-word cap otherwise. Expected together: prompt tokens per LLM question ~3,600 -> ~1,500-2,000, wall ~5.5 s -> ~4-5 s, and the over-filtering / property-name failures reduced; measure, do not assume.

Step 2 (post-demo research core): O2 schema-specialised EBNF decoding as the headline ablation (no grammar / generic Cypher grammar / schema grammar) crossed with O3 selection signals (agreement vs logprob vs validator), on the same benchmark with tokens, latency, exec_acc, grounded, abstain and per-failure-class rates. Add the O9 whole-graph-in-context 'LLM-only' row and the O5 template-first row as reference points so the table answers the developer's 'LLM vs LLM+KG vs templates' question with numbers.

Step 3 (only if GPU memory can be freed): O8 schema-grounded synthetic data (scale the O4 bank to 2-5k pairs with execution + semantic filtering) and LoRA either on Nemotron or on the Gemma-3-4B specialist; report on the held-out compositional split, since iid numbers saturate near 97-98% in this regime.

Do not spend time on: schema linking/pruning (schema fits; literature shows it hurts), DIN-SQL/MAC-SQL-style decomposition (4-8 sequential calls at 45 tok/s), speculative decoding (no MTP heads in this checkpoint), or thinking-mode Cypher generation (decode-bound).

Keep the honest-failure contract as a first-class metric: report abstain_rate on unanswerable questions and the false-abstention rate on answerable ones alongside exec_acc, because O2/O3 filters increase empty predictions (Ozsoy: 1 -> 24-36 empties when adding grammar/schema filters).

Every experiment = one git tag + bench/results/<label>-<sha>.json + the vllm-llm.json server config; restore_state.sh <tag> returns to any point. Add the questions file and few-shot bank to the snapshot so a restore reproduces the exact prompt.
resume_angle: Schema-specialised grammar-constrained text-to-Cypher: an automatically generated EBNF (labels, directed relationship patterns, per-label properties, enumerated values) that makes property hallucination and direction errors unrepresentable, with a measured coverage-vs-accuracy trade-off against a generic Cypher grammar (novel relative to the confidence+ANTLR post-hoc filtering line of Ozsoy et al. 2026, which filters after generation rather than constraining it, and to GraphRAFT which needed fine-tuning).

Execution-grounded best-of-N on a tiny live graph where executing every candidate is ~free: a study of selection signals (result-set agreement, non-empty preference, mean logprob, validator pass) for a 30B-A3B hybrid Mamba MoE model, with the measured n-sampling cost curve (4 candidates at ~1.5x wall time) as the efficiency argument.

A reproducible operational text-to-Cypher benchmark for a temporal, provenance-tagged disaster graph: execution accuracy, grounding (every cited source/time/confidence traceable to a row), honest abstention, tokens and latency per question, with router-covered / paraphrase / free / compositional splits and a per-failure-class taxonomy (property hallucination, relationship-type confusion, direction, over-filtering) mapped to the interventions that fix each.

Token-efficiency engineering on hybrid Mamba serving: diagnosing the disabled/blocked prefix cache (4176-token block alignment) and quantifying prefill vs decode share (decode ~90% of latency), which motivates candidate-count and prompt-compaction decisions rather than the usual 'shorter prompt' reflex.

Schema-grounded synthetic data generation at toy scale (templates over the real graph + LLM paraphrase + execution/semantic validation, following SyntheT2C / SynthCypher / CYQUARK) used both as a kNN few-shot bank and, if compute allows, as LoRA training data, evaluated on a leakage-free compositional split.

options.name: (a) Whole-graph-in-context (serialize the live graph into the prompt, LLM answers directly)
options.description: Dump every node/relationship (compact key=value lines) into the system prompt each question and let Nemotron answer in prose; no Cypher, no retrieval.
options.how_it_applies_here: Probed on the box with the baseline-v0 snapshot (20 entities + 10 events + 36 rels = 7,580 tokens as key=value text, 8,306 as compact JSON). 4/5 questions answered plausibly, but the aggregation question was wrong AND hallucinated an entity: model said '20 people ... Building 14 and Building 7'; gold is 120 people, Building-14 only. The reachability question gave a vague 'must use alternate route' with no traced route. Each event line is ~300 chars (~100 tokens), so at the stated 100-500 events the prompt is ~15k-60k tokens: the upper range exceeds max-model-len 32,768 and the lower range costs ~3-4 s of prefill per question at 5.5k tok/s. Because facts change every second the prefix is invalidated constantly, and the 4,176-token cache block means at best the static-topology head could be cached if it is ordered first and padded past one block.
options.expected_token_effect: ~7.7k prompt tokens now (2.1x the baseline's 3.6k), ~15k-60k at demo event volume; completion tokens ~15-100 (fewer than baseline's ~215 because there is one call).
options.expected_latency_effect: Measured 2.1-5.2 s at 7.7k tokens (prefill-dominated); scales linearly with events, ~3-4 s prefill alone at 20k tokens; no cache reuse when the graph changes.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Good on lookup/provenance/refusal (WG1, WG3, WG4 correct), unreliable on aggregation and path reasoning (WG5 wrong + invented entity; WG2 vague). Grounding cannot be verified against rows because there are no rows: the fact-check would have to run against the whole graph.
options.effort: 2-3 h to build as a benchmark arm (serializer + one prompt); not viable as the primary path.
options.risks: Hallucinated entities in exactly the failure mode the product must never show; no provenance rows for the UI; context blow-up as events accumulate; the model's own eval (AA-LCR long-context 36.1) is weak.

evidence.claim: Local probe: 7,738-7,749 prompt tokens per whole-graph question; WG5 answered '20 people ... Building 14 and Building 7' vs gold 120 people / Building-14 only; WG2 gave no route; WG1/3/4 correct (2.1-5.2 s)
LLMs fail to understand graph structure from text descriptions and show varying performance on connectivity and shortest-path tasks
Graph encoding choice strongly affects LLM graph reasoning; performance degrades as graphs grow
Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B card: AA-LCR long-context 36.1, BFCL v4 53.2; 3.5B active params

options.name: (b) LLM + KG via text-to-Cypher (current baseline)
options.description: Schema+few-shot prompt -> one Cypher -> read-only guard -> execute -> repair loop -> second LLM call composes JSON answer -> regex fact-check.
options.how_it_applies_here: This is the right family for a small, fixed-schema, second-by-second-changing graph: the query executes against live Neo4j, so freshness and provenance are free, and rows give a verifiable grounding target. Its problems are (1) semantic errors (~1/3 of tail questions: wrong property, over-filtering, reversed direction), (2) two decode-heavy calls: at 45 tok/s decode vs 5.5k tok/s prefill, one completion token costs as much latency as ~120 prompt tokens, so the ~120-token Cypher (2.7 s) and ~100-token JSON answer (2.2 s) dominate the 5.5 s, not the 2,765-token schema (~0.5 s), (3) 0% prefix-cache reuse because the hybrid-Mamba block is 4,176 tokens. The installed vLLM 0.26.0 exposes `prefix_match_unit` ('can be set finer than the physical KV cache block sizes (e.g. 32 vs a 1024-token hybrid-model block)') and the 0.26.0 release notes list 'partial prefix-cache hit for hybrid models (#46384)', so a relaunch with --prefix-match-unit could make the schema prompt cacheable (team decision; needs measurement).
options.expected_token_effect: Baseline ~3,600 prompt + ~215 completion per LLM question. Cheap cuts: drop call B for a deterministic renderer (-900 prompt, -100 completion); have the model emit only MATCH/WHERE + ids and hydrate provenance columns with a fixed second read (RETURN clauses are roughly half the few-shot tokens, so ~-50% completion in call A).
options.expected_latency_effect: 5.5 s now; ~3 s if call B becomes deterministic; ~2 s if the Cypher projection is hydrated by the engine; prefix caching saves only ~0.5 s/call.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Execution accuracy stays ~2/3 on the tail unless semantics are fixed; a CYGNET-style pre-execution schema gate (EXPLAIN + label/property/direction check) removes crashes but not wrong-but-valid queries; grounding is already enforced by rows + fact-check.
options.effort: Exists. Schema gate 3-4 h; deterministic renderer 3-4 h; projection hydration 2-3 h; relaunch flag test 30 min plus ~4 min server restart.
options.risks: Small models score low on generic Text2Cypher (~30% exec match for the best models on Neo4j's 2024 benchmark; <10B open models reported under 20% on CypherBench); repairs add calls; per-request disable_any_whitespace is not honoured.

evidence.claim: Best models (GPT-4o, fine-tuned tomasonjo) reach ~30% execution match on Neo4j Text2Cypher (2024) benchmark
CYGNET pre-execution gate catches 100% of parse/constraint/schema-reference errors with zero false positives; corrector 81-95% success (mean 89%) across five LMs, 2,348 CypherBench questions
Grammar + schema-aware test-time filtering improves Text2Cypher validity but 'stronger filtering also increases the number of empty predictions and reduces execution coverage'
vLLM 0.26.0 release notes: 'partial prefix-cache hit for hybrid models' (#46384); PR merged July 2026
Installed vLLM 0.26.0 CacheConfig.prefix_match_unit docstring: finest token boundary a prefix-cache hit can land on, may be finer than the physical hybrid block
Hybrid Attention+SSM models mandate exact-match cache hits because SSM state cannot be rolled back (Marconi, MLSys 2025)
Schema filtering reduces token cost and helps smaller models most in Text2Cypher
Local probe C2: a 273-token schema without few-shots produced syntactically invalid Cypher (RETURN ... WHERE ... RETURN), so schema pruning alone hurts this model

options.name: (c) GraphRAG variants (Microsoft GraphRAG, LightRAG, HybridRAG, HippoRAG, G-Retriever, Think-on-Graph)
options.description: Build a graph/vector index over a text corpus, retrieve subgraphs/communities/paths, generate from retrieved context.
options.how_it_applies_here: Mismatch: every GraphRAG method exists to construct and exploit a graph from unstructured text; RescueGrid already has a typed, provenance-tagged property graph with a known schema and Neo4j as the single source of truth. The expensive/uncertain step (graph construction) is already solved, and the retrieval step is replaced by an exact query. Community summaries (Microsoft) or entity-keyword indices (LightRAG) would be stale within seconds and cannot express 'as of 14:02:45Z' or 'conflict = true'. Think-on-Graph/G-Retriever-style traversal agents are multi-call and target open KGs with unknown schemas.
options.expected_token_effect: Higher than baseline: index maintenance per event plus retrieval context per query (LightRAG hybrid ~$0.03-0.05/query on API models; Microsoft GraphRAG far more), with nothing gained for a 30-entity graph.
options.expected_latency_effect: Worse: extra retrieval + generation; ToG-style iteration is multi-call at ~3 s/call here.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Literature: graphs help multi-hop QA over large corpora, not detail/fact lookups (RAG w/ rerank 60.92 vs GraphRAG-local 49.29 on fact retrieval; RAG 55.28 vs GraphRAG 46.88 on NovelQA detail). Our questions are exact lookups/aggregations/paths over a tiny structured graph, where an executed query is 100% precise by construction.
options.effort: 1-2 days to wire any framework; no expected benefit; frameworks assume text corpora and cloud LLMs.
options.risks: Staleness, non-verifiable answers (no rows), double storage, evaluation artifacts; reviewers would ask why you rebuilt a graph you already had.

evidence.claim: RAG excels on detailed single-hop queries, GraphRAG on multi-hop; NQ F1 RAG 64.78 vs GraphRAG-local 63.01; NovelQA detail RAG 55.28 vs 46.88; MultiHop-RAG HippoRAG2 70.27 vs RAG 67.02
GraphRAG-Bench (ICLR'26): 'GraphRAG frequently underperforms vanilla RAG on many real-world tasks'; benchmark exists to find when graphs help
Secondary summary of GraphRAG-Bench: RAG (w/ rerank) 60.92 vs GraphRAG (local) 49.29 on fact retrieval; HippoRAG2 53.38 vs RAG 42.93 on complex reasoning (unverified against the paper's table)
Microsoft GraphRAG indexing ~$7.50+ per 5,000-word document vs LightRAG ~$0.008; LightRAG ~$0.03-0.05 per query (vendor/blog figures, unverified)
ToG-2 alternates graph and context retrieval over KG+documents; SOTA on 6/7 knowledge-intensive datasets with GPT-3.5 (multi-step, cloud-model setting)

options.name: (d) Vector RAG over event text
options.description: Embed Event nodes / radio transcripts / notes, retrieve top-k by similarity, let the LLM answer from snippets.
options.how_it_applies_here: The graph is small enough that retrieval is not the bottleneck; the hard part is exact temporal/aggregate/path semantics ('last 5 minutes', 'sum occupancy', 'route avoiding blocked roads'), which embeddings cannot express. Useful only as a complement for genuinely free-text fields (raw radio transcripts, Event.details) when the fusion agent stores them, e.g. 'what did radio say about the bridge' where the claim vocabulary is open. Neo4j 5 has native vector + fulltext indexes, so this can be a Cypher clause (db.index.fulltext.queryNodes is already allowlisted) rather than a separate store.
options.expected_token_effect: Similar to baseline call B (~1k prompt) but without the Cypher call: ~1.2k tokens/question; embedding cost per event is tiny (a local embedding model would need ~1-2 GB of the 19 GB free).
options.expected_latency_effect: ~2.5 s (one compose call) plus embedding lookup; no Cypher generation.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Fine for 'find the report about X', poor for counts, time windows, conflicts and routes; grounding is weaker because snippets are not rows with typed fields.
options.effort: 4-6 h (Neo4j vector index + embedder + retrieval clause); as a fulltext-only variant, ~1 h since the index exists.
options.risks: Answers drift from the authoritative status (an old transcript can outrank the current node status); stale embeddings; another model resident in memory.

evidence.claim: RAG is consistently effective for single-hop, detail-oriented queries requiring precise evidence, not for multi-hop/aggregate reasoning
Temporal QA needs explicit time constraints and 'as-of' correctness (TimeQA-style), which similarity retrieval does not encode
The existing guard already allowlists db.index.fulltext.queryNodes, so hybrid fulltext+Cypher needs no new infrastructure

options.name: (e) Agentic / tool-use (ReAct over a small set of typed graph tools, MCP-style)
options.description: Expose typed tools (get_entity, events_since, route, near, conflicts, run_readonly_cypher) and let the model plan multiple calls until it can answer.
options.how_it_applies_here: Would need the server relaunched with --enable-auto-tool-choice and a tool-call parser (memory notes: tool calling currently 400s; qwen3_coder parser suggested). Neo4j's own evaluation of an MCP-Cypher agent used Claude 3.7 Sonnet and still averaged 3.6 tool calls/question at a 0.71 mean score, degrading to 0.535 with a 10-step cap; Nemotron Nano's BFCL v4 is 53.2, so expect more calls and lower accuracy. At ~3 s per call that is 10-15 s per question, over the demo's tolerance, and each loop step re-prefills the growing transcript (no prefix cache reuse under 4,176 tokens per block).
options.expected_token_effect: 3-4x baseline (each step re-sends history): ~10-15k prompt tokens/question.
options.expected_latency_effect: 10-15 s typical, unbounded worst case unless capped.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Better recovery on hard multi-step questions in principle, but the cited agent needed a frontier model; with a 3.5B-active model the planning errors compound. Typed tools do give hard grounding (each tool returns rows).
options.effort: 1-2 days including relaunch flags, tool schemas, loop cap, transcript management (thinking ON output has no opening <think> tag, so history must be sanitized).
options.risks: Latency; tool-parser instability; early stopping/loops; the model was observed to fabricate presupposed entities, which tools only partially catch.

evidence.claim: MCP-Neo4j-Cypher agent (Claude 3.7 Sonnet): mean score 0.71, 3.6 tool calls/question; 0.535 with a 10-step limit; sensitive to typos and under-specified intents
Neo4j Text2Cypher Guide (Feb 2026): prewritten parameterised Cypher tools for common/complex cases, Text2Cypher as generic fallback tool
Nemotron-3-Nano BFCL v4 = 53.2; recommended reasoning-off sampling T=0.6/top_p 0.95 for tool calling
On this box tool calling currently fails (needs --enable-auto-tool-choice + parser); thinking-ON content has no opening tag

options.name: (f) Semantic parsing to a small DSL / slot-filled templates (LLM router -> parameterised Cypher)
options.description: One constrained JSON call classifies intent and fills typed slots (entity, unit, facility, source, minutes, hazard_type...); the engine runs a hand-written parameterised Cypher and renders the answer deterministically from rows.
options.how_it_applies_here: Probed: a 168-token system prompt + strict json_schema produced {intent: recent_changes, entity: 'bridge', source: drone_vision, minutes: 10} for 'What did the drones report about the bridge in the last ten minutes?' in 3.74 s with 72 completion tokens (240 tokens total vs 3,600). The regex router already covers 7 intents; the LLM router generalizes phrasing (typos, synonyms, Hinglish) without new regexes, and the slot schema can enumerate the closed vocabularies (sources, hazard types, unit types) so invented values are unrepresentable. Slots resolve through the existing EntityResolver (aliases/fulltext), and the answer is rendered by the existing fallback builders, so every sentence is row-derived and provenance/highlight come for free. This is exactly what TeCoD formalizes for SQL (template match + constrained decoding: up to +36% execution accuracy over ICL and 2.2x lower latency on matched queries).

options.name: (g) Hybrid: router for known intents + constrained/gated text-to-Cypher for the tail (RECOMMENDED)
options.description: Three tiers: (1) regex router (0.05 s) -> (2) LLM JSON router with typed slots -> parameterised Cypher -> deterministic renderer -> (3) tail: existing text2cypher with a pre-execution schema gate and, as an ablation arm, a schema-compiled grammar (GBNF via xgrammar) that makes reversed directions and unknown properties unrepresentable; compose only for the tail (or render rows deterministically and optionally polish).
options.how_it_applies_here: Keeps the demo-safe path, cuts tokens/latency on the bulk of questions, and turns the tail into a measurable research object. Probes on the box: xgrammar accepted a GBNF Cypher grammar through structured_outputs.grammar; an untyped grammar still let the model reverse NEAR (Hazard->Team) and run to max_tokens on unbounded projections; a direction-typed grammar removed the direction error but the model then picked the wrong pattern (DETECTED_BY instead of NEAR, duplicated conditions); with the full 2,767-token few-shot prompt plus the typed grammar on an unseen question the output was grammatical but semantically wrong and projected an unbound variable (t.id without MATCH (t)). Conclusion: grammar buys syntactic/schema validity, not pattern choice; a real schema-compiled grammar must bind variables per pattern, and it must be evaluated for coverage loss (Ozsoy 2026 warns filtering raises empty predictions). That is precisely the ablation a research write-up needs: baseline vs +schema gate vs +typed grammar vs +router, on execution accuracy, grounding, tokens, latency, and a TrustSQL-style penalty score.
options.expected_token_effect: Routed questions ~200-450 tokens (-88%); tail ~2.9k prompt + ~60-120 completion (drop call B: -1k); overall per-question mean depends on router coverage (expect 70-85% of the benchmark routed).
options.expected_latency_effect: Routed ~1-2 s (0.05 s when regex hits); tail ~3 s (one call) or ~2 s with projection hydration; p95 bounded by the tail's repair loop (cap at 1 repair).
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Covered intents become deterministic; tail execution accuracy is the research variable (baseline ~2/3); grounding stays ~100% by construction (rows + fact-check); abstention on out-of-scope improves because the router has an explicit 'other' and the gate rejects schema-invalid queries before execution.
options.effort: Demo-safe version ~1 day (router + 6 templates + renderers + gate); grammar arm +1 day (schema->GBNF compiler with per-pattern variable binding, tests); benchmark questions + ablations + write-up +1-2 days.
options.risks: Grammar may hurt (format restriction can push a small model off-distribution: duplicated/garbled conditions observed); coverage/abstention trade-off must be reported, not hidden; two code paths to keep in sync (few-shots already double as templates, which helps).

recommendations: Architecture: adopt (g) hybrid. Tier 1 regex router (existing, 0.05 s) -> Tier 2 LLM JSON router with strict json_schema and enumerated slot vocabularies (sources, hazard/unit types) -> parameterised Cypher templates -> deterministic renderer (reuse fallback.py builders; no compose call) -> Tier 3 existing text2cypher only for the tail, with a pre-execution schema gate (EXPLAIN + label/property/relationship-direction check against schema.cypher) before the read transaction.

Freeze the baseline FIRST, before any change: write bench/questions.json (target ~60 questions: 7 templated, ~35 tail across status/provenance/temporal/proximity/route/aggregation/conflict/assignment, ~10 unanswerable/out-of-scope, ~8 paraphrase/typo variants of templated ones), run `NEO4J_URI=bolt://127.0.0.1:7687 .venv/bin/python bench/run_bench.py --label baseline --mode llm` and `--mode auto`, and keep the JSON results. bench/results is empty today, so the '~3,600 tokens / 5.5 s / ~1/3 tail failures' numbers are not yet reproducible artifacts.

Make state recoverable now: `git init` in /home/hp2/kenil/rescuegrid-reasoning, commit, tag `baseline-v0`; commit bench/snapshots/baseline-v0/graph.json and the results JSON; extend run_bench.py to record a server fingerprint (vllm version, model id, launch flags from `ps`, prompt hash of SCHEMA_TEXT/ANSWER_SYSTEM) so any result can be re-run against the same graph + prompts + server config. Restore = checkout tag + ingest the snapshot + same launch flags.

Token/latency levers in order of measured payoff: (1) skip the compose call for routed intents (-1k tokens, -2.2 s); (2) shorten call A output by having the model emit only MATCH/WHERE + ids and hydrating provenance columns with a fixed read (completion tokens dominate at 45 tok/s: 1 completion token ~ 120 prompt tokens of latency); (3) per-intent slot schemas so the router emits ~25 tokens; (4) prefix caching is the smallest win (~0.5 s/call) but is a one-flag relaunch: ask the team to add `--prefix-match-unit 64` (vLLM 0.26.0 supports partial prefix-cache hits for hybrid models, per its release notes and the installed CacheConfig) and verify with the vLLM prefix-cache hit-rate metric before claiming it; do not rely on it for the demo.

Do not pursue GraphRAG/LightRAG/HybridRAG or vector RAG as the primary path: they solve graph construction and retrieval over text corpora; RescueGrid already has the typed graph, and an executed Cypher is exact and fresh by construction. Keep vector/fulltext only as an optional clause for open-vocabulary transcript fields.

Do not pursue the agentic ReAct loop before the demo: it needs a relaunch with a tool-call parser, multiplies calls 3-4x (~10-15 s), and the published MCP-agent result (0.71 with Claude 3.7 Sonnet) used a far stronger model than a 3.5B-active Nano.

Research arm (after the demo, on the frozen benchmark): implement a schema->GBNF compiler for Cypher (labels, per-label properties, typed+directed relationship endpoints, per-pattern variable binding, bounded projections) driven from schema.cypher, run it through xgrammar via structured_outputs.grammar, and report the 2x2 ablation {few-shots on/off} x {grammar off / untyped / typed} plus {schema gate on/off} on execution accuracy, coverage (empty/abstained), grounding, tokens and latency. My quick probes show grammar fixes form but not pattern choice, so the honest expected outcome is 'validity up, exec accuracy flat-to-slightly-up, coverage down' unless combined with the gate and few-shots; publish it either way with a TrustSQL-style penalty score.

Benchmark metrics to report: execution accuracy (row-set match on key columns, existing), grounding rate (existing fact_check), abstention precision/recall on unanswerable questions, a penalty-based reliability score (correct +1, abstain 0, wrong -1 as in TrustSQL), prompt/completion tokens split (they have different costs here), p50/p95 wall time, calls per question, and freshness: replay the same question at two scenario clocks and check the answer changes (as-of correctness).

Keep the read-only and human-in-control guarantees in every arm: the grammar must not be able to produce write clauses (it cannot by construction), the gate runs in a read transaction, and routed answers must still pass through _finish() for conflicts/highlight/provenance.
resume_angle: A reproducible benchmark for grounded, time-aware QA over a live labeled property graph (provenance, conflicts, as-of clock, answerable + unanswerable) with execution accuracy, grounding rate, abstention and a penalty-based reliability score: I found no public benchmark that scores 'as-of' correctness with provenance on a streaming LPG (unverified absence), so the artifact itself is defensible.

Schema-compiled grammar-constrained Cypher decoding on an edge SLM: compile the Neo4j schema (labels, typed/directed relationship endpoints, per-pattern variable binding) into a GBNF grammar enforced by xgrammar so reversed directions and invented properties are unrepresentable; closest prior art is schema-constrained GQL generation (Huawei 2024), PICARD/TeCoD for SQL and GCR's KG-Trie; the novelty is the property-graph typing + the coverage/abstention ablation on a 3.5B-active hybrid-Mamba model running fully offline.

A cost model that separates prompt and completion tokens by measured hardware cost (5.5k tok/s prefill vs 45 tok/s decode on GB10) and shows that output-token reduction (router slots, projection hydration, deterministic rendering) beats prompt compression for latency: an 'output-token-first' token-efficiency result with ablations on real hardware.

Router-vs-generator reliability study: template routing with typed slots vs free text-to-Cypher vs constrained text-to-Cypher, reported as a selective-prediction curve (coverage vs risk), which connects to the 2026 text-to-SQL selective-prediction literature rather than prompt tweaking.

Systems note on hybrid-Mamba prefix caching in practice: the 4,176-token block cliff, the effect of --prefix-match-unit in vLLM 0.26 on a real workload, and prompt-layout implications (static-first ordering) — small but concrete and measurable.
open_questions: Will the team accept a relaunch of the shared 'llm' server with --prefix-match-unit (and possibly --mamba-cache-mode align)? Unverified until measured: whether partial hits actually apply to the Nemotron Mamba2 layers on this build, and whether it costs KV memory.

What is the real event volume at demo time (100 vs 500 events)? It decides whether whole-graph-in-context is even representable (32k limit) and how large the 'recent events' template windows should be.

Router coverage: what fraction of the officer's realistic phrasings map to the ~13 intents? Needs the benchmark question set (bench/questions.json does not exist yet) and a paraphrase set to measure routing accuracy and false-route rate.

Does grammar-constrained decoding hurt this model off-distribution (duplicated conditions and odd exclusions were observed)? Needs the proper schema-compiled grammar with variable binding, not my 10-minute toy grammars, and a comparison at T=0 with beam search if the server exposes it.

Is fine-tuning a small text2cypher LoRA on schema-grounded synthetic pairs feasible on the box (19 GB free, GB10 sm_121a) and serveable alongside Nemotron? Literature says small fine-tuned models become competitive, but memory and vLLM LoRA support for this hybrid architecture are unverified.

Can call B be removed entirely for the tail by rendering rows deterministically (as _rows_summary does) with an optional low-token polish, without losing the officer-facing prose quality the demo needs?

Which selective-prediction signal should gate tail answers: execution success + schema gate only, or a cheap self-verification call? Published logprob signals are weak (AUROC ~0.68), so abstention design should be measured, not assumed.

Shared-schema alignment: if Shresth's shared graph changes labels/ids, the router templates, few-shots and any compiled grammar must regenerate from schema.cypher; the grammar compiler should be schema-driven from day one.

options.name: Skip call B: one-call query + answer-template, rendered deterministically from rows (grounded-by-construction verbalization)
options.description: Call A emits the Cypher plus a short answer template whose slots reference RETURN aliases (e.g. "{name} is {status} since {status_since} ({source}, {confidence})"). The engine executes the query, validates that every slot is a returned column, fills slots from rows (dates/confidences formatted by code), and never asks the model to write prose from rows. The existing _rows_summary() renderer in rescuegrid/qa/engine.py is the fallback when the template is invalid; the JSON-schema compose call stays available as an opt-in for aggregations that need prose.
options.how_it_applies_here: Call B costs ~850 prompt + ~100 completion tokens and ~2.5 s, and its output must then be regex fact-checked (with a second 2.5 s regeneration when it fails). Because every fact in the answer is copied from a row by code, the fact-check becomes a static check on the template and the grounded rate is 100% by construction. Provenance/conflict/highlight fields are already derived from rows in engine.py, so nothing in the QA contract changes.
options.expected_token_effect: Per LLM question: ~3,600 + 215 -> ~2,800 + ~160 tokens (call B removed; the template adds ~30-50 completion tokens to call A). Regeneration path (another ~950 + 100 tokens) disappears.
options.expected_latency_effect: -2.3 to -2.5 s of the 5.5 s (call B is ~100 decode tokens at ~22 ms/token plus overhead); worst case (fact-check regeneration) drops from ~8 s to ~3.2 s. Decode is ~85% of wall time on this box, so removing a whole call is the single largest lever.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: grounded_rate -> 1.0 by construction for slot values; facts_rate should hold (must_mention strings come from rows); prose is more mechanical. exec_acc unchanged. Risk of a template referencing a missing alias is caught statically before rendering.
options.effort: 0.5-1 day: template mini-grammar/regex, slot validation, renderer, bench flag (--verbalizer template|llm), 10-15 unit tests.
options.risks: Answers read more mechanically than LLM prose; multi-row answers need a per-row template plus aggregation phrases; conflicts must be rendered by code (already done in _finish). If the model puts facts in the template text instead of slots, a check that the template contains no source names/times/confidences outside slots is required (reuse fact_check()).

evidence.claim: Template Constrained Decoding (SIGMOD/PACMMOD 2025) reports up to 36% higher execution accuracy and 2.2x lower latency on matched recurring queries by enforcing templates at decode time
AWS reports parameterized query templates cut Text2SQL latency by 80% and token consumption by over 50%
Baseline call B: ANSWER_SYSTEM is 504 tokens by the vLLM tokenizer; compose uses json_schema with maxLength caps and a regex fact-check with one regeneration (engine.py _llm_answer/_compose)
A model-free row renderer (_rows_summary) already exists as the LLMError fallback, so the deterministic path is partly built

options.name: Shrink the Cypher completion: projection macro + short few-shots (no fence)
options.description: The model writes only MATCH/OPTIONAL MATCH/WHERE/WITH/ORDER BY and ends with a fixed marker (e.g. RETURN *PROV*); code appends a canonical provenance projection per bound variable (id, name, status, status_since, source, confidence, raw_evidence_ref, conflict fields). Few-shots are rewritten in the same short form and the ```cypher fence is dropped (extract_cypher already tolerates its absence).
options.how_it_applies_here: Measured with the vLLM tokenizer: the RETURN..LIMIT part is 693 of 1,395 tokens (50%) across the 11 example queries, and the model copies that shape (probe: 111-130 completion tokens for a 2-line question). An appended instruction alone did not change the output shape (120 tokens, identical projection), so the few-shots themselves must change. The macro also guarantees the columns the renderer/provenance code expects and removes the most common hallucination site (invented property names in RETURN).
options.expected_token_effect: Call A completion ~120 -> ~55-70 tokens; call A prompt 2,765 -> ~2,000 (examples 1,591 -> ~800 tokens). Repair prompts shrink proportionally.
options.expected_latency_effect: -1.1 to -1.4 s per call A (decode at ~22 ms/token) plus ~-0.15 s prefill; with option 1 the pipeline lands at ~1.7-2.2 s per LLM question.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Neutral to positive: fewer invented property names (adversarial review finding), consistent provenance columns for grounding. Aggregation queries (sum/collect) need an explicit-RETURN escape hatch that the guard's literal-as-fact check still covers.
options.effort: 0.5 day including rewriting the 11 few-shots and tests in tests/test_cypher_guard.py.
options.risks: Over-generic projection can return more columns than the answer needs (rows JSON grows if call B is kept, cap at 12,000 chars already exists). Queries that project computed values (danger score, hops, people) must keep explicit RETURN; detect by the presence of RETURN and skip the macro.

evidence.claim: RETURN..LIMIT clauses are 693/1,395 = 50% of the few-shot Cypher tokens (vLLM /tokenize on schema_prompt.py examples, 2026-09-25)

Probe on the live endpoint: call A produced 111-130 completion tokens for 'Which sensors are offline and what do they monitor?', copying the 10-property projection of the few-shots; an added map-projection instruction did not change the shape (120 tokens)
Single-stream decode measured at ~45-48 tok/s and prefill ~5.5-6.4k tok/s on this box (2026-09-24), i.e. ~22 ms per completion token vs ~0.18 ms per prompt token

options.name: Turn on vLLM prefix caching for the hybrid model (relaunch flags), with bf16 KV to halve the 4,176-token block
options.description: Relaunch Nemotron with --enable-prefix-caching (vLLM 0.26 keeps prefix caching opt-in for hybrid models; NemotronH declares supports_mamba_prefix_caching=True so it gets mamba_cache_mode='all'). Optionally add --kv-cache-dtype auto (bf16 KV) so the attention block shrinks from 4,176 to ~2,096 tokens (2,176 after chunk-128 alignment in 'all' mode), which lets the 2,710-token static system prompt hit one cached block. Keep the static schema+rules+examples first and the clock+question last (already the case). Do not pass --mamba-block-size (open crash reports).
options.how_it_applies_here: The 0.0% hit rate is not caused by the 4,176 block alone: the current run has enable_prefix_caching=False. The 4,176 comes from per-layer page matching: Mamba state page 2,134,016 B (conv 36,864 + fp32 SSM 2,097,152) divided by 512 B/token/layer of fp8 KV (2 KV heads x 128 dim x K,V) = 4,168 -> 4,176. With bf16 KV it is 2,084 -> 2,096 (2,176 in 'all' mode); with --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 it would be ~2,128 but vLLM forces fp32 SSM for NemotronH for accuracy. Padding the static prefix to >= 4,224 tokens with fp8 KV is legitimate for the engine (identical deterministic prefix) but inflates reported prompt_tokens; if used, the benchmark must report computed tokens = prompt_tokens - cached_tokens.
options.expected_token_effect: Tokens sent unchanged; computed (non-cached) prompt tokens for call A drop by ~2,176 of 2,765 (-79%) with bf16 KV, or by ~4,224 of ~4,300 if the prefix is padded with fp8 KV. Call B (~850 tokens) stays below the block size and gains nothing.
options.expected_latency_effect: Upper bound ~-0.4 s per LLM question (prefill of 2,765 tokens is ~0.45-0.5 s at 5.5k tok/s; per-call fixed overhead ~0.15 s remains). About 8% of the 5.5 s baseline; also makes n>1 candidate sampling cheaper (children share the cached prefix).
options.expected_accuracy_effect: None expected; bf16 KV is at least as precise as fp8 KV (the checkpoint ships kv_cache_quant_algo=FP8 with scale 1.0 warnings in the log).
options.effort: 1-2 hours plus a ~4 minute relaunch window and a team OK (shared model). KV budget halves in tokens with bf16 (13.8 GiB -> ~1.5M tokens instead of 3.1M), still ample.
options.risks: vLLM logs Mamba prefix caching as experimental; open issues exist for explicit --block-size/--mamba-block-size with hybrid models (#53142, #57266) and for spec decode + prefix caching on hybrids (#39809, #54360). Any dynamic prompt change (option 4) that alters the first block defeats the cache, so choose static-prefix-first ordering.

evidence.claim: Current run: enable_prefix_caching=False; 'Setting attention block size to 4176 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size'; 'Padding mamba page size by 0.19%'; KV cache fp8_e4m3; mamba_ssm_cache_dtype forced to float32 for NemotronH
vLLM 0.26 arg_utils: 'Hybrid models support prefix caching but keep it opt-in for now while the feature matures' (default_prefix_caching = supported and not is_hybrid)
NemotronH model declares supports_mamba_prefix_caching = True; with prefix caching on, mamba_cache_mode defaults to 'all' and block size = chunk_size(128) * cdiv(mamba_page/attn_page_per_token, 128)

Model config: 23 Mamba2 + 6 attention + 23 MoE layers, num_key_value_heads=2, head_dim=128, mamba 64 heads x 64 dim, d_state 128, n_groups 8, conv 4, chunk 128 (reproduces 4,176 exactly; bf16 KV gives 2,096)
vLLM issue #40696: for a Mamba-hybrid (Qwen3.5, block 528) a 479-token prompt gets ~0% prefix-cache hits while a 552-token prompt reaches 95.4%, because only fully completed blocks are cached
Tracking issue #26201: 'all' and 'align' Mamba cache modes, --mamba-block-size (PR #27289), align-mode default still an open item, Nemotron-H MTP via PR #33726
Crash reports with explicit hybrid block-size flags: illegal memory access on prefix-cache resume with --block-size (#53142) and out-of-range SSM write with --mamba-block-size (#57266)

options.name: Schema pruning + dynamic few-shot selection (k=3 by entity-masked question skeleton)
options.description: Keep the 815-token schema block but drop type-specific property lines for kinds the question does not mention, and replace the 11 static examples (1,591 tokens) with the 3 most similar examples from a bank of ~30-50 gold pairs, retrieved by BM25/regex over entity-masked question skeletons (no extra model) or a 33M-parameter local embedding model.
options.how_it_applies_here: The prompt is 2,710 tokens: schema 815, rules 304, examples 1,591 (11 examples of 108-268 tokens). The graph has 7 labels and ~10 relationship types, so label pruning is unsafe (unanswerable questions need the full label list to refuse), but property-line pruning and example selection are safe. The bench already has 60 gold pairs across 10 categories to seed the example bank (hold-out required).
options.expected_token_effect: Call A prompt 2,765 -> ~1,200-1,400 tokens (-50 to -55%); combined with option 2's short examples -> ~900-1,000.
options.expected_latency_effect: Only ~-0.25 to -0.3 s (prefill is cheap here); the value is in tokens and in accuracy for a 3B-active model. Conflicts with option 3: a per-question prompt no longer shares a >= block-size static prefix, so pick one per configuration and report the trade-off as an ablation.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Likely positive: Neo4j's schema-filtering study found Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B improved with shorter schemas (P95 prompt 2,697 -> 529-917 tokens) while a large model dropped <5%; DAIL-SQL's skeleton-similarity selection was the best selection strategy on Spider (86.6% EX). Risk of retrieving misleading examples for novel questions.
options.effort: 0.5-1 day (skeleton masking via the existing EntityResolver aliases, BM25 with rank_bm25 or Neo4j fulltext, leave-one-out evaluation on the bench).
options.risks: Retrieval relies on surface similarity; a wrong example can bias the query shape (DAIL-SQL critique). Must keep the ABOUT-direction and 'no timestamp on entities' rules static since those were the adversarial failure modes. Embedding model must be offline (bge-small ~33M params fits) or use BM25.

evidence.claim: Neo4j 'Enhancing Text2Cypher with Schema Filtering': P95 prompt tokens 2,697 (enhanced schema) vs 917 (base) vs 529 (exact-match pruning); smaller models (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B) improved with shorter schemas, Gemini-1.5-Flash dropped <5%
DAIL-SQL: skeleton-similarity example selection was the best few-shot selection strategy, reaching 86.6% execution accuracy on Spider
Our prompt breakdown by the vLLM tokenizer: schema 815, rules 304, examples 1,591 (11 examples, 108-268 tokens each), ANSWER_SYSTEM 504
Bench has 60 gold questions in 10 categories (status 8, provenance 7, temporal 7, proximity 6, route 5, aggregation 6, conflict 4, units 5, unanswerable 6, paraphrase 6), 51 with gold_cypher

options.name: Grammar-constrained read-only Cypher subset (xgrammar EBNF with labels, relationship types and properties enumerated)
options.description: Send structured_outputs={'grammar': <GBNF>} on call A. The grammar admits only MATCH/OPTIONAL MATCH/WHERE/WITH/ORDER BY/LIMIT (plus RETURN or the projection marker), enumerated labels (Entity, Building, Road, Team, Hazard, Sensor, Facility, Event), relationship types, property names, status vocabularies, the functions the few-shots use (toLower, any, collect, reduce, coalesce, size, head, nodes, length, point.distance, duration, round, sum), and forces (:Event)-[:ABOUT]->(n) direction. The Python guard stays as defence in depth.
options.how_it_applies_here: Confirmed on the live endpoint: vLLM 0.26 + xgrammar 0.2.2 accept a GBNF grammar via structured_outputs.grammar; the constrained run returned a valid query (95 completion tokens, TTFT 0.58 s including first compile). It also showed the main hazard: my test grammar lacked function calls and the model was coerced into 'collectentity.id AS monitors', syntactically valid nonsense. Adversarial review attributed ~1/3 of LLM failures to invented property names, over-filtering and reversed direction; the grammar removes the first and third classes and every guard rejection, not the second.
options.expected_token_effect: No change to nominal tokens per call, but each avoided repair round saves ~2,900 prompt + ~120 completion tokens (a repair re-sends the whole schema prompt plus the failed query and error). Guard rejections -> 0 by construction.
options.expected_latency_effect: -3 s on every question that previously needed a syntax/schema repair; per-token overhead is negligible (XGrammar v1 ~45 us/token vs ~22 ms decode); grammar compile happens once per grammar string (cached) but can take >1 s for large grammars, so compile at startup with a warm-up request. Also compatible with speculative decoding later.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Positive on schema-violation and direction errors (CypherBench: schema violations are the dominant small-model error; grammar-constrained decoding beat unconstrained for every Qwen2.5 0.5B-7B size on Spider). Zero effect on semantic errors such as wrong filters (CYGNET: structural validators score 0% on property sibling-swaps). Over-narrow grammars actively hurt (coercion artefact observed).
options.effort: 1 day for a grammar that covers all 11 few-shot constructs, property-per-label tables, and 30+ grammar unit tests; +0.5 day if combined with the projection macro (grammar then ends at ORDER BY/LIMIT).
options.risks: Grammar coercion into valid-but-wrong tokens when a construct is missing; GBNF has no left recursion and repeated optionals can slow sampling; xgrammar compile latency for big grammars (>1 s reported for v1); per-request disable_any_whitespace is server-level in 0.26 (confirmed in structured_outputs config), so whitespace must be modelled in the grammar; string literals must allow arbitrary spoken names.

evidence.claim: Live probe: structured_outputs.grammar accepted by the ZRT/vLLM 0.26 endpoint; constrained output valid, 95 completion tokens, TTFT 0.58 s; missing function rule coerced 'collectentity.id AS monitors'

Installed backends: xgrammar 0.2.2 and llguidance 1.7.6 (outlines absent); xgrammar Grammar follows the llama.cpp GBNF specification; disable_any_whitespace is a server-level StructuredOutputsConfig option supported only by xgrammar/guidance

GBNF syntax: rules, literals, character classes, *, +, ?, {m,n}, alternation, comments; warning that x? x? x? ... repetitions can make sampling extremely slow; left recursion not documented as supported
XGrammar-2 paper: XGrammar v1 ~45.5 us per-token overhead; >1,000 ms grammar compile for large dynamic grammars (XGrammar-2 ~10 ms); PDA state blow-up for non-deterministic grammars

CypherBench: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 61.6% EX, GPT-4o 60.2%, Llama-3.1-8B 18.8%, Gemma2-9B 18.6%, Llama-3.2-3B 11.2%; small models make far more schema-violation errors; reversed direction and entity linking are major error classes
