Grammar-constrained text-to-SQL with Qwen2.5 0.5B-7B (4-bit) on Spider: constrained decoding outperformed unconstrained for all sizes; beam search beat sample+vote at matched budget; larger model beat more inference compute

CYGNET: pre-execution validation chain at 5.6 ms median catches 100% of parse/constraint/schema-reference errors with zero false positives, but property sibling-swaps score 0% (semantic errors are invisible to structural checks); corrector success 81-95%

Confidence-based Text2Cypher with grammar and schema-aware filtering: grammar filtering improves syntactic validity, schema filtering improves execution quality, stricter filtering increases empty predictions

options.name: Speculative decoding (ngram / suffix now; EAGLE3 or draft model later)
options.description: Prompt-lookup (ngram) or suffix decoding needs no draft model and suits Cypher, whose tokens are largely copied from the schema prompt and few-shots; EAGLE3 needs a trained head; MTP needs checkpoint weights.
options.how_it_applies_here: The 09-24 ngram launch (num_speculative_tokens 4, lookup 2-4) actually ran: mean acceptance length 2.6-4.9, draft acceptance 41-97%, generation throughput 86-105 tok/s vs ~45 baseline during repetitive output (block size grew to 4,272; async scheduling disabled). But vLLM PR #56531 (unmerged as of 2026-09-23) documents silent dropped/duplicated tokens for ngram on hybrid recurrent models including Nemotron Mamba2 (12/60 correct before the fix, 60/60 after); the competing fix #55504 is also unmerged. Nemotron 3 Nano ships no MTP head (0 'mtp' tensors in the checkpoint; the tech report puts MTP only in Super/Ultra), and no public EAGLE3 head exists for Nano 3 (a community head exists for the sibling Nemotron-Cascade-2-30B-A3B).
options.expected_token_effect: None on billed tokens; drafted-but-rejected tokens cost compute only.
options.expected_latency_effect: Potential ~-40 to -55% of decode time (2x) on Cypher: ~215 completion tokens x 22 ms = 4.7 s -> ~2.4-2.8 s. Zero today because it must stay off until the hybrid state fix lands.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Negative right now (silent corruption = wrong or invalid Cypher, or an invented value in an answer); neutral by design once fixed (spec decode is lossless with greedy verification).
options.effort: 1-2 hours to configure plus a 60-prompt corruption A/B (greedy outputs with and without spec decode must match exactly) before any demo use; EAGLE3 head training is a multi-day research task with unverified feasibility on GB10.
options.risks: Silent output corruption in vLLM 0.26 (PR #56531/#55504 open); Mamba page padding without speculative widening breaks startup for some hybrids at num_speculative_tokens>=2 (#57721, fixed for NemotronH by passing num_spec); spec decode + prefix caching on hybrids has crash/miss reports (#39809, #54360); async scheduling disabled with ngram. Team must relaunch the shared model.

evidence.claim: 09-24 ngram run on this box: 'SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 4.86 ... Avg Draft acceptance rate: 97.0%' and generation throughput 86.6-105.5 tok/s at 1 running request vs ~45 tok/s without spec decode; block size 4272

PR #56531: ngram spec decode silently drops/duplicates tokens on hybrid recurrent models (Nemotron Mamba2, Qwen3-Next GDN, Kimi-Linear); NVIDIA Nemotron 12/60 -> 60/60 after fix; not merged as of 2026-09-23
PR #55504 (competing fix for zero-draft rows corrupting recurrent state) also open/unmerged as of September 2026

Issue #57721: Mamba-hybrid models fail to start with num_speculative_tokens >= 2 when the model does not pass num_spec into the state shape (vLLM 0.27.1); NemotronH passes num_spec (nemotron_h.py line 779)
Nemotron 3 technical report: MTP layers are present in the two larger models (Super, Ultra), not Nano; local checkpoint index contains zero 'mtp' tensors
Nemotron 3.5 Lightning adds MTP/DFlash/DSpark speculative decoding as a new feature over Nemotron 3 Nano; recommended flags there include --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align
Community EAGLE3 head trained against Nemotron-Cascade-2-30B-A3B (same 23 Mamba + 23 MoE + 6 attention hybrid family), served via vLLM; none published for Nemotron-3-Nano
EAGLE 3.1 on vLLM: 2.03x per-user throughput at concurrency 1, 1.66-1.71x at 4-16 (Kimi K2.6 on GB200)

SuffixDecoding (draft-model-free, suffix trees over prompts and prior outputs): up to 5.3x on agentic benchmarks including Text-to-SQL; available as method 'suffix' in vLLM 0.26 (vllm/v1/spec_decode/suffix_decoding.py)

options.name: Skeleton cache of question -> Cypher (self-extending template library), never an answer cache
options.description: Normalise the question (lower-case, resolve entity mentions to ids via EntityResolver, mask them as slots), look up an exact skeleton match in a store of previously successful (skeleton, Cypher-with-slots) pairs, and re-execute the Cypher on the live graph. Near-miss matches are used only as extra few-shot examples (soft hit), never as the answer. Every LLM query that passed the guard and returned rows is promoted into the store, so the regex router grows online.
options.how_it_applies_here: Watch officers repeat a small set of operational questions with different entities ('where is Rescue 4', 'status of Building 22'); the bench has a paraphrase category to measure this. Because the cached object is a query (re-run on live data), staleness is impossible; the only failure mode is a wrong skeleton match, which exact matching eliminates.
options.expected_token_effect: Hard hit: 0 LLM tokens (with option 1) or ~950 + 100 (if call B kept); miss: unchanged. Hit rate on real traffic is unknown; on the bench's paraphrase category it should approach 100% after one pass.
options.expected_latency_effect: Hard hit ~0.1 s (same as the regex router); expected traffic-weighted saving depends on repetition rate (unmeasured).
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Exact skeleton hits: identical to the first successful run (exec_acc preserved). Embedding-threshold hits are risky: static thresholds give 1-15% wrong-hit rates in production write-ups and vCache shows correct/incorrect hit similarity distributions overlap, hence soft-hit only.
options.effort: 0.5 day (JSON store + skeleton function + bench flag); reuse fusion/resolve.py for masking.
options.risks: Promoting a query that ran but answered the wrong thing (exec_acc false) poisons the cache: only promote queries whose bench/gold or human feedback marks correct, or store with a confidence and require two agreeing runs. Cache must be part of the snapshot state.

evidence.claim: vCache: static similarity thresholds lack guarantees; per-prompt learned thresholds reach up to 12.5x higher hit rate and 26x lower error than static-threshold baselines
Semantic caching error rates of 1-15% depending on threshold vs zero for exact match (practitioner write-up, weaker source)
Existing 7 pre-baked intents answer in ~0.05 s without the model (README Q&A section)

options.name: Logprob-gated routing, abstention and repair budgeting (1-token classification and mean-logprob confidence)
options.description: Use cheap signals to decide where to spend tokens: (a) a 1-token, logprobs=5 classifier for answerable/out-of-scope, (b) mean token logprob of the generated Cypher (request logprobs on call A) to decide whether a zero-row result deserves the repair round, and (c) skip repair on 'easy' questions.
options.how_it_applies_here: Measured: a 108-token, max_tokens=1 classification took 0.77 s under load (expected ~0.2 s idle) and the zero-shot label was wrong ('X' unanswerable with p~0.25 for a plain status question), so it needs few-shots and calibration on the bench before use. The regex router already covers 7 intents at 0.05 s, so the value is not routing but budgeting: each zero-row or error repair costs ~2,900 + 120 tokens and ~3 s.
options.expected_token_effect: +~100 prompt tokens per gated question; saves ~3,000 tokens per avoided futile repair.
options.expected_latency_effect: +0.2 s per gate; -3 s per avoided repair; Neo4j-style selective refinement reported 21-25% wall-time and 30.7% budget savings at -0.2 to -0.5% execution success.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Potentially better abstention calibration on unanswerable questions (bench abstain_rate); risk of skipping a repair that would have succeeded.
options.effort: 0.5 day; calibration data is thin (60 questions), so treat as a research ablation, not a demo feature.
options.risks: Uncalibrated logprobs from a 3B-active MoE; zero-shot classification observed wrong on the first probe; adds a call on the critical path.

evidence.claim: Live probe: 1-token classification, prompt 108 tokens, 0.77 s under concurrent load, top logprobs X -1.37, E -1.5, B -2.25 (wrong label for a status question)

Adaptive test-time inference for Text2Cypher (Gemma-2-9B, Qwen-2.5-7B): difficulty-aware budgeting cut generation budget 30.7% and wall time 21-25% at 83.1% vs 84.0% execution success; skipping refinement on easy questions costs 0.2-0.5%; max two refinement rounds
Neo4j iterative refinement study: verification+correction loop is promising but external DB/LLM calls are costly; first-iteration validation should be narrowed

options.name: Parallel candidates with execution-guided selection (n=3) instead of sequential repair
options.description: Sample 3 Cypher candidates in one request (n=3, temperature ~0.5, or 1 greedy + 2 sampled), run all through the guard and Neo4j, and pick by execution agreement (non-empty, majority row-set) before any repair round.
options.how_it_applies_here: Aggregate decode on this box reaches ~175-180 tok/s at 8-16 streams vs ~45 single-stream, so 3 concurrent candidates cost only ~+0.3-0.8 s of wall time; in vLLM V1, n>1 becomes child requests that re-prefill unless prefix caching is on (option 3). The two pipeline calls cannot be batched together because call B depends on call A's rows; the only real 'batching of the two calls' is the one-call design in option 1.
options.expected_token_effect: Completion tokens x3 for call A (~360) and prompt tokens x3 in accounting unless cached; a token-per-correct-answer metric should be reported alongside.
options.expected_latency_effect: +0.3-0.8 s per question; -3 s wherever it replaces a repair round.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Positive on exec_acc via self-consistency (beam search / sample+vote both helped small grammar-constrained models), at the cost of determinism.
options.effort: 0.5 day.
options.risks: Temperature>0 introduces variance into a demo; 3x token accounting hurts the headline token metric; needs prefix caching to avoid 3x prefill.

evidence.claim: Measured aggregate decode ~175-180 tok/s saturating at 8-16 streams vs 45-48 tok/s single stream (2026-09-24 vllm bench serve)
vLLM V1 implements n>1 as a ParentRequest fanning out child requests (vllm/v1/engine/parallel_sampling.py), so prompt reuse depends on prefix caching
For small grammar-constrained models on Spider, both beam search and sample+vote improved accuracy, beam search more efficiently

options.name: Learned prompt compression (LLMLingua-2 / Selective Context) - evaluated, not recommended (keep as a negative ablation)
options.description: Run the 2,765-token schema prompt through LLMLingua-2 (110M or 550M token classifier) or Selective Context and feed the compressed prompt to call A.
options.how_it_applies_here: These compressors are trained on prose (MeetingBank) and delete low-information tokens; in our prompt the low-frequency tokens are property names, quotes and operators that must be copied verbatim into Cypher. At 5.5k tok/s prefill the entire prompt costs ~0.5 s, so even 3x compression saves at most ~0.35 s, while the RCT evidence shows aggressive compression can raise total cost through output expansion. Hand-authored pruning (options 2 and 4) achieves larger, safer reductions.
options.expected_token_effect: -50 to -80% of prompt tokens nominally (2x-5x in the paper); realistic safe setting on structured text is unknown and likely much lower.
options.expected_latency_effect: <= -0.35 s per call A; possibly slower end-to-end if outputs lengthen or repairs increase.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Expected negative on exec_acc (schema tokens dropped); worth one bench row to prove it.
options.effort: 0.5 day to run as an ablation (models fit trivially in the 19 GB headroom and run offline).
options.risks: Silent removal of schema identifiers; extra CPU/GPU model on the critical path (~10-50 ms).

evidence.claim: LLMLingua-2: 2x-5x compression ratios, 1.6x-2.9x end-to-end latency reduction, 3x-6x faster than prior compressors, evaluated on MeetingBank, LongBench, ZeroScrolls, GSM8K, BBH
LLMLingua-2 compressors are XLM-RoBERTa-large (~550M) and multilingual-BERT-base (~110M) token classifiers
Selective Context: 50% context cost reduction, 36% memory and 32% inference-time reduction, BERTscore -0.023 and faithfulness -0.038 on prose tasks

Pre-registered RCT on prompt compression in production orchestration: 50% retention gave 27.9% mean cost reduction, 20% retention increased cost by 1.8% because outputs expanded; 'output tokens must be treated as a first-class outcome'

key_facts.fact: Wall time is decode-bound: ~215 completion tokens x ~22 ms (45 tok/s) = ~4.7 s of the 5.5 s baseline; prefill of 2,765 + 850 tokens at ~5.5k tok/s is only ~0.65 s. Prompt-side tricks are capped at ~12% latency; completion tokens and call count are the levers.

The 0.0% prefix-cache hit rate is primarily because prefix caching is OFF: the current Nemotron run has enable_prefix_caching=False (vLLM 0.26 keeps it opt-in for hybrid models); NemotronH supports it ('all' mode).

The 4,176-token attention block is per-layer arithmetic: Mamba page 2,134,016 B (fp32 SSM 64x64x128x4 + conv) / 512 B per token per attention layer (fp8 KV, 2 KV heads x 128) = 4,168 -> 4,176; bf16 KV (--kv-cache-dtype auto) gives 2,096 (2,176 in 'all' mode); --mamba-block-size cannot go below this ratio.

Prompt composition (vLLM tokenizer): SCHEMA_TEXT 2,710 tokens = schema 815 + rules 304 + 11 examples 1,591 (108-268 each); ANSWER_SYSTEM 504; RETURN..LIMIT clauses are 50% (693/1,395) of the example Cypher tokens.

xgrammar EBNF (GBNF) grammars work on this endpoint via structured_outputs.grammar (xgrammar 0.2.2, llguidance 1.7.6 installed); an incomplete grammar coerced the model into 'collectentity.id AS monitors', i.e. grammars must cover every construct the few-shots use.

ngram speculative decoding ran on this box on 2026-09-24 with acceptance lengths 2.6-4.9 and up to ~2x generation throughput, but vLLM PRs #56531/#55504 (open) document silent token drops/duplications for ngram on hybrid recurrent models including Nemotron Mamba2 (12/60 correct before the fix).
Nemotron 3 Nano has no MTP head (tech report: MTP only in Super/Ultra; checkpoint has 0 'mtp' tensors) and no public EAGLE3 draft; Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is the variant that ships spec-decode drafts.

vLLM 0.26 spec-decode methods present in the installed package: ngram, ngram_gpu, suffix, medusa, draft_model, eagle, eagle3, dflash and MTP variants incl. nemotron_h_mtp; NemotronH implements SupportsEagle/SupportsEagle3.

For Mamba-hybrids in vLLM, only fully completed blocks are cached: a 479-token prompt got ~0% hits while 552 tokens got 95.4% with a 528-token block (Qwen3.5) - the same cliff applies to our 2,765-token prompt vs 4,176.
Neo4j schema filtering: exact-match pruning cut P95 prompt tokens from 2,697 to 529 and improved Llama-3.1-8B/Qwen2.5-7B accuracy; a large model lost <5%.
CypherBench: sub-10B open models score 11-19% execution accuracy vs ~60% for GPT-4o/Claude 3.5; schema violations and reversed direction dominate small-model errors - matching our adversarial review.
Template Constrained Decoding for recurring text-to-SQL questions: up to +36% execution accuracy and 2.2x lower latency on matched queries (SIGMOD 2025).
Structural validation (CYGNET) catches 100% of parse/schema-reference errors at 5.6 ms but 0% of property sibling-swaps: grammars fix syntax, not semantics.
XGrammar v1 per-token overhead ~45.5 us (negligible vs 22 ms decode); compile can exceed 1 s for large grammars, so compile once and warm up.

LLMLingua-2 gives 2-5x compression on prose benchmarks, but a pre-registered production RCT found aggressive compression raised total cost (+1.8%) via output expansion; moderate compression saved 27.9%.
vCache: static semantic-cache thresholds are unreliable (overlapping similarity distributions); learned per-prompt thresholds give up to 12.5x hit rate and 26x lower error.
Adaptive test-time Text2Cypher: skipping refinement on easy questions costs 0.2-0.5% execution success while saving 21-25% wall time and 30.7% budget (max two refinement rounds).

State is recoverable today: git tag baseline-v0, bench/snapshots/baseline-v0/graph.json, scripts/snapshot_state.sh + restore_state.sh, bench/run_bench.py with 60 gold questions in 10 categories; bench/results is still empty (baseline not yet run).

Live probes ran under concurrent load (engine showed 1-3 running requests, GPU 89-96%): call A total 4.24-9.5 s, TTFT 1.05-1.44 s, decode 16-34.5 tok/s - treat idle numbers (0.15 s TTFT, 45 tok/s) as the reference and rerun timings when the box is quiet.

recommendations: First, run the baseline as-is and snapshot it: NEO4J_URI=bolt://127.0.0.1:7687 .venv/bin/python bench/run_bench.py --label baseline --mode llm (bench/results is empty today), then scripts/snapshot_state.sh baseline-v0-results. Also record the vLLM launch JSON (/opt/hp/zrt/run/vllm-llm.json) in every snapshot, because server flags are part of the experimental state.

Demo-day plan (<= 1 day, no server relaunch needed), each behind an env/CLI flag so every ablation is one bench run: (1) projection macro + short few-shots + no fence (expected call A 120 -> ~65 completion tokens, prompt 2,765 -> ~2,000); (2) one-call query+answer-template with deterministic rendering, keeping the JSON compose call as an explicit fallback for aggregations (removes ~850+100 tokens and ~2.5 s). Expected per LLM question: ~3,600+215 tokens / 5.5 s -> ~2,000-2,100 + ~110-150 tokens / ~2.0-2.5 s, grounded rate 1.0 by construction.

Next (1 day): the read-only schema-constrained xgrammar grammar on call A, covering every construct in the few-shots (collect/reduce/CASE/point.distance/duration/paths), forcing (:Event)-[:ABOUT]->(n), with the projection marker as the terminal; measure guard rejections, repair rounds and exec_acc with and without it. Warm the grammar at startup.

Ask the team for one relaunch when convenient: add --enable-prefix-caching and --kv-cache-dtype auto (block 4,176 -> ~2,176 so the static prompt gets cached); do not set --mamba-block-size; keep speculative decoding OFF in vLLM 0.26 until PR #56531 or #55504 lands, and if it is tried, gate it with a 60-prompt greedy equality test (spec vs no-spec outputs must match byte for byte). Report computed prompt tokens = prompt_tokens - cached_tokens in the bench once caching is on.

Do not spend time on LLMLingua-2/Selective Context except as one negative ablation row; hand-authored pruning (schema property-line pruning + k=3 skeleton-retrieved few-shots) is the token lever, but note it conflicts with static-prefix caching, so evaluate both configurations and report the trade-off.

Research phase after the demo: (a) ablation matrix on the 60-question bench plus a 150-200 question paraphrase/entity-swap extension (prompt variant x decoding constraint x verbalizer x n-candidates), reporting exec_acc, grounded, abstain, computed prompt tokens, completion tokens, p50/p95 latency and tokens-per-correct-answer; (b) the self-extending skeleton template cache measured on the paraphrase category; (c) logprob-gated repair budgeting; (d) reproduce the ngram corruption test on Nemotron as a documented negative result.

Keep the pipeline's honesty guarantees fixed across all variants (read-only guard, 'no matching records is not proof of absence', suggestion requires commander approval); treat any variant that lowers abstain_rate on the 6 unanswerable questions as rejected regardless of token savings.
resume_angle: Grounded-by-construction verbalization for KGQA on edge hardware: a single LLM call emits a Cypher query plus an answer template whose slots are bound to returned columns, so provenance/time/confidence can only come from graph rows; evaluated against a two-call generate-then-fact-check baseline on tokens, latency and grounding rate. Prior art templates the query (TeCoD, parameterized text2SQL) rather than the answer, which makes this defensible as a novel contribution.

A measured, decode-bound cost model of on-device Text2Cypher on an NVIDIA GB10 with a Mamba-2/attention/MoE hybrid: showing that ~85% of latency is decode at 45 tok/s, that prompt compression is the wrong lever at 5.5k tok/s prefill, and quantifying vLLM's hybrid prefix-cache cliff (4,176 tokens, derived analytically from the fp8-KV/fp32-SSM page ratio and halved by KV dtype) with a reproducible script.

Schema-constrained read-only Cypher grammar with a projection macro under a token budget: ablations on guard rejections, repair rounds, schema-violation errors and completion tokens, including a documented grammar-coercion failure mode (valid-but-nonsense output when the grammar omits a construct) and the CYGNET-style boundary between structural and semantic errors.

Rigorous negative results that reviewers value: LLMLingua-2 on structured schema prompts, and ngram speculative decoding correctness on Mamba hybrids in vLLM 0.26 (reproducing the open-PR corruption test on Nemotron), each with numbers rather than anecdotes.

A self-extending template library (question skeleton -> parameterised Cypher) that promotes LLM-generated queries into the model-free router, with exact-match-only hard hits and an explicit error analysis of similarity-threshold caches on a live, time-varying graph.
open_questions: Will the team accept a relaunch of the shared Nemotron with --enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype auto (and later spec decode)? Prefix caching for Mamba layers is logged as experimental in vLLM 0.26; stability under the vision model's co-residency is untested here.

How often does the baseline actually take a repair round or a fact-check regeneration? This decides how much latency the grammar and the template verbalizer recover; bench/results is empty until the baseline runs.

Does vLLM 0.26's chat-completions usage expose prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens once caching is on? The serving code references cached_tokens; verify the field after the relaunch so the benchmark can report computed tokens.

Are suffix decoding ('suffix') and ngram with num_speculative_tokens=1 affected by the same recurrent-state corruption on NemotronH in 0.26? Unverified; only the 60-prompt greedy-equality test can answer it.
Is training an EAGLE3 head for Nemotron-3-Nano feasible on the GB10 (memory headroom ~19 GB, data needs)? Unverified; a community head exists only for Nemotron-Cascade-2.
What is the real repetition rate of watch-officer questions during an incident? It sets the value of the skeleton cache; the bench's 6 paraphrase questions are a proxy only.

Clean idle timings: all live probes in this session ran under 1-3 concurrent requests from other users (decode 16-34 tok/s vs 45 idle); the baseline bench must be run on a quiet box or with concurrency recorded.

options.name: O1. RescueGrid-QA gold set: human seeds + execution-verified LLM paraphrases + difficulty/phrasing tiers + unanswerables
options.description: Build the gold set the way CypherBench, PIPE-Cypher and Mind-the-Query do, scaled to a fixed 6-label schema: (a) ~40 human-written seed questions covering the 9 operational categories (status, provenance, temporal, proximity/NEAR, route/CONNECTS_TO, aggregation, conflict, assignment, sensor) each with a gold Cypher that Kenil executes on the frozen snapshot bench/snapshots/baseline-v0/graph.json and inspects by hand; (b) 3-5 LLM-generated paraphrases per seed in fixed phrasing tiers (long NL, short NL, radio-speak/terse, and one 'semantically similar but different question' distractor with its own gold), each re-executed and manually spot-checked; (c) difficulty tiers assigned mechanically from the gold Cypher (Spider-style component count: hops, OPTIONAL MATCH, aggregation, path length, time filter) plus CypherBench-style pattern class; (d) ~24 unanswerable/abstain items in AbstentionBench-style categories that fit this domain: out-of-schema entity ('Where is Engine 12?'), out-of-schema property ('what is the wind speed'), false premise ('why did Building 22 collapse' when intact), underspecified ('is it safe?'), stale/time-travel ('what was the status yesterday' beyond the audit trail), non-query (dispatch/mutation requests = refusal category). Store as bench/questions.json with: id, seed_id, category, tier, phrasing, gold_cypher, compare mode, gold_row_hash, must_mention/must_not_mention, answerable, expected_abstain_category.
options.how_it_applies_here: bench/run_bench.py already reads bench/questions.json and computes exec_acc/grounded/facts/abstain, but the file does not exist yet, so there is no baseline number at all. The 7 pre-baked intents and 11 few-shot Q/Cypher pairs in schema_prompt.py must be marked as 'seen' seeds (leakage-aware split, as PIPE-Cypher does with few-shot signatures) and evaluated separately from unseen seeds; otherwise the LLM path's accuracy is inflated by questions it has verbatim in its prompt. The adversarial review's known failure modes (invented property names, over-filtering, reversed ABOUT direction) each get at least 3 seeds so the error taxonomy has power.
options.expected_token_effect: None on the system (measurement only). Bench runtime: ~140 questions x ~3.6k tokens = ~0.5M prompt tokens per full LLM-mode pass.
options.expected_latency_effect: None on the system. One full pass in mode=llm at ~5.5 s/question is ~13 min for 140 questions (x K repeats).
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Makes accuracy measurable; expect the honest baseline on unseen seeds to land well below the 'about two-thirds pass' from the adversarial review because paraphrase tiers (short/terse) are known to cut execution accuracy sharply (Jackal: 86.0% long NL vs 35.7% short NL for the same queries).
options.effort: ~1 day of Kenil's time: 4-6 h writing and executing 40 seed gold queries, 2-3 h generating/verifying ~140 paraphrases with the local model, 1 h unanswerables and the seen/unseen split.
options.risks: Self-authored gold (one annotator) is the weakest link; CypherBench had authors inspect every test item and PIPE-Cypher audited 80 judge labels with a second annotator. Gold Cypher that over-specifies columns makes strict EX fail spuriously; declare a compare mode per question. LLM paraphrases drift in meaning (CypherBench needed three verification rounds); every paraphrase must be re-executed and its rows compared to the seed's rows before acceptance. Paraphrases of one seed are correlated, so per-question CIs must use clustered SEs by seed.

evidence.claim: CypherBench generates questions by instantiating hand-written MATCH/RETURN templates on sampled subgraphs, LLM-rewriting to NL while preserving entity names, three rounds of LLM verification for meaning changes such as reversed relations, and the authors inspecting every test-set instance (2,488 questions across 7 domains).

PIPE-Cypher accepts only gold queries that execute non-empty, are read-only, parser-valid and schema-valid; it balances 8 workload categories at 375 each (3,000 examples, 0.609 acceptance rate) and finds zero-shot transfer 0.036 vs 0.200 with leakage-aware few-shot.

Mind the Query (EMNLP 2025 Industry) validates 27,529 NL/Cypher pairs over 11 graphs with automated schema, runtime and value checks plus manual review for logical correctness, and categorizes queries by complexity.

Jackal reports execution accuracy by request type for the same JQL: Long NL 86.0%, Short NL 35.7%, Semantically Similar 22.7%, Semantically Exact 99.3%, and ships a static snapshot for reproducibility.
Spider's hardness levels (easy/medium/hard/extra) are assigned mechanically from counts of SQL components (aggregates, select columns, where conditions, group by, nesting, set operations).
AbstentionBench groups unanswerable items into six categories (Answer Unknown, False Premise, Stale, Subjective, Underspecified Context, Underspecified Intent) across 20 datasets.
Neo4j's own error analysis found models struggle most with synthetic data sources and assigns easy/challenging tiers by quantiles of model scores rather than by query structure.

options.name: O2. Three-level execution accuracy: strict EX (CypherBench semantics) + key-projected EX + evidence-set Jaccard (PSJS adapted to entity ids)
options.description: Replace the single lenient exec_acc with three declared metrics. EX_strict(q)=1 iff predicted and gold result tables are identical up to row and column permutation, compared as multisets when the gold has no ORDER BY and as ordered lists when it does (floats rounded to 3 dp, datetimes ISO, nulls kept, nested lists sorted). EX_key(q)=1 iff the projection onto the question's declared key columns matches as a set (today's behaviour; keep it, but label it lenient). EvJ(q)=|E_pred ∩ E_gold|/|E_pred ∪ E_gold| where E is the set of entity ids appearing anywhere in the rows; this is CypherBench's Provenance Subgraph Jaccard adapted to ids because our rows already carry ids (no elementId rewrite needed). Report all three; use EX_strict as the headline text-to-Cypher number and EvJ as partial credit for 'right entities, wrong columns'.
options.how_it_applies_here: run_bench.py's score_exec defaults to compare={'key':['id']} as a set, so a query that returns the right ids with the wrong status/source/confidence columns scores 1.0, which is precisely the failure the compose step then propagates into the answer. Strict EX requires the gold Cypher to declare the columns the answer needs, which also forces gold authors to decide what 'the answer' is. EvJ is cheap to compute from existing rows and gives the error analysis a graded signal.
options.expected_token_effect: None (metric only).
options.expected_latency_effect: None; comparison cost is microseconds on 25-row results.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Headline number will drop versus key-projected EX; that is the point. FLEX found plain EX still carries both false positives and false negatives (average -3.15 from FP corrections, +6.07 from FN corrections on Spider/BIRD leaders), so keep a small manual audit of disagreements between EX_strict and EX_key.
options.effort: 2-3 h: port CypherBench's to_hashable/quick_rej/multiset logic (~100 lines), add per-question compare mode, add EvJ.
options.risks: Strict EX over-penalises benign extra columns (e.g., the model returns name and status when gold returns only status); mitigate with a 'gold columns subset' variant reported alongside. ORDER BY detection by substring is crude (CypherBench does the same). Nested collect() structures need deterministic sorting or they will spuriously mismatch.

evidence.claim: CypherBench's execution_accuracy.py converts rows to hashable tuples, treats order as mattering only when 'order by' appears in the target Cypher, compares as multisets (bags) otherwise, searches column permutations for equivalence, returns 1.0 when both results are empty and 0.0 on any exception.
CypherBench paper defines EX as two tables being identical if one can be transformed into the other by row and column permutations; gpt-4o scores 60.18%, llama3.1-8b 18.82%, llama3.2-3b 11.20%.
PSJS = |target_ps ∩ pred_ps| / |target_ps ∪ pred_ps| over element ids of the matched subgraph, obtained by rewriting the RETURN clause to collect(distinct elementId(var)).
BIRD defines EX as the proportion of examples whose predicted and gold SQL produce identical result sets, and VES as sqrt(E(gold)/E(pred)) efficiency credit only for EX-correct queries.
FLEX (NAACL 2025) reaches Cohen's kappa 87.04 with human experts versus 62.00 for EX and shifts leaderboard scores by -3.15 (false positives) and +6.07 (false negatives).

Neo4j's benchmark stringifies execution outputs of predicted and reference Cypher in the same order/format and applies ExactMatch; execution-based evaluation only covers the subset with a live database.

options.name: O3. Multi-snapshot semantic accuracy: test-suite accuracy adapted to a time-versioned property graph
options.description: Adapt Zhong et al.'s distilled test-suite idea: execute both gold and predicted Cypher on S=4-6 frozen graph snapshots taken at different replay points (e.g., after event 3, after the Bridge conflict, after extra_team_moves_away.json, after a synthetic 'conflict resolved' event, an empty-hazard world). EX_multi(q)=min over snapshots of EX_strict. A predicted query that only coincidentally matches on the demo snapshot (the classic over-filtering bug: adding 'AND h.source = radio_asr' that happens to be true today) is caught when the snapshot changes. No extra LLM calls: the same predicted Cypher is re-run on each snapshot (milliseconds).
options.how_it_applies_here: The graph is tiny (20-30 entities) so a single snapshot has very few distinguishing states; many wrong queries return the same 1-3 rows as the gold. The project already has a snapshot dump (bench/snapshots/baseline-v0/graph.json) and replay ingestion (scripts/ingest.py --reset + events/*.json), so additional snapshots are one ingest run each. This directly targets the adversarial-review failure classes 'over-filtering' and 'reversed direction', which are invisible on a snapshot where the filter is vacuous.
options.expected_token_effect: None (no additional LLM calls; predicted Cypher is cached from the primary run).
options.expected_latency_effect: Bench-only: +S Neo4j executions per question (~10-30 ms each per PIPE-Cypher's p50 12 ms / p95 33 ms). Needs a snapshot load/restore step (~seconds each) or S parallel databases.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: EX_multi ≤ EX_strict by construction; expect a visible gap, which is the finding (queries right for the wrong reason). Zhong et al. measured that single-database exact-set match yields 2.5% false negatives on average and 8.1% worst-case versus test-suite accuracy, and that single-db execution produces false positives that test suites remove.
options.effort: 3-4 h: a snapshot loader that restores graph.json into the private Neo4j (or a --snapshot flag to ingest.py), 4-5 event subsets, and a loop in run_bench. Half a day if a restore path from graph.json has to be written from scratch.
options.risks: Gold queries that legitimately depend on $now must be re-evaluated with each snapshot's replay clock (engine.now() already reads max(Event.timestamp)). Snapshots must be committed with hashes or results are not reproducible. Over-strict if a snapshot has zero rows for both (CypherBench returns 1.0 for empty==empty; keep that rule).

evidence.claim: Test-suite accuracy distills a small set of databases with high code coverage of the gold query and computes denotation accuracy on all of them, giving a tight upper bound on semantic accuracy; on 21 Spider submissions the single-db exact-set metric had 2.5% false negatives on average and 8.1% worst-case.
Jackal ships a static snapshot of the evaluated Jira instance because live systems drift and identical queries would otherwise produce different results.
PIPE-Cypher validates gold queries by deterministic execution on live Neo4j with p50 11.995 ms and p95 32.832 ms per query.

CypherBench error analysis on 50 sampled failures per model found reversed relation direction, entity-linking errors, schema violations (more common in small models) and MATCH patterns misaligned with question intent.

options.name: O4. Grounding by construction: structured claims in the compose schema, checked deterministically (LLM judge only for calibration)
options.description: Extend AnswerDraft (json_schema enforced by xgrammar) with claims: list of {entity_id, property, value, source?, time?, confidence?} (max ~6) and require every sentence of `answer` to be backed by a claim. Metrics: ClaimPrecision(q)=#claims supported by at least one row / #claims (a claim is supported iff the entity_id, property and value co-occur in one row or nested record, with source/time/confidence co-occurring in that same record); Grounded(q)=1 iff ClaimPrecision=1; UnsupportedClaimRate over all questions; plus the existing provenance-attribution check (fact_check) retained as ProvAttr. This turns 'faithfulness' from an LLM-judge score into a deterministic, auditable metric. Keep one LLM-as-judge faithfulness score (RAGAS-style claim decomposition with the local model) only as a secondary metric, validated once against ~80 human-labelled answers with Cohen's kappa reported.
options.how_it_applies_here: Today grounded_rate is a regex over source/time/confidence tokens and says nothing about status or entity claims ('Building 22 is collapsed' passes if no number is quoted). The compose step already uses grammar-constrained JSON with maxLength caps, so adding a claims array is a schema edit, not a new mechanism. The judge cannot be a frontier model (offline device), so a small local judge must be calibrated or it is noise; the deterministic check avoids that dependency for the headline number.
options.expected_token_effect: +40-90 completion tokens per composed answer (claims array), i.e. roughly +20-40% on call B's ~100 completion tokens; prompt +~60 tokens for the schema/instructions. No judge tokens for the headline metric.
options.expected_latency_effect: +1-2 s per LLM question at ~45 tok/s decode unless the answer text is shortened to compensate (claims can replace part of the prose budget).
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Grounded rate becomes stricter, so it will drop; but answer quality may rise because the model must name the row it is quoting (a form of self-verification). Unverified for this model; measure with the ablation 'claims on/off'.
options.effort: 3-4 h for schema + checker + bench metric; +2-3 h if the judge calibration study (80 labels) is done.
options.risks: Grammar-constrained decoding with more required fields can push the model to emit empty or template claims; cap and validate. Claims for aggregates (people=120) need a rule (value equals a row value or a sum over rows). LLM judges show position, verbosity and self-preference biases and are unreliable for RAG without domain calibration; a self-judged score (same Nemotron judging Nemotron) is the textbook self-preference case and must not be the headline.

evidence.claim: RAGAS faithfulness = supported claims / total claims after decomposing the answer into atomic statements and NLI-style verification; scores drift when decomposition over/under-splits and the judge must be treated as part of the metric definition.

Eval-Pair Matrix (July 2026) finds judges under-flag answers that sidestep induced contradictions (-4.3 pp) and recommends reporting full judge matrices, answer-paired effects and label-task alignment for grounded RAG judge studies.
LLM judges exhibit position bias (swapping order shifts pairwise accuracy by >10% in code judging), verbosity bias and self-preference bias (higher scores for lower-perplexity, self-like outputs).
Self-preference bias: an LLM judge assigns higher scores to outputs with lower perplexity under its own policy.
PIPE-Cypher calibrates a local Qwen3.5-9B judge against 80 human labels: Cohen's kappa 0.60, 80.0% agreement, precision 1.00, recall 0.714.
Landis & Koch bands (0.41-0.60 moderate, 0.61-0.80 substantial, 0.81-1.00 almost perfect) are widely used but were not empirically justified; Fleiss uses >0.75 excellent, 0.40-0.75 fair to good.

options.name: O5. Abstention and reliability scoring: explicit answerable flag + AbstentionBench recall/precision + TrustSQL penalty score
options.description: Add `answerable: bool` and `abstain_reason` enum (no_matching_records, out_of_schema, underspecified, false_premise, refusal_readonly, refusal_dispatch) to the structured output so abstention is detected from a field, not a regex. Metrics: AbstentionRecall = correct abstentions / unanswerable items (per category); FalseRefusalRate = abstentions on answerable items / answerable items (= 1 - abstention precision's complement, report both); RefusalAccuracy on mutation/dispatch prompts (must be 1.0 and graph counts unchanged, already tested); Reliability Score RS_c = mean over all items of (+1 correct answer or correct abstention; 0 abstain on answerable; -c wrong answer or answering an unanswerable) for c in {0, 10, N}. Also report coverage (fraction answered) vs accuracy-when-answered as a selective-prediction pair.
options.how_it_applies_here: ABSTAIN_RX in run_bench.py matches phrases like 'no matching record'; any wording change in engine.py silently breaks the metric, and the regex cannot distinguish an honest 'no records' from a wrong query that returned zero rows (the engine reports both identically). In an EOC, answering an unanswerable question wrongly costs more than abstaining, which is exactly TrustSQL's asymmetric-penalty argument; RS_10 is the metric to optimise, not raw accuracy. AbstentionBench's finding that reasoning mode worsens abstention is directly relevant to the enable_thinking ablation.
options.expected_token_effect: +~10 completion tokens per composed answer for the two fields.
options.expected_latency_effect: Negligible (<0.3 s).
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Exposes the trade-off: stricter guards/zero-row handling raise abstention recall but raise false refusals (Ozsoy 2026 saw stricter grammar/schema filtering increase empty predictions and reduce coverage). RS_10 will reward the current 'honest empty result' behaviour over invented answers.
options.effort: ~2 h (fields, checker, metrics, 24 unanswerable items shared with O1).
options.risks: Zero-row results from a wrong query are still reported as 'no matching records', which scores as a correct abstention on unanswerables but as a false negative on answerables; the multi-snapshot EX (O3) and EvJ separate these. Penalty c is a design choice; report all three so reviewers cannot accuse cherry-picking.

evidence.claim: TrustSQL's Reliability Score gives +1 for correct SQL or correct abstention, 0 for abstaining on feasible questions, and -c for wrong SQL or answering infeasible questions, evaluated at c=0, 10 and N; an all-abstain baseline scores 50% at every c.

AbstentionBench reports abstention recall, precision and F1 using a Llama-3.1-8B judge with 88% accuracy on human-annotated samples; scaling reasoning budget generally worsens abstention; a system prompt encouraging abstention boosts recall without significant precision loss.

Query Carefully builds 80 no-answer questions in 8 categories (non-SQL, out-of-schema column/value, out-of-domain, four ambiguity types) against 99 answerable ones and reports 0.8 overall unanswerable detection with only 0.3 on column ambiguity and 0.5 on missing values.
Grammar- and schema-aware filtering at test time improves executable validity but stricter filtering increases empty predictions and reduces execution coverage (reliability vs recall trade-off).

CYGNET's pre-execution gate catches 100% of parse, constraint and schema-reference errors at 5.6 ms median latency with zero false positives on 1,135 labelled queries, but scores 0% on semantic sibling-swaps, marking the structural/semantic boundary.

options.name: O6. Statistical protocol: K repeats, pass^K, Wilson CIs with seed-clustered SEs, paired McNemar vs baseline, power table
options.description: Because temperature 0 is measurably non-deterministic on this endpoint (probe: 8 identical calls on 2 prompts produced 5 distinct Cypher outputs, one syntactically invalid), every configuration is run K times (K=3 for demo-day, K=5 for the report) and scored per run. Report per metric: mean ± SE (Miller's CLT SE with clustering by seed_id because paraphrases of one seed are correlated), Wilson 95% CI on the per-question mean-of-K, pass^K (all K runs correct) and pass@K as reliability bounds, and for every comparison against baseline-v0 a paired analysis on the same questions: paired-difference SE and an exact McNemar test on discordant question pairs (majority-of-K outcome). Record the discordance rate q to size future runs.
options.how_it_applies_here: With n≈140 questions and observed accuracy ~0.7 the Wilson 95% CI half-width is about ±7.5 pp (±11.3 pp at n=60, ±15.6 pp at n=30), so any single-run 'improvement' below ~8 pp is noise; paired design rescues this: with q=0.25 disagreement, a 15 pp paired improvement needs only ~80 questions at 80% power, and 12 fixed vs 2 broken questions is already p=0.013 by exact McNemar. K repeats also give the demo a 'worst-case' story (pass^3 = 0.343 at per-question p=0.7 vs 0.729 at p=0.9), which is what an EOC user cares about.
options.expected_token_effect: Bench cost x K (K=3: ~1.5M prompt tokens per full LLM-mode pass). No system change.
options.expected_latency_effect: Bench wall time x K: ~13 min x 3 ≈ 40 min per configuration in mode=llm on an otherwise idle box; an 8-cell ablation grid at K=3 is ~5-6 h of box time.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: None on the system; changes what can be claimed. Expect pass^3 to be 10-25 pp below mean accuracy given the observed output variance (unverified until measured).
options.effort: ~2 h to add K, aggregation, Wilson/clustered SE, paired McNemar and pass^K to run_bench; box time as above.
options.risks: Latency numbers are confounded by co-tenant load on the shared GPU (vision/ASR); log concurrent load or run with the box idle and state it. Miller advises against lowering temperature just to reduce variance unless the deployed setting is that temperature (here it is: temperature 0 is the production setting, so it is legitimate, but sampling variance must still be reported). If the team enables batch-invariant kernels or disables prefix caching later, results shift; pin the server config hash in each results file.

evidence.claim: Local probe on the ZRT/vLLM endpoint (thinking off, temperature 0, max_tokens 300): 5 identical text2cypher calls gave 2 distinct outputs (one valid, one syntactically invalid pattern); 3 identical calls on a second question gave 3 distinct outputs; usage.prompt_tokens_details was absent (no cached_tokens reporting).

Miller (Anthropic, 2024): SE_CLT = sqrt(Var(s)/n); clustered SEs can exceed naive SEs by >3x; paired-difference SE = sqrt(Var(s_A - s_B)/n) exploits agreement on easy/hard questions; with K resamples Var(s_i)=σ_i²/K and K should grow only until E[σ_i²]/K ≪ Var(x); detecting a 3% difference at 80% power needs ~969 questions unpaired; advises against changing temperature to reduce variance unless studying that temperature.

Thinking Machines: with temperature-0 greedy decoding, Qwen3-235B produced 80 unique completions out of 1000 identical runs (divergence around token 103) because kernels are not batch-invariant; batch-invariant kernels made 1000/1000 identical.

Patodiya (Sept 2026): prefix caching makes identical requests diverge in 36.2% of episodes at 16-bit and 75.0% at 4-bit weight quantization; with caching disabled repeated execution was bit-identical, bounding other nondeterminism at 0.5%.
tau-bench's pass^k = probability that all k i.i.d. trials succeed (p^k), a strict reliability measure versus pass@k.
Wilson score interval is recommended as the default binomial CI, safe for small samples and extreme proportions; Wald intervals are not.
Dietterich (1998) recommends McNemar's test for comparing two classifiers on the same test set when retraining is impractical; it is as powerful as the 5x2cv t-test in that setting.

Computed on the box for this design: Wilson 95% CI half-width at p=0.70 is ±0.156 (n=30), ±0.113 (n=60), ±0.089 (n=100), ±0.073 (n=150); exact McNemar p=0.013 for 12 fixed/2 broken; paired n≈80 for delta=0.15 at q=0.25; pass^3 = 0.343 at p=0.7, 0.729 at p=0.9.
evidence.source_url: local computation (no URL); formulas per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binomial_proportion_confidence_interval and https://arxiv.org/html/2411.00640

options.name: O7. Cost accounting: per-call token ledger, cached-token reporting, latency percentiles, tokens/seconds-per-correct (Cost-of-Pass), accuracy-vs-cost Pareto
options.description: Extend the CALLS ledger to record per call: role (cypher, repair_k, zero_row_retry, compose, compose_retry), prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cached_tokens (usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens when the server exposes it), finish_reason, seconds, and concurrent-load marker. Per question: total tokens, LLM calls, LLM-seconds, wall p50/p95; per configuration: TokensPerCorrect = mean total tokens / accuracy (Cost-of-Pass with tokens as the currency, since inference is local and dollar cost is 0), SecondsPerCorrect = mean wall / accuracy, and an accuracy-vs-mean-tokens Pareto plot across all variants (baseline, schema-pruned, fewer shots, no repair, claims on/off, thinking on/off). Also VES-style efficiency credit is unnecessary here (queries run in ms) but Cypher execution time should be logged to catch runaway path queries.
options.how_it_applies_here: The stated goal is token efficiency; without a ledger split by call role you cannot tell whether savings come from a smaller schema prompt (call A, 2,765 tokens recomputed every time because the 4,176-token KV block prevents prefix-cache hits) or from fewer repair rounds. Cached tokens are currently not reported by the server (probe showed prompt_tokens_details=None), so a cache-hit metric requires the team to start vLLM with --enable-prompt-tokens-details; until then, the block-size fact implies cached=0 and should be stated. Kapoor et al.'s warning applies verbatim: repair rounds and zero-row retries are 'repeated sampling' that buy accuracy with tokens and must be shown on the Pareto plot, not hidden in accuracy.
options.expected_token_effect: None on the system; makes the token effect of every other option measurable.
options.expected_latency_effect: None.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: None; reframes the headline as accuracy per 1k tokens and per second.
options.effort: 1-2 h in run_bench (ledger fields + two derived metrics + a matplotlib Pareto script). Server flag change is a team decision, not code.
options.risks: Latency on a shared GPU is not a property of the method; report LLM-seconds and tokens as primary, wall-clock as secondary with load noted. Cached-token counters in vLLM have had bugs (e.g., disaggregated mode reporting prompt_tokens-1); validate against the 4,176-block expectation.

evidence.claim: Kapoor et al.: report dollar/token cost alongside accuracy, plot accuracy-cost Pareto frontiers, because repeated sampling inflates accuracy; simple retry/warming/escalation baselines Pareto-dominate LATS which costs over 50x more.
Cost-of-Pass (ICLR 2026) formalizes the expected cost of generating a correct solution (cost per attempt / success probability) and frontier cost-of-pass across models.

vLLM reports usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens only when started with --enable-prompt-tokens-details together with prefix caching; there are open bugs about zero-cached-token omission and disaggregated-mode miscounts.
Schema filtering cut the P95 prompt from 2,697 tokens (enhanced schema) to 529 (exact-match pruning), with 7-8B models performing better on shorter prompts and Gemini-1.5-Flash losing under 5%.
Adaptive trace budgeting cut average generation budget 30.7% and wall-clock 21-25% at comparable quality; selective refinement lost only 0.2-0.5% execution success.
BIRD's VES credits efficiency only for EX-correct queries via sqrt(E(gold)/E(pred)).

options.name: O8. Paraphrase-robustness and consistency as first-class axes (phrasing tiers, per-seed consistency rate)
options.description: Score every seed across its phrasing tier variants and report: accuracy per tier (long NL / short NL / radio-speak / distractor), ConsistencyRate = fraction of seeds whose variants all yield the same EX_strict outcome (and the same entity-id set), and Mizrahi-style max/avg/min-over-paraphrases performance. Treat the pre-baked regex router as a system under test here: a router miss on a paraphrase silently changes which path answers.
options.how_it_applies_here: The regex intent router is brittle by design (tests/test_qa_review_regressions.py already enumerates phrasing fixes), and the LLM path's few-shots are verbatim seeds. A watch officer under stress speaks in fragments ('bridge status?', 'RT4 where'), which is exactly Jackal's Short-NL regime where the best model fell from 86.0% to 35.7%. Reporting tiers separately prevents a 'long NL only' benchmark from overstating field readiness.
options.expected_token_effect: None on the system.
options.expected_latency_effect: Bench time scales with the number of variants (already counted in O1).
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Expect a large gap between tiers; the gap itself is a headline finding and motivates the router/normalisation ablation.
options.effort: ~1 h of scoring code once O1's questions carry seed_id and phrasing fields.
options.risks: Paraphrase generation by the same model that is evaluated leaks its own phrasing preferences (a self-preference analogue); mix in human-written short forms from the regression tests and from teammates. Clustered SEs by seed are mandatory (Miller).

evidence.claim: Mizrahi et al. (TACL 2024): across 6.5M instances, 20 LLMs and 39 tasks, different instruction paraphrases change both absolute performance and model rankings; they propose max/avg/combined/saturation metrics over paraphrases.
Jackal: the same JQL targets scored 86.0% (Long NL), 35.7% (Short NL), 22.7% (Semantically Similar), 99.3% (Semantically Exact).
SCORE evaluates each question under 10 semantically equivalent prompts and reports a Consistency Rate; PARACONSIST and PromptSET are 2025 paraphrase-sensitivity benchmarks.
Clustered standard errors are needed when questions come in correlated groups; ignoring clustering understates SE by up to >3x.

options.name: O9. Fixed error taxonomy + ablation grid (the part that separates research from prompt-tweaking)
options.description: Label every failed question (majority-of-K) with one primary code from a closed taxonomy merged from CypherBench and Neo4j's analysis: reversed_direction, invented_property, invented_label_or_value, entity_linking (name vs id, alias miss), over_filtering (extra WHERE), under_filtering, wrong_pattern (MATCH not matching intent), wrong_aggregation_or_order, guard_rejection, syntax_error, zero_rows_true_negative, compose_ungrounded (rows right, answer wrong), highlight_wrong, timeout/format. Then run a pre-registered ablation grid with K repeats and paired stats: few-shots {0, 5, 11}; schema {full, pruned-by-question}; repair rounds {0, 1, 2}; zero-row retry {on, off}; compose fact-check regeneration {on, off}; structured claims {on, off}; thinking {off, on} (with max_tokens raised); plus a 'model swap' cell if a second small text2cypher model fits in the free 19 GB (team decision). Report per-cell accuracy, tokens, and the error-code histogram shift.
options.how_it_applies_here: The adversarial review's three named failure classes are already taxonomy codes; the grid's cells map one-to-one onto existing switches in text2cypher.py (max_repairs, zero-row retry), engine.py (fact-check regeneration), schema_prompt.py (few-shots, schema text) and the request's enable_thinking flag, so no new machinery is needed to run it. The ablation is what turns 'we changed the prompt' into 'component X accounts for Y pp at Z tokens'.
options.expected_token_effect: Bench cost: ~10 cells x K=3 x ~0.5M prompt tokens ≈ 15M prompt tokens of local inference; no dollar cost.
options.expected_latency_effect: ~5-7 h of box time for the grid at K=3 (LLM-only mode, 140 questions), best run overnight with the box idle.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Identifies which components carry accuracy; literature suggests schema pruning is neutral-to-positive for 7-8B-class models and repair rounds buy accuracy at token cost; reasoning mode may hurt abstention (AbstentionBench) while helping hard multi-hop queries (unverified for Nemotron-3-Nano).
options.effort: Taxonomy labelling: ~1-2 h per configuration for a 50-failure sample (CypherBench's sample size). Grid runner: ~2 h. Box time as above.
options.risks: Pre-register the grid and the primary metric (RS_10 or EX_strict) before running, otherwise it is p-hacking with extra steps. Manual labels by one person; have a teammate double-label 20 items and report agreement. Thinking-on cells need larger max_tokens and will dominate wall time.

evidence.claim: CypherBench's human error analysis used 50 randomly sampled incorrect predictions per model and 10 categories including reversed direction, entity linking, schema violations and pattern misalignment.

Neo4j's analysis lists additional matches/fields, wrong ground truth, naming mismatches, WHERE-vs-property confusion and node-vs-property confusion, plus ambiguity (top-k without a ranking key) and MAX-vs-ORDER BY choices.
Schema filtering: 7-8B models performed better with shorter prompts; larger models benefit less but still save cost.
AbstentionBench: reasoning interventions degrade abstention despite boosting accuracy, across 20 frontier LLMs.
Kapoor et al. document that repeated sampling/retry confounds architecture comparisons unless cost is controlled.

options.name: O10. Reproducibility artefacts and the short technical report / benchmark card
options.description: Every results file records: git sha (exists), questions.json sha256, snapshot sha256(s), prompt hash (SCHEMA_TEXT + ANSWER_SYSTEM), model id and served-model config (vLLM version 0.26.0, FP8, max-model-len, block size 4176, prefix caching on/off, thinking flag), K, temperature, sampling params, bench mode, box load note, timestamp. Tag each milestone (baseline-v0 exists; add bench-v0 when the first full K=3 baseline run lands). Publish a benchmark card (datasheet-style: motivation, composition by category/tier/phrasing, collection process, verification, known limitations, leakage split) and, if time allows post-demo, Croissant metadata for the question set. Report structure (6-8 pages): 1 Problem and constraints (offline, provenance, humans-in-control); 2 Baseline system; 3 RescueGrid-QA benchmark (construction, tiers, unanswerables, verification, statistics); 4 Metrics (formal definitions from O2-O8); 5 Results: baseline with CIs, ablation grid with paired tests, Pareto plot; 6 Error analysis by taxonomy; 7 Limitations (small synthetic graph, single annotator, single model family, shared-GPU latency); 8 Reproducibility (hashes, commands, seeds); appendices: prompts, gold set card, raw tables.
options.how_it_applies_here: bench/run_bench.py is still untracked (git status shows '?? bench/run_bench.py') and bench/results is empty, so the 'recoverable state' the developer asked for currently covers the graph and code but not the benchmark. A results file that lacks the prompt hash cannot distinguish a prompt change from a model-behaviour change, which matters because the server is non-deterministic.
options.expected_token_effect: None.
options.expected_latency_effect: None.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: None; determines whether any number can be defended later.
options.effort: ~1 h for hashes/config capture in run_bench; 3-4 h for the report skeleton and benchmark card after the demo.
options.risks: Shared Neo4j (port 7688) must never be benchmarked (run_bench already refuses); if Shresth's schema diverges, the benchmark stays pinned to the private snapshot and says so. Over-claiming novelty in the report is the main reputational risk; see resume_angle.

evidence.claim: NeurIPS 2025 Datasets & Benchmarks introduced mandatory structured (Croissant) metadata and a formal checklist; 85.7% of 497 accepted papers include a retrievable Croissant document.
Kapoor et al. document standardization failures in agent evals: inconsistent benchmark modifications, missing error bars, external dependencies, and subtle implementation bugs.
Jackal and CypherBench both ship static snapshots plus open scoring code as the reproducibility unit for execution-based benchmarks.
Prefix-cache state must be explicitly managed and recorded for reproducible LLM evaluation (divergence 36.2%-75% with caching on).

key_facts.fact: The local ZRT/vLLM Nemotron endpoint is not deterministic at temperature 0 with thinking off: 5 identical text2cypher requests produced 2 distinct outputs (calls 2-5 identical to each other but different from call 1; the majority variant contained an invalid pattern '-[h:Hazard]-[:AFFECTS]->'), and 3 identical requests on a second question produced 3 distinct queries; prompt_tokens=2,778 for the schema prompt + question; usage.prompt_tokens_details was None (no cached_tokens reporting).

bench/run_bench.py exists but is untracked in git; bench/questions.json does not exist; bench/results/ is empty; the only tag is baseline-v0 with a graph dump at bench/snapshots/baseline-v0/graph.json. Its exec_acc defaults to a set comparison on key column ['id'] (lenient), its abstention metric is a regex over answer text, and it has no repeats, CIs, per-tier or per-seed grouping.

CypherBench (11 property graphs, >10k questions): gpt-4o 60.18% EX, claude-3.5-sonnet 61.58%, llama3.1-70b 38.84%, llama3.1-8b 18.82%, llama3.2-3b 11.20%; no <10B model exceeds 20%; EX = tables equal up to row/column permutation; PSJS = Jaccard over matched element ids.
CypherBench's scorer compares rows as multisets when the gold has no 'order by', as ordered lists otherwise, searches column permutations, scores empty==empty as 1.0 and any exception as 0.0.

Test-suite accuracy (Zhong et al., EMNLP 2020): single-database exact-set matching had 2.5% false negatives on average and 8.1% worst-case across 21 Spider submissions; distilled multi-database suites give a tight upper bound on semantic accuracy.
FLEX (NAACL 2025): LLM-expert judging reaches Cohen's kappa 87.04 vs 62.00 for execution accuracy; re-scoring Spider/BIRD leaders moved scores -3.15 (false positives) and +6.07 (false negatives).
Neo4j evaluates Text2Cypher with Google-BLEU (lexical) and execution-based ExactMatch on stringified results; the 2025v1 dataset has 40,384 rows (35.9k train / 4.44k test).

Schema filtering (Ozsoy 2025) reduced P95 prompt tokens from 2,697 (enhanced schema) to 917 (base), 529 (exact-match pruning), 532 (NER-masked pruning), 753 (similarity); Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B did better with shorter prompts; Gemini-1.5-Flash lost <5%.

Adaptive test-time inference for Text2Cypher (Ozsoy, Sept 2026): 30.7% lower average generation budget and 21-25% wall-clock savings at comparable quality; selective refinement lost only 0.2-0.5% execution success.
Grammar- and schema-aware test-time filtering (Ozsoy, May 2026) raises syntactic validity and execution quality but stricter filtering increases empty predictions and lowers coverage.

CYGNET (June 2026): a 5.6 ms median pre-execution gate catches 100% of parse, constraint and schema-reference errors on 1,135 labelled queries with zero false positives; an LLM corrector succeeds 81-95% (mean 89%) across five models; semantic sibling-swaps are caught 0%.

PIPE-Cypher (June 2026): 3,000 accepted NL-Cypher pairs over FinBench/SNB, 8 balanced workload categories x 375, 1,569 easy / 1,431 medium, local Qwen3.5-9B judge calibrated on 80 human labels (kappa 0.60, precision 1.00, recall 0.714), zero-shot mean EX 0.036 vs 0.200 leakage-aware few-shot across 11 models.
Mind the Query (EMNLP 2025 Industry): 27,529 NL/Cypher pairs over 11 graphs validated by automated schema, runtime and value checks plus manual logical review, categorized by complexity.

Jackal (Sept 2025): 100k NL-JQL pairs with execution-based scoring on a static snapshot; best model 60.3% EX averaged over request types: Long NL 86.0%, Short NL 35.7%, Semantically Similar 22.7%, Semantically Exact 99.3%.

TrustSQL's Reliability Score: +1 correct answer or correct abstention, 0 abstain-on-answerable, -c wrong answer or answering an infeasible question, evaluated at c=0, 10, N; an all-abstain baseline scores 50% at every c.

AbstentionBench (NeurIPS 2025): 20 datasets, 6 abstention categories; abstention detected by a Llama-3.1-8B judge with 88% accuracy on human-annotated samples; metrics are abstention recall/precision/F1; scaling reasoning budget generally worsens abstention; an abstention-encouraging system prompt helps.
Query Carefully (Dec 2025): 80 no-answer questions in 8 categories vs 99 answerable; 0.8 overall unanswerable detection, 0.3 on column ambiguity, 0.5 on missing values.

Miller (Anthropic, Nov 2024): report CLT standard errors (sqrt(Var/n)), use clustered SEs for grouped questions (can be >3x naive), use paired differences on shared questions, add K resamples until E[σ_i²]/K ≪ Var(x); ~969 questions to detect a 3% difference at 80% power unpaired; do not lower temperature merely to reduce variance.
Thinking Machines (2025): temperature-0 greedy decoding of Qwen3-235B gave 80 unique completions in 1000 runs due to non-batch-invariant kernels; batch-invariant kernels gave 1000/1000 identical.

Patodiya (Sept 2026): with prefix caching enabled, identical requests diverged in 36.2% of episodes at 16-bit and 75.0% at 4-bit quantization over 800 agentic episodes; caching off was bit-identical, bounding other sources at 0.5%.
vLLM emits usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens only with --enable-prompt-tokens-details (and prefix caching on); open issues cover omitted zeros and disaggregated-mode miscounts.

Kapoor et al. (AI Agents That Matter): evaluate accuracy jointly with cost (tokens/dollars), plot Pareto frontiers; simple retry/warming/escalation baselines Pareto-dominate LATS, which costs >50x more; repeated sampling confounds comparisons; most agent benchmarks lack proper holdouts and error bars.
Cost-of-Pass (ICLR 2026) defines the expected cost of obtaining a correct solution as the economic metric and shows frontier cost-of-pass halving every 2.6 months on MATH500 (May 2024-Feb 2025).
tau-bench's pass^k is the probability that all k trials succeed (p^k), a strict reliability metric distinct from pass@k.

Mizrahi et al. (TACL 2024): across 6.5M instances, 20 LLMs, 39 tasks, single-prompt evaluation is brittle and paraphrases change absolute scores and rankings; they propose max/avg/combined/saturation metrics over paraphrases.

LLM-as-judge surveys document position bias (>10% accuracy shifts from swapping order in pairwise code judging), verbosity bias and self-preference bias (favouring low-perplexity, self-like outputs); off-the-shelf chat-validated judges are unreliable for RAG without domain calibration.

Eval-Pair Matrix (July 2026): RAG faithfulness judges under-flag answers that avoid an induced contradictory claim (-4.3 pp); recommends reporting full judge matrices, answer-paired effects and label-task alignment.

RAGAS faithfulness = supported claims / total claims via statement decomposition + NLI-style verification; scores shift materially with judge model/prompt, so the judge is part of the metric definition.
Landis & Koch kappa bands (0.41-0.60 moderate, 0.61-0.80 substantial, 0.81-1.00 almost perfect) rest on opinion, not evidence; Fleiss uses >0.75 excellent, 0.40-0.75 fair-to-good.
NeurIPS 2025 Datasets & Benchmarks requires structured Croissant metadata and a formal checklist; 426 of 497 accepted papers (85.7%) include a retrievable Croissant document.

Computed on the box for this design: Wilson 95% CI half-width at observed accuracy 0.70 is ±0.156 (n=30), ±0.113 (n=60), ±0.089 (n=100), ±0.073 (n=150), ±0.051 (n=300); exact McNemar two-sided p = 0.039 (8 fixed/1 broken), 0.013 (12/2), 0.077 (12/4); paired questions needed at 80% power: ~80 for a 15 pp gain with 25% discordance, ~189 for 10 pp; pass^3 = 0.343 at p=0.7, 0.512 at 0.8, 0.729 at 0.9.
key_facts.source_url: local computation (no URL); formulas per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binomial_proportion_confidence_interval and https://arxiv.org/html/2411.00640

key_facts.fact: KGQA convention: Hits@1 = gold set intersects the first answer set; F1 = set-level precision/recall between predicted and gold answer sets; papers have inconsistently labelled the same computation Hits@1 vs Hit (attribution of the unified-protocol proposal unverified).

recommendations: BEFORE THE DEMO (about 6-8 h of work, the rest is box time): (1) commit bench/run_bench.py and tag bench-v0; (2) write bench/questions.json v0: 30-40 human seeds with gold Cypher executed on the frozen snapshot and hand-checked, mark the 7 pre-baked intents and 11 few-shots as 'seen', add 15-24 unanswerables and 4 mutation/dispatch refusals; (3) add EX_strict (CypherBench multiset/ordered semantics) next to today's key-projected EX, and EvJ; (4) add K=3 repeats, mean±SE, Wilson 95% CI, pass^3, and the per-call token ledger with cached_tokens (will be null until the server flag is on: say so); (5) run baseline-v0 in mode=auto and mode=llm at K=3 with the box otherwise idle and freeze bench/results/baseline-v0-*.json with questions/snapshot/prompt hashes. This produces the one defensible baseline table for the demo.

AFTER THE DEMO, in this order: O3 multi-snapshot EX (biggest credibility gain per hour, no LLM cost), O5 explicit answerable/abstain fields + RS_c, O4 structured claims + deterministic ClaimPrecision (with a one-time 80-item human calibration of any LLM judge), O1 paraphrase tiers to ~140 questions, then the pre-registered O9 ablation grid at K=3-5 overnight, then O10 report and benchmark card.

METRIC DEFINITIONS TO ADOPT VERBATIM: EX_strict(q)=1 iff multiset(rows_pred)=multiset(rows_gold) up to column permutation (ordered if gold has ORDER BY; floats 3 dp; ISO datetimes; nested lists sorted). EX_key(q): set equality on declared key columns (lenient, secondary). EX_multi(q)=min_s EX_strict on snapshots s in S. EvJ(q)=|ids_pred ∩ ids_gold| / |ids_pred ∪ ids_gold| over entity ids in rows. ClaimPrecision(q)=#claims with (entity_id, property, value[, source, time, confidence]) co-occurring in one row or nested record / #claims; Grounded(q)=1 iff ClaimPrecision=1; ProvAttr(q)=1 iff current fact_check returns no problems. HighlightAcc(q)=1 iff highlight.id equals the gold subject id. AbstentionRecall = correct abstentions / unanswerable; FalseRefusal = abstentions / answerable; RS_c = mean(+1 correct-or-correct-abstain, 0 abstain-on-answerable, -c wrong-or-answered-unanswerable), c in {0,10,N}. Correct(q) = EX_strict AND Grounded AND HighlightAcc for answerable; = correct abstention for unanswerable. Reliability: per-question mean over K, pass^K, pass@K; ConsistencyRate over paraphrase groups. Cost: prompt/completion/cached tokens per call role, LLM calls per question, LLM-seconds, wall p50/p95, TokensPerCorrect = mean total tokens / Correct rate, SecondsPerCorrect. Uncertainty: seed-clustered SE, Wilson 95% CI, paired McNemar exact p vs baseline-v0 on majority-of-K outcomes.

RESULTS TABLE LAYOUT (Table 1, one row per system variant: baseline-v0 auto | baseline-v0 llm-only | each ablation cell | final): columns = n | K | Correct % [95% CI] | EX_strict % | EX_multi % | EX_key % | EvJ | ClaimPrec % | Grounded % | HighlightAcc % | AbsRecall % | FalseRefusal % | RS_10 | pass^3 % | Consistency % | prompt tok/q (cached) | compl tok/q | calls/q | LLM s/q | wall p50/p95 s | tok-per-correct | Δ Correct vs baseline (paired, McNemar p). Table 2: Correct % by category (status, provenance, temporal, proximity, route, aggregation, conflict, assignment, sensor, unanswerable, refusal) x phrasing tier (long/short/radio/distractor) x difficulty (easy/medium/hard), with seen vs unseen seeds split. Table 3: error-taxonomy histogram per variant (counts of reversed_direction, invented_property, entity_linking, over_filtering, wrong_pattern, wrong_aggregation, guard_rejection, syntax_error, compose_ungrounded, highlight_wrong, other). Figure 1: accuracy (Correct % and RS_10) vs mean total tokens per question, one point per variant with CI bars, Pareto frontier drawn. Figure 2: pass^k for k=1..5 per variant.

DO NOT: report a single-run accuracy; use the same Nemotron as an uncalibrated judge of its own answers as the headline grounding metric; benchmark against the shared Neo4j on 7688; include the 11 few-shot questions in the 'unseen' score; treat wall-clock on the shared GPU as a property of the method (report LLM-seconds and tokens first); change temperature to make numbers stable (production is temperature 0; report the variance instead).

ASK THE TEAM (server-side, not code): start vLLM with --enable-prompt-tokens-details so cached_tokens is reported; record the exact serving flags (block size 4176, prefix caching, FP8) in the results metadata; if a batch-invariant or caching-off run is possible during a quiet window, run baseline K=5 once under it to quantify how much of the observed variance is serving-induced.

GOLD-SET HYGIENE: every gold Cypher must (a) execute non-empty on the primary snapshot unless the question is a legitimate 'none' case, (b) return the columns the answer needs (id, status, status_since, source, confidence, raw_evidence_ref where relevant), (c) carry a declared compare mode and key columns, (d) be re-executed on every snapshot with its row hash stored; paraphrases inherit the seed's gold and are rejected if their intent changed; have one teammate blind-check 20 seeds and report agreement.

RESUME-SAFE FRAMING OF THE CONTRIBUTION: 'a provenance- and time-first text-to-Cypher benchmark with multi-snapshot execution accuracy, penalty-scored abstention, deterministic claim-level grounding, and cost-per-correct accounting for an on-device 3B-active MoE, with K-repeat paired statistics that quantify FP8/serving nondeterminism' — not 'improved prompt accuracy from X to Y'.
resume_angle: Grounding by construction: forcing the answer step to emit machine-checkable claims under grammar-constrained decoding turns 'faithfulness' from an LLM-judge score (biased, uncalibrated, expensive offline) into a deterministic metric with 100% coverage and zero judge tokens; reporting ClaimPrecision alongside a human-calibrated judge (kappa on 80 items) is a methodological claim that survives scrutiny regardless of how good the model is.

Multi-snapshot execution accuracy for a time-versioned property graph: adapting distilled test-suite accuracy (text-to-SQL, 2020) to Cypher over replayed graph states; no current Cypher benchmark (CypherBench, Neo4j text2cypher-2025v1, Mind the Query, PIPE-Cypher, Jackal) scores queries across multiple graph states, and the audit-trail/replay design of RescueGrid makes it nearly free. The measurable gap EX_strict - EX_multi is a novel, honest number.

Quantified serving nondeterminism as an evaluation confound on edge hardware: an FP8 hybrid-Mamba MoE served by vLLM on GB10 produced 5 distinct temp-0 Cypher outputs in 8 identical calls; reporting pass^k, seed-clustered CIs and paired McNemar tests, and tying variance to serving config, is exactly the rigor recent work (Miller 2024; Thinking Machines 2025; Patodiya 2026) calls for and almost no applied text-to-Cypher project does.

Reliability-scored abstention for an operational domain: penalty-based RS_c (TrustSQL) plus AbstentionBench-style categories tailored to EOC questions (out-of-schema unit, false-premise collapse, stale time-travel, dispatch refusal) gives a decision-relevant headline metric and an honest 'coverage vs accuracy-when-answered' curve; this frames humans-in-control as a measured property, not a slogan.

Cost-per-correct Pareto on device with a component ablation: because inference is local, tokens and seconds are the currency; a pre-registered ablation grid (few-shots, schema pruning, repair rounds, zero-row retry, fact-check regeneration, claims, thinking) with paired significance shows which components buy accuracy per 1k tokens, the analysis Kapoor et al. and Cost-of-Pass advocate and which distinguishes research from prompt-tweaking.

A small but complete, reproducible artefact: RescueGrid-QA (seeds + verified paraphrases + tiers + unanswerables), frozen snapshots with hashes, scoring code, results keyed by prompt/model/config hashes, a benchmark card; the credibility comes from completeness and honesty (single annotator, synthetic events, one model family stated up front), not from size.

What would make it look like prompt-tweaking: a single-run accuracy on 20 questions that include the few-shot examples; 'we added rules to the prompt and it went from 60% to 80%'; a self-judged faithfulness score; no CIs, no ablation, no error taxonomy, no cost axis; results that cannot be regenerated because the prompt/model/config were not hashed.
open_questions: Root cause of the observed temperature-0 nondeterminism on this endpoint: batch composition from co-tenant requests, FP8 numerics, or prefix-cache state (the 4,176-token block should make cache hits impossible for our 2.8k prompt, which points to batching/numerics)? A quiet-window K=5 run with the box idle, and ideally one with prefix caching disabled, would settle it; both need team access to the server flags.

Who provides the second annotator for gold-set and error-taxonomy agreement (a teammate blind-checking ~20 seeds and ~20 failure labels)? Without it the benchmark has a single-annotator caveat that must be stated.

Which primary metric is pre-registered for the ablation grid: EX_strict (text-to-Cypher purity) or RS_10 (operational reliability)? Recommend RS_10 as primary and EX_strict as secondary, but this is a framing decision Kenil should make before running the grid.

Does a second small text-to-Cypher model (e.g., Neo4j's Gemma-3-4B text2cypher fine-tune) fit in the ~19 GB free alongside Nemotron and the vision model, and is a model-swap ablation acceptable to the team? Without it, all claims are single-model-family.

How large should the final gold set be? ~140 answerable + ~24 unanswerable gives ±7.5 pp CIs and ~80-question paired power for 15 pp effects; going to 300 halves the CI but costs another day of authoring and 2x box time per variant.

Will Shresth's shared schema diverge from the private one before the post-demo research phase? The benchmark should stay pinned to the private snapshot; if the shared schema wins, gold Cypher must be re-authored.

Should highlight.id and suggestion fields be scored (HighlightAcc, suggestion-requires-approval always true) as part of Correct, or reported only as secondary UI metrics? Recommend including HighlightAcc in Correct because the camera fly-to is user-visible.

Thinking-mode cells: what max_tokens and timeout budget are acceptable (reasoning traces can be thousands of tokens at ~45 tok/s), and should they be run at all given AbstentionBench's finding that reasoning worsens abstention?

Whether to compute a RAGAS-style judged faithfulness at all offline: the only judge available is the same Nemotron (self-preference risk) or the Qwen3-VL-8B already resident; either needs the 80-item human calibration before its numbers are reported.

options.name: A. Verified query library + tiny router (the cheap cousin)
