options.description: Grow the 7 pre-baked templates into a ~25-30 template library that covers every benchmark category (status, provenance, temporal, proximity, route, aggregation, conflict, units, paraphrase), route questions with a 22M-parameter sentence embedder (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 kNN/logistic head) plus the existing EntityResolver for slot filling, and let the 30B handle only the long tail. Every 30B-generated query that executes and is approved gets appended to the library (question embedding -> verified Cypher), so the library grows during use (Neo4j's 'application logging' pattern). Add a dynamic few-shot retriever (top-k similar library pairs) to the 30B prompt for the long tail.
options.how_it_applies_here: Schema is fixed and tiny (20 entities, 6 labels, 10 rel types), the 60-question benchmark has only ~10 intent families, and the regex router already exists (rescuegrid/qa/fallback.py). KG2Cypher (June 2026) shows a BERT-base class router at 99.66% is what makes a production Text2Cypher system reliable; Neo4j's Feb-2026 guide says high-complexity/frequent queries must be dedicated tools, not free generation. The route/reachability template is already the only correct implementation of blocked/conflicted-road logic.
options.expected_token_effect: ~0 LLM tokens for routed questions (today ~3,600 prompt + ~215 completion per LLM question); long tail keeps the 30B but can drop from 11 static few-shots to 3 retrieved ones (~2,765 -> ~1,200 prompt tokens).
options.expected_latency_effect: Routed: ~0.05-0.2 s (embedding + Cypher) vs ~5.5 s; long tail unchanged (~5.5 s) or slightly better with the shorter prompt.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Routed questions are exact by construction (verified Cypher); the risk moves to router precision. On the ~2/3 of benchmark questions that map to a template family, expect exec_acc near 100% vs the reported ~1/3 LLM failure rate; abstention on unanswerables becomes a router decision with a similarity threshold.
options.effort: 4-6 hours for library + router + threshold tuning; +2 h to wire the 'cache verified 30B queries' loop. Safe to ship before the demo.
options.risks: Router false positives (wrong template with a confident score) are worse than an honest refusal: needs a similarity threshold and the benchmark's paraphrase/unanswerable sets to tune it. Templates must be reviewed for the same reversed-direction/over-filter bugs. Does not look like 'research' on its own unless benchmarked as an ablation arm against B/C.

evidence.claim: KG2Cypher (June 2026): prompt-only gpt-oss-120B produced executable Cypher (~100% exec) but 0.0-4.2% EM / F1 0.0024-0.0655; a KLUE-BERT-base 11-way domain classifier reached 99.66% and LoRA SFT raised execution-result F1 from 0.806 to 0.950 (broadcast) and 0.70 to 0.92 (company).

Neo4j Text2Cypher guide (Feb 9, 2026): high-complexity or frequent queries should use dedicated pre-written parameterised tools; dynamic few-shot retrieval via vector similarity with a threshold; deterministic validators (regex/CyVer) over LLM validation; mine successful past queries to grow the example pool.
all-MiniLM-L6-v2 is a 22.7M-parameter sentence encoder (384-d) intended for similarity/clustering, runnable offline on CPU.

CYGNET (June 2026): a pre-execution regex/AST/EXPLAIN/mirror-execute gate validates Cypher at 5.6 ms median and an LLM corrector repairs 81-95% of structurally broken queries; the existing guard in text2cypher.py is the regex tier of this design.

options.name: B. LoRA-distilled small dense student for Cypher (Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B first; 0.5B/3B as ablations), grounded synthetic data, served merged on a third ZRT service
options.description: Generate schema-grounded training pairs the CYQUARK/KG2Cypher way: enumerate tree patterns over the fixed schema (label, relationship, property, time-window, aggregation slots) -> deterministic Cypher -> deterministic proto-question -> 30B paraphrases 3 variants per pair (thinking off, ~40 tokens each) -> execute every query on the private 7687 graph and keep only executable, non-empty, semantically-checked pairs (30B as logical-meaning judge). LoRA (r=16, all linear) on Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct in BF16 with plain PEFT (no Unsloth, no bitsandbytes), 2-3 epochs, then merge_and_unload and serve as a plain model via `zrt serve hf:<merged> --label cypher --gpu-memory-fraction ~0.08`. The student replaces only call A (Cypher); the 30B keeps call B (compose) and the fact-check stays. Swap is one env var (LLM_BASE_URL/LLM_MODEL per call).
options.how_it_applies_here: Fine-tuned small models close most of the gap to frontier models on Text2Cypher (CYQUARK-4B 76.2 vs Claude Opus 4.7 78.6 average; even 0.8B reaches 73.3), and prompt-only generation is exactly where the current pipeline fails (invented properties, direction, over-filtering). A student needs no schema or few-shots in the prompt, so the 2,765-token prefix that the hybrid engine cannot cache disappears, and a dense model gets 16-token-block prefix caching for whatever short prompt remains. Verified today on this box: PEFT LoRA runs on GB10 (torch 2.11.0+cu130, peft 0.21.0, transformers 5.12.1): 0.5B model, 1,692 train tok/s, 9.8 GB peak, adapter saved in 38 s total.
options.expected_token_effect: Call A prompt ~2,765 -> ~150-300 tokens (question + $now + optional 1-line schema hint); completion ~120 -> ~80-100 (no fences, less repair). Per-question total ~3,600 -> ~1,100-1,300 prompt tokens (call B unchanged). Repair rounds should fall (fewer syntax/property errors).
options.expected_latency_effect: Honest estimate, not measured: GB10 is 273 GB/s so decode is bandwidth-bound; a 1.5B BF16 model reads ~3.1 GB/token vs ~3.5 GB for the 30B-A3B FP8 active experts, so decode speed is only ~1.5-2x better (roughly 60-90 tok/s vs 45). Call A ~3.0 s -> ~1.2-1.8 s; end-to-end ~5.5 s -> ~3.5-4 s. A 0.5B or FP8-quantised student is needed for <1 s; a 3B/4B BF16 student decodes no faster than today.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Literature: small models go from <20-38% zero-shot to 70-85% execution accuracy after fine-tuning on grounded data (CypherBench <10B models <20% EX; CYQUARK-4B 85.4 on CypherBench; SynthCypher 7-8B 15-31% -> 67-71%; Qwen2.5-3B + GRPO 85% on unseen schemas). On a single fixed schema with in-distribution paraphrases, expect exec_acc on the 51 gold questions well above the current ~2/3, but the benchmark paraphrases must be held out of the training paraphrases to make that number honest.
options.effort: ~1 day window: 6-8 h of focused work with high variance (data 2-3 h, train 0.5-1 h, eval 0.5 h, serving 1-2 h with a FlashInfer JIT risk) - stretch goal only, never on the demo path. ~1 week: 2-3 days for a solid version with 3 model sizes and a data-size curve.
options.risks: (1) Serving: a new BF16 dense model may trigger FlashInfer JIT for an uncached kernel variant (cache holds only the bf16-q/e4m3-kv prefill variant, gemm_sm120, fused_moe_120); launch with MAX_JOBS=2 (memory note: 22 parallel nvcc jobs OOM-killed earlier launches) or pass --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 / a non-FlashInfer attention backend. (2) Memory: ~16 GB available; 1.5B training fits (~8-10 GB with grad checkpointing), 3B is borderline, 4B+ needs the vision service stopped or 4-bit (bitsandbytes 0.50.2 ships an aarch64 wheel with GB10 4-bit heuristics, but unverified on this box). Train and serve sequentially, not concurrently. (3) Data quality: the 30B as a naive Cypher writer produced 0/3 executable queries in the probe (unqualified `status` variables) and hit a 300-token cap in 2/3 batches; CYQUARK shows LLM-written data scores far below grounded generation (42.6 vs 64.6; 26.3 vs 78.5) - so the generator must be pattern-based with the LLM only paraphrasing. (4) Adding a model is a team decision (memory budget shared with vision/ASR). (5) Latency gain is modest for >=3B students on this bandwidth.

evidence.claim: CYQUARK (June 12, 2026): zero-shot Qwen3.5-4B averages 37.94 across MindTheQuery/Text2GQL-Bench/CypherBench/Zograscope, Qwen3.6-27B 60.67; fine-tuned CYQUARK-4B 76.21 and CYQUARK-0.8B 73.30 vs Claude Opus 4.7 78.58 and GPT-5.5 78.52; filtering adds up to 6 points; GPT-5.5-prompted training data scored 42.64 vs 64.58 (MP) and 26.33 vs 78.47 (Zograscope); training was 1 epoch, batch 16, lr 5e-6 on one A100.
CypherBench (Dec 2024): zero-shot EX for <10B open models is <20% (llama3.1-8b 18.82, gemma2-9b 18.61, llama3.2-3b 11.20); qwen2.5-72b 41.87; gpt-4o 60.18; claude-3.5-sonnet 61.58.

options.name: C. Constrained semantic parsing: the student emits {template_id, params} instead of free Cypher (A + B combined)
options.description: Same data generation and LoRA recipe as B, but the training target is a short JSON (template id from the library in A plus slot values such as entity, minutes, source, status), decoded with vLLM json_schema (xgrammar) so the output is always valid. The library expands to Cypher; anything outside the library returns an explicit 'unsupported' class that falls through to the 30B free-Cypher path. Ablation arm: same student trained on free Cypher (B) vs template+params (C).
options.how_it_applies_here: Read-only, humans-in-control and 'never invent' are hard requirements: with C the only Cypher that ever runs is the reviewed library, so the guard, the zero-row repair loop and most fact-check failures disappear for routed questions. Output is ~20 tokens, which is where the latency actually is on a bandwidth-bound GB10.
options.expected_token_effect: Prompt ~150-250 tokens, completion ~20-30 tokens (vs ~2,765 + ~120 today) for the Cypher step; ~0 repair calls.
options.expected_latency_effect: Cypher step ~3.0 s -> ~0.3-0.6 s with a 0.5-1.5B student; end-to-end dominated by the 30B compose call (~2.5 s) unless compose is also templated for library answers (then ~0.5 s total).
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Bounded by template coverage: exact on covered intents (execution is by construction correct), honest 'unsupported' otherwise. Expected to beat B on exec_acc and grounding for the benchmark's ~9 answerable categories; loses on genuinely novel compositional questions, which is why the 30B fallback stays.
options.effort: +3-4 h on top of A and B's data pipeline (label each grounded pair with its template id, JSON schema, tiny expansion layer). Feasible in the 1-week window; in the 1-day window only if A is done and B's training loop is already running.
options.risks: Coverage ceiling and the temptation to keep adding templates; slot extraction errors (wrong entity) must go through the resolver's ambiguity refusal; requires the benchmark to include held-out compositional questions so the trade-off is measured, not hidden.

evidence.claim: Structured outputs via xgrammar (json_schema with maxLength, regex, EBNF) are confirmed working on the resident vLLM 0.26 endpoint (task context; engine.py already uses json_schema for AnswerDraft).

Grammar/schema-aware filtering of Cypher candidates improved execution success by up to +22.9 pp (Gemma-2-9b) but only as a post-generation filter and at the cost of more empty predictions - constrained decoding at generation time is the unexplored variant.
KG2Cypher: class-conditioned prompting with a 99.66% domain classifier plus a LoRA generator reached 95.2% EM / 99.9% execution / 0.964 execution-result F1 on 11 classes.

options.name: D. Assist the 30B without training: schema pruning + retrieved few-shots + schema-aware EBNF constrained decoding
options.description: Keep Nemotron for Cypher but (1) shrink the static prompt (only the schema lines relevant to the predicted intent family, 3 retrieved few-shots instead of 11), (2) constrain decoding with an xgrammar EBNF grammar whose terminals are exactly the schema's labels, relationship types, property names and status values (so invented properties and write clauses cannot be emitted), (3) keep the guard as a second line. Also try to get prefix caching back by padding the shared system prefix to >= 4,176 tokens (one hybrid block) - cheap to test, because the engine caches only whole blocks.
options.how_it_applies_here: Directly attacks the measured 0% prefix-cache hit and the ~2,765-token recomputation, and the dominant error class (invented property names) without adding a model; needs no memory. Works today with the resident engine and is a clean ablation arm for the paper.
options.expected_token_effect: Prompt ~2,765 -> ~600-1,200 tokens (schema-filtering literature: ~80% cut at p95, 921 -> 344 median); completion unchanged (~120). If the >=4,176-token padded-prefix trick works, billed prompt tokens stay high but prefill compute drops (~0.5 s).
options.expected_latency_effect: Prefill ~0.5 s -> ~0.1-0.2 s; decode unchanged (~2.7 s for 120 tokens at 45 tok/s); grammar-constrained decoding adds a small per-token mask cost. Net ~0.3-0.4 s per Cypher call, plus fewer repair rounds (each ~3 s).
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Literature: shorter schemas helped 7-8B models (+~2% exec) and cost larger models ~2%; grammar/schema constraints improved execution success by 20+ pp when used as filters; expect the biggest win on the 'invented property' failure class, none on logic errors (reversed direction, over-filtering).
options.effort: 3-5 h (grammar authoring from schema/schema.cypher is mechanical; retrieval reuses A's embedder). Demo-safe if behind a flag.
options.risks: EBNF for full Cypher is large; a restricted sub-grammar (MATCH/OPTIONAL MATCH/WITH/WHERE/RETURN/ORDER/LIMIT, no CALL) may reject valid queries the model wants; xgrammar compile time for a big grammar; per-request disable_any_whitespace is not honoured on this server.

evidence.claim: Schema filtering (May 2025): pruned schema cut p95 prompt tokens from 2,697 to 529 and median from 921 to 344; Llama-3.1-8B gained ~2% exec accuracy with shorter prompts, Qwen2.5-7B and Gemini-1.5-Flash lost ~2%.

vLLM sets the attention block size to the Mamba page size for hybrid models (528 tokens for Qwen3.5; 4,176 on this Nemotron engine per the task context); prefix caching keeps only fully completed blocks, so a prompt shorter than one block gets a 0% hit (issue #40696, Apr 2026, unresolved).

Adaptive test-time inference for Text2Cypher (Sept 2, 2026): trace budgeting + selective execution-guided refinement cut generation budget 30.7% and wall-clock 21-25% with 0.2-0.5% execution-success loss (Gemma-2-9B, Qwen-2.5-7B).

options.name: E. NO-GO variants: LoRA on the 30B itself; Mamba/GDN-hybrid students (Nemotron-3-Nano-4B, Qwen3.5-0.8B/2B/4B); Unsloth/GRPO in the 1-day window
options.description: (i) Training a LoRA for NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B: PEFT needs BF16 weights (~60 GB) that do not fit in the ~16 GB free, the resident checkpoint is FP8 (not PEFT-trainable), and attaching an adapter requires restarting the shared 'llm' service with --enable-lora (vLLM 0.26 does declare LoRA support for NemotronH). (ii) Nemotron-3-Nano-4B (3.97B, Mamba-2 hybrid, 4 attention layers, Mar 2026) and Qwen3.5 small models (Gated DeltaNet hybrid, Mar 2026) are the strongest small bases on paper, but HF training needs mamba_ssm/causal_conv1d or flash-linear-attention kernels that are absent from the box's venv and would have to be built for sm_121a/aarch64. (iii) Unsloth: NVIDIA's Spark playbook uses the NGC PyTorch container (hp2 is not in the docker group), community reports need transformers pinned to 5.5.0 (5.12.1 installed) and three aarch64 patches (issue #4867, open). (iv) GRPO (TRL 1.13) needs a rollout engine plus policy in memory - not with 16 GB free.
options.how_it_applies_here: Only relevant as a 1-week item: Qwen3.5-0.8B/4B are exactly what CYQUARK fine-tuned (73-76 avg), so if the Unsloth container route is unblocked (sudo/docker), they become the best students; Nemotron-3-Nano-4B would be the on-brand HP/NVIDIA story but is the riskiest to train here.
options.expected_token_effect: Same as B if it worked.
options.expected_latency_effect: Hybrid students decode faster per byte than dense at long context but bring back the large-block prefix-caching problem (528-token blocks for Qwen3.5) that the dense student avoids.
options.expected_accuracy_effect: Potentially +3-5 points over Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B judged by CYQUARK's 0.8B/4B numbers; unverified on this schema.
options.effort: 1 day: no-go. 1 week: 1-2 days if docker/sudo is granted for the NGC container; otherwise skip.
options.risks: Kernel builds on sm_121a/aarch64, transformers version pins that conflict with the vLLM venv, docker access, and the shared-service restart for (i).

recommendations: 1-DAY WINDOW (demo within ~1 day): GO on Option A (verified query library + MiniLM router + growing cache of execution-verified 30B queries) and Option D's cheap parts (3 retrieved few-shots instead of 11, schema lines per intent family, and a 10-minute test of padding the shared prefix to >= 4,176 tokens to recover prefix caching). CONDITIONAL GO on Option B only as a post-demo stretch that never sits on the demo path: Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct, BF16 PEFT LoRA r=16 (the smoke test proves the stack), ~1-2k grounded pairs, merge the adapter and serve as a plain model on a third ZRT label with MAX_JOBS=2 and the 30B path kept as the env-var fallback. NO-GO in this window on Nemotron-3-Nano-4B / Qwen3.5 hybrids, Unsloth, GRPO, and any LoRA on the 30B.

Before touching anything: run `scripts/snapshot_state.sh` on a new tag and run `bench/run_bench.py --label baseline --mode llm` and `--mode auto` against 7687 so the baseline numbers (exec_acc, grounded, abstain, tokens, latency p50/p95, repairs) are frozen in bench/results and in the tag; every experiment becomes a new label + tag, so 'come back to where we are now' is `scripts/restore_state.sh <tag>` plus `git checkout`.

Freeze bench/questions.json (or a split of it) as a held-out set NOW, before generating training paraphrases; never let the 30B see the benchmark questions when paraphrasing, and de-duplicate training questions against the benchmark by embedding similarity (>0.9) to keep exec_acc honest.

Build the data generator pattern-first, not LLM-first: enumerate (label, relationship, property, filter, time-window, aggregation) tree patterns over the fixed schema -> deterministic Cypher (reuse the 7 template families + fallback.py logic) -> deterministic proto-question -> 30B paraphrase x3 with thinking off and ~60 max_tokens (~1 s each; ~35 min for 2k) -> execute on 7687, keep executable+non-empty (plus a share of legitimately-empty negatives), 30B as logical-meaning judge; log the reject rate. The probe showed LLM-written Cypher is unreliable (0/3 executable) and CYQUARK shows it trains worse.

Train in this order and size: 0.5B (sanity, 10 min), 1.5B (main), 3B only with gradient checkpointing and batch 1-2 while the vision service is up; use plain PEFT + SDPA, lr 2e-4, r=16, 2-3 epochs, seed fixed, save adapter + merged weights + the exact data file hash and config under a versioned `distill/` directory outside the demo path. Do not run training and the new serving instance concurrently in ~16 GB.

Serving choice: merge the LoRA (peft merge_and_unload) and serve the merged BF16 model on its own ZRT label with --max-model-len 4096 and a small --gpu-memory-fraction (~0.08); if FlashInfer starts JIT-compiling, pass --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 (matches the cached prefill variant) or switch attention backend; only use --enable-lora/--lora-modules if the team wants hot-swappable adapters (proxy routing by adapter name is unverified).

Keep call B (answer composition) on the 30B for now; a small student for prose composition is a grounding risk. For library-routed questions use templated composition (the deterministic `_rows_summary` path already exists) so those answers need zero LLM tokens.

1-WEEK WINDOW: turn this into the research artefact: (1) baseline 30B few-shot; (2) 30B + retrieval + schema pruning; (3) 30B + schema-aware EBNF constrained decoding; (4) students 0.5B/1.5B/3B LoRA on grounded data; (5) the same student on 30B self-instruct data (reproduces CYQUARK's finding on an operational graph); (6) template+params student (Option C) vs free-Cypher student; (7) a data-size curve (250/500/1k/2k/4k pairs) - the literature has no number for 'how few pairs suffice for one fixed schema', so this curve is itself a contribution. If docker/sudo becomes available, add Qwen3.5-0.8B/4B via the NGC + Unsloth route as the strongest-base arm.

Report tokens honestly: the win from the student is prompt tokens (~3,600 -> ~1,200 per question) and repair rounds; the decode-latency win on a 273 GB/s box is only large for <=1.5B or FP8 students, so publish per-call latency by model size rather than a single speedup number.

scores.option: EVAL-1. Statistical protocol: K repeats, seed-clustered SEs, Wilson CIs, pass^K, paired McNemar vs baseline (L4 O6)
scores.reasoning: This is the single thing that separates research from prompt-tweaking here. Measured facts make it mandatory: T=0 is non-deterministic on this endpoint (two lenses independently observed different greedy outputs), n=60 gives a Wilson half-width of about +/-11 pp at p=0.7, and the existing baseline files are single runs. Paired design rescues power (12 fixed / 2 broken is already p=0.013). Costs ~2 h of code and box time only. A hiring manager reading 'correct 0.63 -> 0.78 [paired McNemar p=0.01, K=3]' believes it; '0.63 -> 0.78' alone is noise.
unsupported_claims: Patodiya arXiv 2609.04748 (prefix caching -> 36-75% divergence) is after my knowledge cutoff and I could not verify it; treat as unverified until fetched
The claim that bench/results is empty (L1, L4) is wrong: two single-run baseline files exist at c3108e3

scores.option: EVAL-2. Multi-snapshot execution accuracy (test-suite accuracy adapted to replayed graph states) (L4 O3)
scores.reasoning: The most defensible novel angle in the whole dossier, and nearly free: no LLM calls, just re-executing each predicted Cypher on 4-6 replayed snapshots and taking the min. It directly targets the over-filtering failure visible in the baseline JSON (tm06 filtered on `>= $now`, cf01 added a spurious 5-minute window) which a single snapshot cannot distinguish from correct queries. Zhong et al. 2020 is solid prior art for SQL; the adaptation to a time-versioned LPG with an audit trail is a real gap. The EX_strict - EX_multi gap is an honest headline number.
unsupported_claims: 'No current Cypher benchmark scores queries across multiple graph states' is an unverified absence claim; phrase it as 'to our knowledge' in the write-up

scores.option: EVAL-3. Fixed error taxonomy + pre-registered ablation grid (L4 O9)
scores.reasoning: Turns 'we changed the prompt' into 'component X accounts for Y pp at Z tokens'. Every grid cell maps to an existing switch (max_repairs, zero-row retry, fact-check regeneration, few-shot count, enable_thinking). Crucially, my read of the baseline JSON shows the dominant failure classes are NOT the ones the dossier assumes (see missing facts): the taxonomy must be built from the data, not from CypherBench's list. Pre-registration of the primary metric before running the grid is what makes the result survive a skeptical reviewer.
unsupported_claims: The dossier's assumption that 'invented property names / reversed direction' dominate is not what the baseline shows: guard_rejections = 0 in both runs; the observed failures are projection omissions, entity linking, time-window semantics and fact-check misses on the deterministic route renderer

scores.option: EVAL-4. Gold set upgrade: seen/unseen split, phrasing tiers, verified paraphrases, ~24 categorised unanswerables (L4 O1 + O8)
scores.reasoning: Necessary for credibility: the current 60-question set has 1 verbatim overlap with the 11 few-shots ('Can Ambulance 2 still reach the hospital?' = rt01) plus several near-paraphrases, only 6 unanswerables, and the 6 'paraphrase' items are all absorbed by the regex router in auto mode. Jackal's tier gap (86.0% long-NL vs 35.7% short-NL, verified) is exactly the radio-speak regime an EOC officer uses. Single-annotator gold is the stated weakness; a teammate blind-check of 20 seeds is cheap insurance.
unsupported_claims: KG2Cypher, PIPE-Cypher and CYGNET (June 2026) are after my cutoff and their numbers are unverified by me
'Expect the honest baseline on unseen seeds to land well below two-thirds' is a projection, not a measurement

scores.option: EVAL-5. Three-level execution accuracy: EX_strict (CypherBench multiset semantics) + EX_key + evidence-set Jaccard (L4 O2)
scores.reasoning: The current score_exec defaults to set equality on ['id'] for 39/60 questions, so a query returning the right ids with wrong status/source columns scores 1.0 and the compose step then propagates the wrong column. Porting CypherBench's ~100-line comparator is 2-3 h and makes the headline number comparable to published Cypher work. EvJ gives graded partial credit for error analysis. Reviewers will ask for this.

scores.option: EVAL-6. Abstention as a first-class metric: explicit answerable flag, abstention recall / false-refusal, TrustSQL-style RS_c (L4 O5)
scores.reasoning: The abstain metric today is ABSTAIN_RX over answer text and was edited in commit 6d30e04 after the baseline ran, which is fragile. With 'humans stay in control' as a product contract, a penalty-scored reliability metric is the right headline for an operational domain and prevents O-grammar/O-best-of-N filters from hiding coverage loss (Ozsoy: empties 1 -> 24 -> 36, verified). Cheap (~2 h + more unanswerable items).
unsupported_claims: AbstentionBench's 'reasoning worsens abstention' has not been checked for Nemotron; run the thinking on/off cell before citing it as applicable

scores.option: EVAL-7. Cost accounting + reproducibility artefacts: per-call ledger with cached_tokens, prompt/config hashes, tokens-per-correct Pareto, benchmark card and short report (L4 O7 + O10)
scores.reasoning: Mostly exists (CALLS ledger, git sha, snapshot scripts) but two gaps matter for rigor: results lack a prompt hash and server-config fingerprint, and the committed baseline results were produced at c3108e3 while 6d30e04 changed engine fact-check, abstain regex and questions.json, so HEAD cannot reproduce the frozen numbers. Kapoor et al.'s accuracy-vs-cost Pareto is the correct frame for a token-efficiency thesis and exposes best-of-N and repair rounds honestly.
unsupported_claims: cached_tokens will stay null until the team relaunches with --enable-prompt-tokens-details; do not report a cache-hit metric before then

scores.option: EVAL-8. Structured claims in the compose schema, deterministic ClaimPrecision, calibrated local judge as secondary (L4 O4)
scores.reasoning: Methodologically attractive (grounding as a deterministic metric, not a self-judged score) but it adds 40-90 completion tokens per answer on a box where each completion token costs ~22 ms, i.e. +1-2 s, which contradicts the token-efficiency goal, and more required JSON fields risk degenerate constrained outputs. The deterministic renderer (SYS-2) achieves grounded-by-construction for row-shaped answers at zero extra tokens. Keep as an ablation arm for the LLM-compose path only; the 80-item judge calibration is worth doing once.
unsupported_claims: 'Answer quality may rise because the model must name the row' is speculation for this model

scores.option: SYS-1. Projection macro + short few-shots: model emits MATCH/WHERE only, engine hydrates the canonical provenance projection (L3 opt 2; L2 'projection hydration')
scores.reasoning: Best evidence-to-effort ratio in the dossier and it targets what the baseline actually shows: 3 of 6 temporal failures (tm02, tm04, tm07) and cf01/rt05 are must_mention misses where the LLM's RETURN omitted the entity id/name, so the compose step could not say it. Measured: RETURN..LIMIT is 50% of few-shot Cypher tokens and the model copies that shape; on a decode-bound box (45 tok/s vs 5.5k tok/s prefill) halving completion tokens is worth ~1.2 s. Guarantees the columns the renderer and fact-check need. As research it is an 'output-token-first' ablation with a clean mechanism story. Needs an explicit-RETURN escape for computed values (danger score, people).
unsupported_claims: Latency numbers were probed under co-tenant load (decode 16-34 tok/s); re-measure idle

scores.option: SYS-2. Skip or shrink call B: deterministic row renderer / answer template with slots bound to RETURN aliases, LLM compose only for novel shapes (L1 O6, L3 opt 1, L2 (g) part)
scores.reasoning: Largest single latency lever (call B is ~2.5 s of ~6 s plus a 2.5 s regeneration when the fact-check fails) and grounding becomes 1.0 by construction on the rendered path. The 'query + answer-template in one call' variant is a defensible small contribution: prior art templates the query (TeCoD, parameterised text2SQL), not the verbalisation. Risk is stilted prose in the demo and nested collect() rows; measure fluency loss honestly rather than hide it.
unsupported_claims: TeCoD and the AWS parameterized-templates post are cited as evidence, but both are about query templates; there is no cited literature support for the answer-template claim, it rests on the measured decode arithmetic only

'Grounded rate -> 1.0 by construction' holds only if the template check rejects literals outside slots; the baseline shows the deterministic route renderer itself failed the regex fact-check (rt01, rt04 grounded=False), so renderers must be benchmarked too

scores.option: SYS-3. Template-first routing upgrade: 20-30 parameterised templates, LLM json_schema slot filling or embedding/NLI matcher, explicit 'other' class (L1 O5, L2 (f)/(g) tiers, L5 A, L3 opt 7 skeleton cache)
scores.reasoning: High demo value and the core TeCoD claim is verified (up to 36% higher EX than ICL, 2.2x lower latency on matched queries); a 168-token router probe worked on this endpoint. But as research it is engineering unless reported as a coverage-vs-risk (selective prediction) curve on the paraphrase tier, and the baseline warns that templates are not automatically correct: the route category scored 0.4 in auto mode with the template path. Nemotron's BFCL 53.2 argues for json_schema slots over native tool calls. The self-extending skeleton cache (L3 opt 7) belongs inside this option with exact-match-only hits and no answer caching.
unsupported_claims: 'Matched ~60% -> ~90%' and 'BIRD 38-48% -> 86-92%' for TeCoD are not in the abstract I could verify; only the 'up to 36%' and '2.2x' headline claims are confirmed
KG2Cypher 99.66% router figure is unverified (post-cutoff)
'Expect 70-85% of the benchmark routed' is a guess; today auto mode routes 17/60

scores.option: SYS-4. Execution-grounded best-of-N: n=3-4 sampling in one request, guard/grammar filter, execute all, select by result agreement + non-empty preference + mean logprob (L1 O3, L3 opt 9)
scores.reasoning: Evidence is solid and verified (Ozsoy 2605.10318: 77.6 -> 85.4% with confidence selection on Gemma-2-9B, 789 test questions; gains from 3 samples in 2503.24364), execution of 4 candidates on a 30-node graph is free, and the measured cost is 1.5x wall for n=4 (9.5 s vs 6.1 s). A selection-signal ablation (agreement vs logprob vs validator vs non-empty) on a hybrid Mamba MoE is a small but real study. It conflicts with the token headline (3-4x completion tokens) so it must be reported on the tokens-per-correct Pareto, and correlated errors (all 5 candidates chose NEAR over ASSIGNED_TO) bound the gain.
unsupported_claims: n>1 combined with json_schema/EBNF on vLLM 0.26 is unverified
Logprob confidence is a weak selective-prediction signal (AUROC ~0.675 in 2607.06799, unverified post-cutoff paper); do not rely on it alone

scores.option: SYS-5. Compact schema + dynamic kNN few-shot retrieval (k=3) from an execution-validated question bank (L1 O4, L3 opt 4, L5 A/D parts)
scores.reasoning: Strongest literature lever for small models on a fixed schema (DAIL-SQL masked-question selection; ZOGRASCOPE 97% iid with dynamic ICL; Neo4j schema filtering helps 7-8B models), and it cuts prompt tokens ~2,765 -> ~1,200. The rigor threat is leakage: the bench already overlaps the 11 few-shots, and a bank generated by the same model that is evaluated will encode its own phrasing. Requires a frozen held-out split BEFORE bank generation and a compositional split to be honest (ZOGRASCOPE drops to 71-75% compositional). A probe showed a 273-token schema without few-shots produced invalid Cypher, so examples are load-bearing. Conflicts with prefix caching; report the trade-off.
unsupported_claims: PIPE-Cypher and ZOGRASCOPE figures are post-cutoff/unverified by me
'Expect invented-property errors to drop' is not what the baseline needs fixing; expect gains on projection shape and time-window idioms instead

scores.option: SYS-6. Schema-specialised grammar-constrained Cypher decoding (EBNF/GBNF via xgrammar) (L1 O2, L2 (g) grammar arm, L3 opt 5, L5 D part)
scores.reasoning: Three lenses pitch this as the headline novelty; the data says it is an ablation arm. (a) The baseline has guard_rejections = 0 and its failures are semantic (projection omissions, entity linking, time windows, pattern choice), which grammars cannot fix (CYGNET-style validators score 0% on sibling swaps). (b) L2's own probes: constrained outputs were grammatical but semantically wrong in 3/3, including an unbound variable. (c) Ozsoy (verified) shows filtering raises empties 1 -> 24 -> 36, and 2608.25761 shows an incomplete grammar costs EX. (d) Novelty is partial: Huawei's schema-constrained GQL grammar (CEUR 2024) and PICARD are close prior art. Honest expected outcome: validity up, EX flat, coverage down. Worth one grid dimension because a documented coercion failure mode is a publishable negative; not worth being the thesis.
unsupported_claims: 'Structural error classes -> ~0' and GraphRAFT's +5.4 Hit@1 are cited as expected gains, but GraphRAFT needed fine-tuning and this baseline has no structural rejections to remove
'Combining EBNF with n>1 in vLLM 0.26' unverified

scores.option: SYS-7. Gated, cheaper execution-feedback repair: deterministic validator/direction corrector, structured error vocabulary, logprob-gated budgeting (L1 O7, L3 opt 8)
scores.reasoning: The baseline spent 19 repair rounds on 59 LLM questions (~3 s and ~2.9k tokens each, ~1 s average per question) and p95 latency is 14.25 s, so repair budgeting is a measurable lever; Ozsoy's adaptive budgeting (21-25% wall, -0.2-0.5% EX) is the right template. A schema-aware direction corrector is ~0 ms. But logprob gating is weak (the 1-token classifier probe mislabelled a plain status question) and repair mis-fixes are ~9%. Solid engineering, modest novelty.
unsupported_claims: Multi-Agent GraphRAG and RAMPART/CYGNET numbers are post-cutoff and unverified; they also come from frontier or 7B+ models, not a 3B-active hybrid
Deterministic direction flipping is unsafe for CONNECTS_TO (undirected by convention)

scores.option: SYS-8. Prefix-caching relaunch (--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 16, or bf16 KV / prefix padding) (L1 O1, L3 opt 3, L2 (b) part, L5 D part)
scores.reasoning: Verified locally: enable_prefix_caching=False on the running engine (hybrid models are opt-in in 0.26.0), --prefix-match-unit exists, NemotronH declares SupportsMambaPrefixCaching, and PR #46384 is merged (2026-07-12). Zero accuracy risk, but the gain is ~0.5-0.7 s of ~6 s because prefill is cheap; the PR's own benchmark shows only 0.13 -> 0.10 s TTFT at 10k tokens. For research rigor it is a mild negative unless K-repeats exist, since prefix caching is reported to increase nondeterminism. The 4,176-token block diagnosis (fp32 SSM page / fp8 KV per-token bytes) is a nice reproducible systems note. Needs a team relaunch; unverified on NemotronH FP8 on sm_121a.
unsupported_claims: 'Computed prefill drops from ~3,600 to ~900 tokens' is plausible but unmeasured on this model; PR #46384 was demonstrated only on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8
bf16-KV block of 2,096/2,176 is arithmetic from config.json, not observed

Unsloth's ~60 GB for Nemotron 3 Nano LoRA and the 60-90 tok/s student decode estimate are unverified

scores.reasoning: Cannot express time windows, aggregates, conflicts or routes; only useful as an optional fulltext clause for open-vocabulary transcript fields, which the guard already allowlists (db.index.fulltext.queryNodes). Not a research angle for this project.

scores.reasoning: Needs a server relaunch with a tool parser, multiplies calls 3-4x (10-15 s at ~3 s/call), and Neo4j's own MCP-Cypher evaluation reached only 0.71 with Claude 3.7 Sonnet at 3.6 calls/question; Nemotron's BFCL 53.2 predicts worse. Post-demo it is at most a reference row.

scores.reasoning: The schema fits in 815 tokens (380 compact); 'Death of Schema Linking' shows linking costs 2.7-4.8 EX when the schema fits; decomposition means 4-8 sequential calls at 45 tok/s. Negative on every axis the project cares about.

top_plan: Step 0 (today, ~3 h, no server change): re-baseline at HEAD. The committed results (baseline-*-c3108e3.json) predate commit 6d30e04, which changed engine.py fact-check, the abstain regex and questions.json, so they are not reproducible from HEAD. Add to run_bench: K=3 repeats, mean +/- seed-clustered SE, Wilson 95% CI, pass^3, paired McNemar vs a named baseline file, EX_strict (CypherBench multiset semantics) beside EX_key, EvJ, per-call ledger role (cypher/repair_k/zero_row/compose/compose_retry), prompt hash of SCHEMA_TEXT+ANSWER_SYSTEM, and the vllm-llm.json fingerprint. Mark rt01 and other few-shot overlaps as 'seen'. Run --mode llm and --mode auto on an idle box, commit results, tag baseline-v1, run scripts/snapshot_state.sh baseline-v1. Freeze this question set as held-out before generating any few-shot bank or paraphrases.

Step 1 (pre-demo, ~1 day, each behind a flag = one ablation cell): output-token-first changes that match the observed failure signature. (a) Projection macro + hydration: model emits MATCH/WHERE/WITH/ORDER/LIMIT, engine appends the canonical provenance projection (fixes the entity-name omissions behind tm02/tm04/tm07/cf01/rt05 and halves completion tokens). (b) Deterministic renderer / answer-template for row-shaped results, LLM compose only for novel shapes, with the template checked for literals outside slots (removes ~2.5 s and makes grounding 1.0 by construction). The actual failure signature contradicts the dossier's 'invented property / reversed direction' framing: of the temporal/route/conflict failures, most are must_mention misses because the generated RETURN omitted the entity id/name (tm02, tm04, tm07, cf01, rt05), one is a time-filter semantic error (tm06 used >= $now), one is entity linking (rt03 used the display name as the id), one is a 'versus' comparison ignored (cf03), and two are template-path route answers that failed the regex fact-check (rt01, rt04 grounded=False on the deterministic renderer, possibly fixed by 6d30e04, unverified). 39 of 60 questions use the default compare mode (set equality on ['id']); the remaining use rowcount / contains_any / value, so the current exec_acc mixes four semantics; EX_strict must be declared per question.

Add prompt hash, questions/snapshot sha256 and the server fingerprint (/opt/hp/zrt/run/vllm-llm.json, vllm 0.26.0, block 4176, enable_prefix_caching=False) to run_bench results; add a 'role' field to the calls ledger and a 'seen' flag on the 11 few-shot/7-template questions; audit the template-tier disagreements (rt01, rt04, rt05, un02, pp01, tm07) and the missed abstention na02, fix gold/compare or the template; re-run --mode auto and --mode llm at K=3 with the box quiet; commit + tag baseline-v1 and snapshot_state.sh.

Step 1 (pre-demo, ~1 day, all behind env flags with baseline defaults): demo-safe tier 2. Grow the parameterised template library from 7 to ~13-15 intents covering the failing categories (temporal 'between'/'since HH:MM', proximity within N m, list-all-reports provenance, people-in-status aggregation, assignment), matched by an LLM json_schema slot router with enumerated vocabularies, explicit 'other' and a confidence gate; render routed answers deterministically (no call B); one regression test per template. Adopt only if paired bench shows correct_rate up and abstain_rate/false-route not worse.

Step 2 (pre-demo, ~0.5 day): bound the LLM tail. Deterministic pre-execution gate (label/property/relationship-direction check + EXPLAIN in a read transaction) before execution; cap to 1 repair + 1 zero-row retry; hard per-question deadline (~8 s) that falls back to the honest 'no matching records' renderer; skip call B when rows match a known shape. Re-run bench; target p95 < 8 s with no drop in abstain_rate.

Step 3 (demo run-book): script the demo questions so every scripted one is answered by tier 1/2, rehearse each 3x and record pass^3; keep the Nemotron server untouched until after the demo (no relaunch, no prefix caching, no KV dtype change, no speculative decoding); show 'querying graph' state for unscripted audience questions on the LLM path.

Step 4 (post-demo research core, on the frozen benchmark v1 at K=3): add multi-snapshot EX_strict, explicit abstain fields + RS_10, three-level EX; then the pre-registered ablation grid: schema-compiled grammar (off / generic / typed) x best-of-N selection signals x compact schema + kNN few-shots (bank generated from templates, leakage-checked) x projection macro, plus the whole-graph-in-context and template-only reference rows. Ask the team for one relaunch with --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 16 --enable-prompt-tokens-details, verify prefix_cache_hits_total > 0 and 60-prompt output equality before using it in any reported run. Every experiment = git tag + results JSON + server config.

Step 5 (stretch, only if ~10 GB can be reserved and the team agrees): Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B student LoRA on pattern-grounded, execution-verified synthetic pairs with a data-size curve (250/500/1k/2k) and a free-Cypher vs template+params variant, evaluated on the held-out compositional split; never on the demo path.
reject: Speculative decoding (ngram/suffix/EAGLE3/MTP): PR #56531 confirms silent token corruption on Nemotron-3-Nano (12/60) and is still open; no MTP head in the FP8 checkpoint; silent wrong Cypher is the worst demo failure.

Server relaunch of any kind before the demo (prefix caching, bf16 KV, tool parser): <=0.7 s upside, shared with the vision/ASR teammates, experimental Mamba caching, and it changes reproducibility/nondeterminism.
GraphRAG/LightRAG/HybridRAG/HippoRAG/ToG: the typed graph already exists; indices go stale in seconds and cannot express as-of, conflict or provenance semantics.
Vector RAG as a primary path: cannot do time windows, aggregates, conflicts or routes; keep at most a fulltext clause inside a Cypher template.
Agentic ReAct tool loop: needs a relaunch with a tool-call parser, 10-15 s per question, and the cited 0.71 result used Claude 3.7 Sonnet, not a 3.5B-active model.
Whole-graph-in-context as a product path: hallucinated an entity in the probe, no rows/provenance, exceeds 32k context at 100-500 events; keep as one benchmark row only.
DIN-SQL/MAC-SQL/CHESS decomposition and schema linking: schema fits in 380-815 tokens; linking hurts when it fits; +10-20 s of sequential calls.
LoRA on the 30B Nemotron, hybrid students (Nano-4B, Qwen3.5), Unsloth, GRPO: ~60 GB needed vs ~16 GB free, FP8 base untrainable, missing kernels/container, shared-service restart.
LLMLingua-2 / Selective Context: deletes schema identifiers; prefill ceiling is ~0.35 s; at most one negative ablation row.
Logprob-gated routing/abstention on the critical path: probe mislabelled a plain status question, signals are uncalibrated and weak (AUROC ~0.68).
Auto-promoting executed LLM queries into the template cache without human approval: ~1 in 4 executed baseline queries is wrong (exec_acc 0.745), so this poisons the safety tier.

Rewriting the 11 few-shots (projection macro), schema-compiled grammar, best-of-N sampling and structured claims BEFORE the demo: each changes model output shape or adds decode tokens/variance a day before a live run; all are good post-demo ablations.
missing: The 'demo-safe' template tier is itself failing benchmark questions (tm07 mis-routes 'between 14:00 and 14:01' to the last-5-minutes template with a 'No time window given' preamble; rt01/rt04 route answers score exec=None; un02, pp01, rt05 score wrong) and auto-mode abstain_rate is 0.833 vs 1.0 in llm mode; no researcher proposed auditing gold/compare for template answers or a per-template regression test before using the bench to rank options.

No option enforces a wall-clock budget: baseline p95 is 14.25 s in llm mode because 12/60 questions chained 3-5 calls (p50 11.8 s) and all of the slowest were still wrong; a hard per-question deadline with graceful fallback to the honest renderer is the single most watch-officer-relevant fix and nobody named it.

Co-tenancy during the demo: every live probe ran with the vision/ASR services sharing the GPU and decode fell to 16-40 tok/s; no one proposed limiting concurrent QA calls, pre-warming, or measuring the QA path under realistic co-load rather than idle.

A demo run-book: deciding which scripted questions go through tier 1/2 vs the LLM path, rehearsing each 3x (pass^3), and a visible 'querying' state for unscripted questions; none of the five lenses treated the demo as a rehearsable artefact.

Feature-flag discipline for recoverability: every new tier/behaviour behind an env flag with baseline defaults, so 'go back to now' is git checkout + flags off rather than a code revert; only partly implied by one lens.
Free memory is ~15-16 GB (free -g), not the 19 GB in the task context; any added model must be sized against the smaller figure and the FlashInfer JIT spike.

Freshness under mutation was not tested by any option: replaying the same question at two scenario clocks (and after an event that flips a status) should be a bench check, since 'facts change every second' is a stated requirement.

draft.decision: Keep LLM+KG via text-to-Cypher as the core, but move the model out of the prose: a three-tier, grounded-by-construction answer layer where the LLM emits structure (typed slots for a parameterised template library, or Cypher plus a slot-bound answer template) and code renders every sentence from Neo4j rows, so the second "compose" call disappears on most questions and grounding is 1.0 by construction. Tier 1 = existing regex router, Tier 2 = new json_schema slot router over ~13 templates with an explicit 'other' class and confidence gate, Tier 3 = the existing text-to-Cypher tail with compact schema, k=3 dynamic few-shots, static schema check, a 1-repair budget and a hard deadline. The research artefact is the benchmark around it (K-repeat paired stats, multi-snapshot execution accuracy, penalty-scored abstention, tokens-per-correct) plus pre-registered ablations of best-of-N selection and schema-compiled grammar decoding on the tail.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: LLM-only: serialise the whole graph into the prompt and answer without Cypher
why_not_alternatives.reason: Measured 7.6-8.9k prompt tokens today (2x the baseline) and 15-60k at 100-500 events against max-model-len 32,768; the local probe got the aggregation wrong and invented an entity (20 people / Building 7 vs gold 120 / Building-14); there are no rows, so provenance, highlight ids and the fact-check cannot exist. Kept as one reference row in the benchmark only.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Vector RAG over event text / transcripts
why_not_alternatives.reason: Similarity retrieval cannot express 'last N minutes', sums, routes over blocked/conflicted roads or as-of semantics; an old transcript can outrank the current node status. The one useful form (fulltext clause inside Cypher) is already allowlisted via db.index.fulltext.queryNodes and needs no new architecture.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: GraphRAG family (Microsoft GraphRAG, LightRAG, HippoRAG, Think-on-Graph)
why_not_alternatives.reason: These construct and index a graph from unstructured text; RescueGrid already has a typed, provenance-tagged property graph and an executed Cypher is exact and fresh. Community summaries go stale within seconds on a live graph; GraphRAG-Bench and the RAG-vs-GraphRAG study show graphs help multi-hop over large corpora, not fact lookups (arXiv 2502.11371, 2506.05690).

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Agentic ReAct / MCP tool loop
why_not_alternatives.reason: Needs a relaunch with --enable-auto-tool-choice and a tool parser (tool calling 400s today), multiplies calls 3-4x at ~3 s each (10-15 s per question, unbounded worst case), and Neo4j's own MCP-Cypher agent scored 0.71 with 3.6 calls/question using Claude 3.7 Sonnet; Nemotron Nano's BFCL v4 is 53.2.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: DIN-SQL / MAC-SQL / CHESS-style decomposition and schema linking
why_not_alternatives.reason: The schema fits in 815 tokens (380 compact), where 'The Death of Schema Linking' shows linking costs 2.7-4.8 EX points; decomposition is 4-8 sequential calls at 45 tok/s (+10-20 s per question on this box).

why_not_alternatives.alternative: LoRA on the 30B Nemotron itself, or Mamba/GDN-hybrid students (Nemotron-3-Nano-4B, Qwen3.5) via Unsloth/GRPO
why_not_alternatives.reason: 16-bit LoRA of Nemotron 3 Nano needs ~60 GB (Unsloth docs) vs 12-14 GB free; the resident checkpoint is FP8; serving an adapter needs a restart of the shared service; hybrid students need mamba_ssm/fla kernels absent for sm_121a/aarch64 and a docker/NGC route not available to this user.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Speculative decoding now (ngram / suffix / EAGLE3 / MTP)
why_not_alternatives.reason: The FP8 Nano checkpoint has no MTP head and no public EAGLE3 draft; ngram on hybrid recurrent models has open silent-corruption PRs (#56531/#55504: Nemotron 12/60 correct before the fix) and was already reverted on this box. Post-demo only as a documented negative result with a greedy-equality test.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Learned prompt compression (LLMLingua-2 / Selective Context)
why_not_alternatives.reason: Prefill of the whole 2.8k prompt costs ~0.5 s of a ~5 s question, so the ceiling is ~0.35 s, and the compressors delete exactly the low-frequency schema identifiers Cypher must copy verbatim. At most one negative ablation row.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Schema-compiled grammar-constrained decoding as the headline thesis
why_not_alternatives.reason: The baseline has 0 guard rejections and its failures are semantic (value lookups, time-window idioms, projection omissions); three independent probes on this endpoint produced grammatical-but-wrong Cypher (reversed NEAR, unbound variable, 'collectentity.id' coercion), and filtering raises empty predictions (Ozsoy 2026: 1 -> 24 -> 36). Kept as one pre-registered ablation dimension, not the system.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Adding Neo4j's text-to-cypher-Gemma-3-4B as a resident specialist
why_not_alternatives.reason: ~8 GB BF16 plus KV barely fits the 12-14 GB free next to Nemotron (47.5 GB) and Qwen3-VL (26.8 GB), the model card publishes no accuracy numbers, and a fourth model is a team decision. A 0.5-1.5B student trained on our own schema is the better use of the same memory, post-demo.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Relaunching the shared 'llm' server before the demo (prefix caching, bf16 KV, tool parser)
why_not_alternatives.reason: Upper bound ~0.5-0.7 s per LLM question (prefill is cheap; decode dominates), Mamba prefix caching is logged experimental in vLLM 0.26, PR #46384 lists 'shared system prompt followed by divergent user content' as a limitation, and it interrupts the vision/ASR teammates. Post-demo bundle only, verified by vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total > 0.

metrics.name: Correct
metrics.definition: Per question: for answerable items EX_strict AND Grounded AND Facts AND HighlightAcc; for unanswerable items a correct abstention. Reported as mean over K=3 runs with Wilson 95% CI and seed-clustered SE; deltas vs baseline-v1 as paired exact McNemar p on majority-of-K outcomes.

metrics.name: EX_strict
metrics.definition: 1 iff multiset(rows_pred) == multiset(rows_gold) up to column permutation (ordered comparison when the gold Cypher contains ORDER BY; floats rounded to 3 dp, datetimes ISO, nested lists sorted, empty==empty scores 1), CypherBench semantics. EX_key (today's set equality on declared key columns) is kept as the lenient secondary.

metrics.name: EX_multi
metrics.definition: min over S=4-6 replayed graph snapshots of EX_strict when the same predicted Cypher is re-executed on each snapshot with that snapshot's replay clock as $now; the gap EX_strict - EX_multi measures queries that are right on one snapshot only (over-filtering).

metrics.name: EvJ
metrics.definition: Jaccard of entity-id sets: |ids_pred ∩ ids_gold| / |ids_pred ∪ ids_gold| over all entity ids appearing anywhere in the returned rows (partial credit for right entities, wrong columns).

metrics.name: Grounded
metrics.definition: 1 iff fact_check(answer, rows) returns no problem: every source / time / confidence / percentage mentioned in the answer co-occurs in one row or nested record; on the deterministic-render path this is 1 by construction and is still computed.

metrics.name: Facts
metrics.definition: 1 iff every must_mention string appears (case-insensitive) and no must_not_mention string appears in the answer.

metrics.name: HighlightAcc
metrics.definition: 1 iff highlight.id equals the gold subject id (or one of the accepted ids) for the question; user-visible because it drives the camera fly-to.

metrics.name: AbstentionRecall / FalseRefusal
metrics.definition: AbstentionRecall = correct abstentions / unanswerable questions (detected from an explicit answerable=false field once added, regex ABSTAIN_RX until then); FalseRefusal = abstentions on answerable questions / answerable questions.

metrics.name: RS_c (reliability score)
metrics.definition: TrustSQL-style: mean over all questions of +1 for a correct answer or a correct abstention, 0 for abstaining on an answerable question, -c for a wrong answer or for answering an unanswerable question; reported at c in {0, 10, N}; RS_10 is the pre-registered primary metric for the ablation grid.

metrics.name: pass^3 and ConsistencyRate
metrics.definition: pass^3 = fraction of questions correct in all 3 repeats (reliability under serving nondeterminism); ConsistencyRate = fraction of paraphrase groups whose members all get the same Correct outcome.

metrics.name: Tokens per question (by call role)
metrics.definition: prompt_tokens and completion_tokens per question, split by call role (cypher, repair_k, zero_row_retry, compose, compose_retry, router) from the CALLS ledger; cached_tokens reported once the server exposes prompt_tokens_details (null until --enable-prompt-tokens-details); computed prefill = prompt - cached.

metrics.name: Latency
metrics.definition: wall p50 / p95 per question, LLM-seconds per question (sum of call durations), calls per LLM question, and the vLLM concurrent-request count at run time (co-tenant load); LLM-seconds and tokens are primary, wall-clock secondary.

metrics.name: TokensPerCorrect / SecondsPerCorrect
metrics.definition: mean total tokens per question / Correct rate, and mean wall seconds / Correct rate (Cost-of-Pass with tokens as the currency, since inference is local); every variant is plotted on an RS_10-vs-tokens Pareto chart.

metrics.name: Router metrics (Tier 1+2)
metrics.definition: coverage = fraction of questions routed; false-route rate = routed questions whose template answer is not Correct; reported as a coverage-vs-risk curve across the confidence-gate threshold on the paraphrase/short-NL tier.

metrics.name: Error taxonomy histogram
metrics.definition: Each failed question (majority-of-K) gets one primary code: value_lookup_miss, time_window_semantics, projection_omission, entity_linking, over_filtering, wrong_pattern, wrong_aggregation, reversed_direction, invented_property, guard_rejection, syntax_error, compose_ungrounded, highlight_wrong, timeout; 20 labels double-checked by a teammate with agreement reported.

roadmap.step: S0. Freeze baseline-v1: add per-call role, server fingerprint (vllm-llm.json, vLLM version, SCHEMA_TEXT/ANSWER_SYSTEM sha256, questions.json + snapshot sha256, concurrent-load marker) and K=3 repeats with Wilson CI, pass^3 and paired McNemar to bench/run_bench.py; flag the 11 few-shot / 7 template questions as seen; run --mode llm and --mode auto at K=3 on an idle box; scripts/snapshot_state.sh baseline-v1
roadmap.hypothesis: The committed single-run numbers are not reproducible from HEAD (scoring changed between c3108e3 and 6d30e04, correct 0.633 -> 0.733 on identical code paths) and T=0 is non-deterministic on this endpoint, so no option can be ranked without repeats and pairing
roadmap.expected_gain: A defensible baseline table: expect correct ~0.70-0.75 [95% CI about +/-11 pp at n=60], pass^3 10-20 pp below the mean, ~4.4k prompt + ~220 completion tokens and ~5 s p50 per LLM question
roadmap.effort: ~3 h code + ~45 min box time (60 questions x 2 modes x K=3 at ~7 min per llm pass)
roadmap.how_to_measure: bench/results/baseline-v1-{llm,auto}-5556dbc-k{1,2,3}.json with the fingerprint block; scripts/restore_state.sh baseline-v1 must reproduce the mean within the CI

roadmap.step: S1. Sweep the six existing feature flags as bench cells (compact_schema, dyn_fewshot k=3, fewshot_v2, entity_link, schema_check, router_v2) and adopt the winners as the new default QA_FEATURES
roadmap.hypothesis: compact_schema+dyn_fewshot cuts call-A prompt tokens from 2,818 to ~1,300 (measured prompt sizes: 2,710 -> 1,301; 1,152 with fewshot_v2) without lowering Correct, and entity_link+schema_check cut repairs (18/59) and the entity-linking/value-lookup failures (st07, tm03, un02, px04)
roadmap.expected_gain: Prompt tokens per LLM question ~4,400 -> ~2,300; repairs 18 -> <10; Correct +5 to +10 pp on temporal/units/status (unverified until measured)
roadmap.effort: ~1 h wiring + ~50 min box time per cell at K=3 (run compact+dyn+entity+schema first, singles after)
roadmap.how_to_measure: Paired McNemar vs baseline-v1 per cell; accept a flag only if Correct is not worse (p>0.05 on the losing side) and abstain stays 6/6

roadmap.step: S2. Repair budgeting and a hard deadline: max_repairs 2 -> 1 (keep the zero-row retry), a schema_check-driven structured error message, and an 8 s per-question deadline that falls back to the honest 'no matching records' or the pre-baked renderer
roadmap.hypothesis: The second repair round rarely rescues a question (tm05: 5 calls, 14.4 s, still wrong; px05: 3 calls, error) so removing it cuts p95 without cutting Correct; adaptive budgeting literature reports 21-25% wall-clock savings for 0.2-0.5% loss (arXiv 2609.02324)
roadmap.expected_gain: p95 11.6 s -> <8 s; ~2.9k tokens saved per avoided round; Correct unchanged within CI
roadmap.how_to_measure: latency_p95_s, repairs, tokens per question, paired Correct; count of deadline hits logged as a warning

roadmap.step: S3. Skip call B: deterministic renderer for known row shapes (single-entity status rows, Event lists, routes, aggregation rows with people/count columns) built on QAEngine._rows_summary and the fallback builders; LLM json_schema compose only for shapes the renderer does not recognise, with 'Keep answer under 60 words' always on
roadmap.hypothesis: Call B costs 842 prompt + 84 completion tokens and 2.13 s (49 of 59 LLM questions) and is where ungrounded numbers enter (tm02, tm05, px05 grounded=False); rendering from rows removes it on >=60% of LLM questions and makes Grounded 1.0 on that path
roadmap.expected_gain: -2.1 s p50 and -900 tokens on rendered questions (LLM question p50 ~5.1 s -> ~3 s); grounded_rate 0.944 -> ~1.0; Facts unchanged or up (entity name always rendered)
roadmap.effort: ~4-5 h including a template check that no literal outside a row cell can appear in the rendered text
roadmap.how_to_measure: Grounded, Facts, tokens by call role (compose calls per question should drop to <0.4), latency p50; the renderer path is benchmarked exactly like the LLM path, with a per-shape unit test in tests/test_qa_fallback.py

roadmap.step: S4. Tier 2: LLM slot router (json_schema with enumerated intents, sources, unit/hazard types, explicit 'other', confidence >= 0.6 gate, 3 few-shot examples in a ~250-token prompt) feeding the template library grown from 7 to ~13 intents (value_lookup, event_detail/first-event, time_range_events, status_since 'how long', confirmed_since, within_radius, near_unit, staged_at, blocked_roads_with_buildings, people_in_status), rendered deterministically; one regression test per template
roadmap.hypothesis: EOC questions are recurrent shapes; the categories the LLM path fails (temporal 0.14, proximity 0.67) are exactly the ones a parameterised query expresses deterministically, and TeCoD reports up to 36% higher execution accuracy and 2.2x lower latency on matched queries (arXiv 2604.28028)
roadmap.expected_gain: Routed questions ~250 prompt + ~30 completion tokens and ~1 s; router coverage >= 50% of the non-regex tail with false-route rate < 5%; temporal category 0.14 -> >= 0.7; overall Correct >= 0.85 (unverified until measured)
roadmap.effort: ~5-6 h (router prompt + schema 1 h, six templates 3 h, tests 1-2 h); ship whatever subset is green by demo time, the rest lands post-demo
roadmap.how_to_measure: Router coverage and false-route rate on all 60 questions plus the paraphrase tier; paired Correct vs S3; per-template regression tests in tests/test_qa_fallback.py

roadmap.step: S5. Demo freeze: tag demo-v1 with the winning QA_FEATURES, run mode=auto, rehearse each scripted question 3x and record pass^3; no server relaunch, no temperature > 0, and keep the fusion agent's own LLM calls off the QA critical path during the live demo
roadmap.hypothesis: Under co-tenant load decode drops to 16-34 tok/s (probes on 2026-09-25), so scripted questions must be Tier 1/2 and the tail must have the 8 s deadline
roadmap.expected_gain: Every scripted question answers in < 2 s with pass^3 = 1.0; unscripted questions bounded at 8 s
roadmap.how_to_measure: bench --only <scripted ids> at K=3; scripts/restore_state.sh demo-v1 reproduces it

roadmap.step: S6. Evaluation upgrade: EX_strict + EvJ scorer (port CypherBench's ~100-line comparator), explicit answerable/abstain_reason fields in the output contract, RS_c, multi-snapshot EX over 4-6 replayed graph states (ingest.py --reset + event subsets, per-snapshot $now), ~15 more categorised unanswerables, short/radio-speak paraphrase tiers to ~140 questions, error-taxonomy labelling with a second annotator on 20 items
roadmap.hypothesis: Today's exec_acc mixes four compare semantics and scores right-ids-wrong-columns as correct; a single snapshot cannot detect over-filtering (Zhong et al. 2020 report 2.5% average / 8.1% worst-case false negatives for single-database matching); abstention is a regex
roadmap.expected_gain: A benchmark that survives review: EX_strict below EX_key by an honest margin, a measured EX_strict - EX_multi gap, RS_10 as primary metric, CI half-width ~+/-7.5 pp at n=140
roadmap.effort: ~1 day of authoring + ~3 h code; no LLM cost for the snapshot loop
roadmap.how_to_measure: Re-score the frozen baseline-v1 and demo-v1 result files under the new metrics (rows and gold_rows are stored) before running anything new

roadmap.step: S7. Projection macro + short few-shots: the model emits MATCH/OPTIONAL MATCH/WHERE/WITH/ORDER BY/LIMIT and a RETURN marker; code appends the canonical provenance projection per bound variable; explicit RETURN kept for computed values (danger, people, hops)
roadmap.hypothesis: RETURN..LIMIT is 50% of the few-shot Cypher tokens and the model copies that shape (116 completion tokens per call A); on a decode-bound box one completion token costs the wall time of ~120 prompt tokens, and the omitted-id failures (tm04, cf01, rt05) disappear when the projection is canonical
roadmap.expected_gain: Call A completion 116 -> ~65 tokens (-1.1 s per call), prompt -700 tokens from shorter examples; Facts up on temporal/conflict
roadmap.effort: ~0.5 day (rewrite the few-shot bank in the short form, hydration code, tests)
roadmap.how_to_measure: completion tokens per call A, paired Correct, error-taxonomy shift for projection_omission

roadmap.step: S8. One-call query + slot-bound answer template: call A returns Cypher plus a template whose slots reference RETURN aliases ('{name} is {status} since {status_since} ({source}, {confidence})'); the engine validates every slot against the returned columns, fills them from rows, and rejects templates containing sources/times/numbers outside slots
roadmap.hypothesis: Grounding can be enforced at the interface instead of checked after the fact: prior art templates the query (TeCoD, parameterised text2SQL) but not the verbalisation, so this is the defensible systems contribution; it extends S3's deterministic rendering to novel row shapes without a second call
roadmap.expected_gain: Compose call removed on ~100% of LLM questions (-2.1 s, -900 tokens), Grounded 1.0 by construction, +30-50 completion tokens on call A; fluency loss to be measured, not hidden
roadmap.effort: ~1 day (template mini-grammar, slot validator, per-row and aggregate phrasing, 15 unit tests)
roadmap.how_to_measure: Ablation compose {LLM, deterministic, slot-template}: Grounded, Facts, tokens, latency, and a 20-answer blind fluency rating by a teammate

roadmap.step: S9. Execution-grounded best-of-4 on the tail: n=4 in one request at T=0.7 (verified: n>1 works with json_schema and EBNF on this endpoint), guard + schema_check filter, execute all candidates (milliseconds on a 30-node graph), select by result-set agreement, non-empty preference and mean token logprob
roadmap.hypothesis: Greedy decoding is already non-deterministic here, so sampling + a measured selection criterion replaces luck; confidence-based selection lifted Gemma-2-9B from 77.6% to 85.4% execution success (arXiv 2605.10318) and gains appear from 3 samples (arXiv 2503.24364); n=4 measured at 1.5x wall time on this box
roadmap.expected_gain: Tail exec_acc +5 to +10 pp at ~3.5x call-A completion tokens; reported on the tokens-per-correct Pareto, not as a free win; cannot fix unanimous semantic misreads (NEAR vs ASSIGNED_TO)
roadmap.how_to_measure: Selection-signal ablation (agreement / logprob / non-empty / validator) on EX_strict, RS_10, tokens and latency

roadmap.step: S10. Schema-compiled EBNF grammar for read-only Cypher via xgrammar structured_outputs.grammar (labels, directed relationship endpoints, per-label properties, enumerated status/source values, per-pattern variable binding, every construct in the gold set), with a coverage test that all 51 gold queries parse
roadmap.hypothesis: Grammar removes structural error classes but not pattern choice; honest expected outcome is validity up, EX flat-to-slightly-up, coverage down (empties rise), which is itself a publishable result on a 3B-active hybrid model
roadmap.expected_gain: guard/schema rejections -> 0, repairs down; EX_strict change within +/-5 pp; empties measured
roadmap.how_to_measure: 2x2 grid {few-shots static/kNN} x {grammar off/typed} plus schema_check on/off; report EX_strict, coverage, RS_10, tokens

roadmap.step: S11. Ask the team for one relaunch bundle of the shared 'llm' label: --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 16 --enable-prompt-tokens-details (optionally --kv-cache-dtype auto to halve the 4,176-token block); test a warm-up request ending exactly at the shared prefix boundary
roadmap.hypothesis: Prefix caching is simply off (enable_prefix_caching=False; hybrid models are opt-in in vLLM 0.26) and the flags exist in the installed build (PR #46384 merged 2026-07-12), but the PR's own limitation for shared-prefix-then-divergent workloads means a hit is not guaranteed
roadmap.expected_gain: -0.4 to -0.7 s per LLM question (prefill of ~2.8k tokens), cached_tokens finally reported; zero accuracy change but possibly more output variance (must be measured with K=3)
roadmap.effort: ~2 h plus a ~4 min server restart; revert if vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total stays 0
roadmap.how_to_measure: prefix_cache_hits_total > 0, usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, latency and pass^3 before/after on identical questions

roadmap.step: S12. Stretch (only with team OK for a third ZRT label and while the vision model can be idle): pattern-first synthetic data generator (schema tree patterns -> deterministic Cypher -> 30B paraphrase x3 -> execute and filter, de-duplicated against the benchmark), LoRA r=16 BF16 on Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B then 1.5B (PEFT smoke test already runs at 1,692 tok/s, 9.8 GB peak), merged and served with --gpu-memory-fraction ~0.08; data-size curve 250/500/1k/2k pairs; free-Cypher vs template_id+params student
roadmap.hypothesis: Fine-tuned small models close most of the gap to frontier models on Text2Cypher (CYQUARK, arXiv 2606.14325) and nobody has published how few verified pairs one fixed schema needs; the token win is the schema prompt (~2.8k -> ~300)
roadmap.expected_gain: Call A prompt ~300 tokens; tail exec_acc on the held-out compositional split reported as a curve; decode speedup only ~1.5-2x for a 1.5B model on a 273 GB/s device
roadmap.how_to_measure: Same benchmark, model-swap cell; data-size curve on EX_strict and RS_10; report FlashInfer JIT and memory

ablations: A0. Reference rows: baseline-v1 llm-only vs auto (regex router + llm) vs router-only (templates, no LLM tail) vs whole-graph-in-context LLM-only (no Cypher) - answers the 'LLM vs LLM+KG vs templates' question with numbers

A1. Prompt: {pinned 2,710-token prompt, compact_schema, dyn_fewshot k=3, compact+dyn, compact+fewshot_v2+dyn (1,152 tokens)} on Correct, EX_strict, tokens; leakage-controlled (few-shot bank never contains a benchmark question)
A2. Validation/repair: schema_check {off,on} x max_repairs {0,1,2} x zero-row retry {off,on} on repairs, p95, tokens, Correct

A3. Compose: {LLM json_schema compose, LLM compose + 60-word cap, deterministic renderer, slot-bound answer template} on Grounded, Facts, completion tokens, latency, plus a 20-answer blind fluency rating
A4. Routing tier: Tier 2 slot router {off, on} x confidence gate {0.5, 0.6, 0.8} reported as coverage vs false-route curve on the paraphrase/short-NL tier
A5. Decoding: n=1 greedy vs best-of-4 with selection signal {result agreement, mean logprob, non-empty preference, validator pass, combined} on EX_strict, RS_10, tokens-per-correct
A6. Grammar: {none, schema-compiled typed EBNF} x {few-shots static, kNN} with coverage (empty predictions) and structural-vs-semantic error split
A7. Thinking: enable_thinking {off, on with max_tokens 2048} on the tail only, reporting AbstentionRecall (reasoning is reported to worsen abstention) and latency
A8. Serving: prefix caching {off, on (align, prefix-match-unit 16)} on latency, cached_tokens and pass^3 at K=3 - a systems note, not an accuracy claim
A9. Negative rows kept for honesty: LLMLingua-2 prompt compression on call A; ngram speculative decoding greedy-equality test on 60 prompts (expected corruption per vLLM PR #56531)
A10. Stretch: student model {none, Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B LoRA, 1.5B LoRA} x training data {pattern-grounded, 30B self-instruct} x data size {250, 500, 1k, 2k} on the held-out compositional split

Statistics for every cell: K=3, mean +/- seed-clustered SE, Wilson 95% CI, pass^3, paired exact McNemar vs baseline-v1 on majority-of-K outcomes; RS_10 pre-registered as primary, EX_strict secondary; every results file carries git sha, prompt hash, questions/snapshot sha256, server fingerprint and concurrent-load marker
draft.resume_framing: Built RescueGrid-QA, a provenance- and time-first text-to-Cypher benchmark and answer layer for an offline disaster-response command post running a 30B-A3B hybrid Mamba/MoE model (FP8, vLLM 0.26) on an NVIDIA GB10 edge box: (1) a measured cost model showing decode dominates (45 tok/s vs 5.5k tok/s prefill, one output token ~ 120 prompt tokens of latency) that motivated an output-token-first design; (2) grounded-by-construction verbalisation - the model emits typed slots or Cypher plus a slot-bound answer template and code renders every sentence from graph rows - removing the second LLM call on most questions and making provenance grounding 1.0 by construction; (3) a three-tier router/template/text-to-Cypher architecture reported as a coverage-vs-risk curve with penalty-scored abstention (TrustSQL-style RS_10) so 'humans stay in control' is a measured property; (4) multi-snapshot execution accuracy (test-suite accuracy adapted to a time-versioned property graph with an audit trail) that exposes queries correct on one graph state only; (5) pre-registered ablations of prompt layout, repair budgeting, best-of-N execution-grounded selection and schema-compiled grammar decoding under K-repeat, paired statistics that quantify FP8/serving nondeterminism; with reproducible, hash-fingerprinted, snapshot-restorable experiment state. Framed honestly as 'a benchmark, a cost model and a grounding-by-construction result on edge hardware', never as 'prompt tuning raised accuracy from X to Y'.
risks: Single-run baseline numbers are already stale and non-reproducible (scoring changed between c3108e3 and 6d30e04; T=0 outputs differ between identical calls); mitigation: S0 re-baseline at HEAD with K=3 and pairing before any change is adopted

Co-tenant load during the demo (vision, ASR, fusion agent) halves decode speed (16-34 tok/s measured vs ~45 idle); mitigation: scripted questions on Tier 1/2, 8 s deadline on the tail, record concurrent-load in every results file

A confidently wrong template answer is worse than an honest refusal; mitigation: Tier 2 requires confidence >= 0.6 and an explicit 'other' class, one regression test per template, false-route rate reported on the paraphrase tier, never auto-promote executed LLM queries into the template library without human approval (exec_acc is ~0.8, so ~1 in 5 executed queries is wrong)

Deterministic rendering reads mechanically and the existing renderer itself failed the regex fact-check on route answers in an earlier run; mitigation: renderer outputs are benchmarked like any other path and the LLM compose stays available for novel shapes

Few-shot / benchmark leakage inflates accuracy ('Can Ambulance 2 still reach the hospital?' is verbatim in both; several near-paraphrases); mitigation: seen/unseen flag, freeze the question set before generating any few-shot bank or paraphrases, de-duplicate by similarity
n=60 gives a Wilson CI of about +/-11 pp; unpaired single-run deltas below ~8-11 pp are noise; mitigation: paired McNemar on shared questions, extend to ~140 questions post-demo, pre-register RS_10

Grammar-constrained decoding can push the model into grammatical nonsense when a construct is missing (observed 'collectentity.id' coercion, unbound variables) and raises empty predictions; mitigation: coverage test over all gold queries, keep the regex guard as defence in depth, treat as an ablation not the product path
Best-of-N multiplies completion tokens 3-4x and adds sampling variance; mitigation: post-demo only, reported on tokens-per-correct, temperature 0 remains the production setting

Prefix-caching relaunch may not hit for our shared-prefix-then-question layout on NemotronH FP8 (unverified on sm_121a), may increase output nondeterminism, and interrupts teammates; mitigation: post-demo, verify hits > 0, K=3 before/after, revert if no hit

Memory headroom is 12-14 GB, not 19 GB; any student model must be trained and served sequentially, a BF16 dense model may trigger a FlashInfer JIT (cap MAX_JOBS), and adding a model is a team decision

Shared graph schema drift (Shresth's 7688 instance) would invalidate gold Cypher, templates and the schema check; mitigation: benchmark pinned to the private snapshot, schema_check and templates regenerated from schema/schema.cypher, run_bench and snapshot scripts refuse 7688

Self-judged metrics (Nemotron judging Nemotron) carry self-preference bias; mitigation: headline grounding metric is deterministic; any LLM judge is calibrated on ~80 human labels with kappa reported or not reported at all

Over-claiming novelty; mitigation: cite the closest prior art explicitly (TeCoD, PICARD, Huawei schema-constrained GQL, Ozsoy 2026 filtering, Zhong 2020 test suites) and frame contributions as adaptation + measurement on edge hardware
