red.verdict: Direction is right (LLM+KG via text-to-Cypher, tiers, a benchmark as the research object) and most server-side claims check out on this box: prefix caching is simply off, the 4176 block and fp8 KV are in the log, --prefix-match-unit/--mamba-cache-mode exist in the installed vLLM 0.26.0, disable_any_whitespace is server-level, and n=2 with json_schema and with an EBNF grammar plus logprobs works on the live endpoint (verified with one probe each). But the plan as written should not be approved: (1) the headline research claims rest on a benchmark that is already contaminated and test-tuned: the fewshot_v2 bank contains six bench questions verbatim, schema_check was written against the bench failures, and S4 proposes writing templates for the remaining failing bench questions; there is no dev/test split, so every paired 'gain' is optimistically biased. (2) The all-flags run that already exists at HEAD 8d1c86c contradicts S1's hypothesis (repairs 18->29, calls 2.14->2.42, p50 5.08->5.79 s, +6.7 pp with 8 fixed/4 broken, McNemar p about 0.39), and the S1 acceptance rule ('not worse at p>0.05') is vacuous at n=60. (3) 'Grounded 1.0 by construction' is false for the code S3 proposes to reuse: the existing deterministic renderers already fail the fact-check regex on tm07/rt01/rt04, the scorer flags tm02 ungrounded when the engine does not, and zero-row wrong answers score as grounded. (4) RS_10 as the pre-registered primary metric on a 90%-answerable set rewards refusal over answering (all-abstain beats the baseline), which pulls the ablation grid away from the product goal. (5) The demo-window timeline (S0-S5 about 16-18 h of code plus 4-8 h of K=3 box time, plus unbudgeted gold authoring) is not executable in ~1 day while the developer also builds the fusion agent, and S2/S4 change the live path the day before the demo with an uncalibrated confidence gate and a deadline that returns a false 'no matching records'. Recommended scope for the demo window: freeze baseline-v1 at HEAD with the role/fingerprint ledger and a dev/test split; fix the two real latency bugs (unterminated code fence not stripped; finish_reason=length fed to the guard three times, 21.7 s on px02); ship the deterministic renderer only for shapes the templates already render, keep LLM compose otherwise, and reconcile the renderer with the grounding check; rehearse scripted questions in mode=auto. Move the flag sweep, the Tier-2 router, and all novelty claims to the post-demo week on a held-out question set with corrected metrics (Correct or RS_1 primary, Grounded over answered questions only, seen-flag computed per configuration). Memory headroom is 9 GB free / 11 GB available today, not 12-14, so S12 and any resident specialist model are off the table without stopping the vision service.

attacks.claim: S1/A1: sweep the six existing flags, adopt compact_schema+dyn_fewshot+fewshot_v2 as the new default; A1 is 'leakage-controlled (few-shot bank never contains a benchmark question)'; S0 marks only the 11 pinned few-shots and 7 template questions as 'seen'.
attacks.problem: The fewshot_v2 bank in rescuegrid/qa/fewshot.py contains six bench questions verbatim (rt01, px04, cf01, tm07, un01, st01) plus near-duplicates of tm01/tm02 (token Jaccard 0.75-0.80); with dyn_fewshot the TF-IDF selector puts the identical question at the top of the prompt, so those items become retrieval, not generalisation. Three of the eight questions 'fixed' in the existing all-llm-8d1c86c run (px04, tm07, cf01) are exactly those leaked items. schema_check.py's own docstring says it 'catches the failure classes the benchmark exposed', and S4 proposes templates for the specific failing bench questions (first_event, status_since, confirmed_since = tm04, tm03, tm06). This is test-set-driven development with no dev/test split; every paired delta reported against baseline-v1 is optimistically biased and a reviewer will reject the accuracy story outright.
attacks.fix: Before any further feature work: (a) strip the six verbatim and two near-dup entries from EXAMPLES_V2 (or replace them with entity-swapped variants and mark the originals seen), (b) compute the 'seen' flag per run from the bank actually used (hash of the rendered examples) and store it in the results file, (c) split bench/questions.json into dev (used for flag/template design) and held-out test now, and author the 140-question extension as the test set with nobody looking at per-question failures; report unseen-only Correct as the headline.

attacks.claim: Roadmap S0-S5 fit in the demo window (~1 day): S0 3 h, S1 1 h + 50 min box per cell, S2 2 h, S3 4-5 h, S4 5-6 h, S5 1 h.
attacks.problem: That is 16-18 h of coding plus K=3 box time (about 7 min per llm pass, so about 21 min per cell; the S1 grid alone is 10 cells in bench/ladder.sh = 3.5 h) while the developer is also building the fusion agent, and it omits unbudgeted authoring the metrics require: HighlightAcc needs gold highlight ids for 54 answerable questions (questions.json has no such field), ConsistencyRate needs seed_id/paraphrase_of fields (none exist), and explicit answerable/abstain_reason fields need a contract change. S3 and S4 both touch the live auto path the day before the demo with per-template tests still to be written.
attacks.fix: Cut the demo window to: S0-lite (roles + fingerprint + K=3 on the existing 60 questions, no new gold), the two bug fixes below, S3 restricted to row shapes the fallback already renders (event lists, single-entity status), and S5. Defer S1's sweep, S2's structured errors, and S4's router to the post-demo week; gold highlight ids and seed ids are authored with the 140-question test set.

attacks.claim: S1 hypothesis: entity_link+schema_check cut repairs 18 -> <10 and Correct +5 to +10 pp; compact_schema+dyn_fewshot cut call-A prompt tokens 'without lowering Correct'; acceptance rule: 'accept a flag only if Correct is not worse (p>0.05 on the losing side)'.
attacks.problem: The all-flags run already exists at HEAD (bench/results/all-llm-8d1c86c.json, git 8d1c86c, which the proposal never mentions; it cites 5556dbc as HEAD). Measured vs baseline-llm-6d30e04: repairs 18 -> 29 (+61%), calls/LLM-question 2.14 -> 2.42, completion tokens 221 -> 247, p50 5.08 -> 5.79 s, guard rejections 0 -> 2, three finish=length truncations vs zero; Correct 0.733 -> 0.800 with 8 fixed / 4 broken (exact McNemar p about 0.39) and three of the fixes are leaked questions. Prompt tokens did drop (4,377 -> 2,477). The acceptance criterion is non-inferiority with no margin and no power: at n=60 nothing short of a 10 pp regression is 'significantly worse', so every flag passes by default.
attacks.fix: Report the 8d1c86c run as the first data point and reframe S1's hypothesis (schema_check trades latency for prompt tokens; measure whether the extra rounds rescue anything). Replace the acceptance rule with a pre-specified non-inferiority margin on the paired mean-of-K difference (e.g. lower 90% paired-bootstrap bound > -3 pp) plus 'no category loses more than one question' and 'repairs and p95 not worse'; state explicitly that n=60 cannot certify gains below ~10 pp and reserve significance claims for the held-out 140-question set.

attacks.claim: S3/S8: rendering from rows removes call B and 'makes Grounded 1.0 by construction'; call B 'is where ungrounded numbers enter (tm02, tm05, px05 grounded=False)'.
attacks.problem: Verified against the code and results: (a) the existing deterministic renderers the proposal wants to reuse already fail fact_check: in all-auto-8d1c86c the template answer for tm07 is scored grounded=False because it prints the window boundary '14:01:00Z' and the summary count, and rt01/rt04's route renderer cites road times/confidences absent from its evidence rows (6 problems each); (b) tm02's grounded=False in both cited runs is a scorer artefact: fact_check(answer, evidence) returns [] in the engine (no regeneration fired), but run_bench.py appends Conflict rows, which flips any_source on while the model's Cypher filtered on e.source without projecting it, yielding 'no row has radio_asr with 14:00:32, 0.78' for a fully grounded sentence; (c) px05 is an error case with zero rows (grounded=False comes from the r.mode != 'error' branch), so only tm05 is a genuine call-B hallucination; (d) run_bench scores zero-row wrong answers as grounded=True (st06, st07, pv03, px04 in the baseline), so grounded_rate is inflated and gameable by returning nothing. The regex only checks sources/times/confidences: a template '{name} is collapsed and evacuated' with a literal status outside a slot is invisible to it, so 'grounded by construction' is only as strong as a three-pattern regex.
attacks.fix: Fix the metric before optimising it: score Grounded only over answered questions with rows (report coverage separately), run the same fact_check inputs in engine and bench (evidence only, or evidence+conflicts in both), and make renderers print only values that are row cells (no window boundaries, no counts unless a count column exists). For S8, restrict template text to a closed vocabulary of connectives (or a per-shape phrase library) and reject any token outside slots that matches an entity name, status value, relationship word, number or time; add unit tests that every rendered/template answer passes fact_check on its own rows.

attacks.claim: S2: max_repairs 2 -> 1 plus an 8 s per-question deadline 'that falls back to the honest no matching records or the pre-baked renderer' cuts p95 11.6 -> <8 s; tm05/px05 are cited as evidence the second repair rarely rescues.
attacks.problem: The worst outlier in the latest run (px02, 21.7 s, mode=error) is a parser bug, not a model limit: all three calls hit finish=length at 320 tokens with a degenerate 'position_since AS position_since' loop, extract_cypher's _FENCE regex requires a closing fence so the truncated output kept its leading ```cypher and was rejected by the guard twice ('query must start with MATCH...'), and the truncated query was re-fed as the 'previous query' each round. A deadline hides this instead of fixing it, and the real fix (bounded projection, S7) is deferred post-demo. Worse, returning 'The graph query found no matching records' on a timeout is a false statement (no query ran) and violates the honesty contract; it would also be counted as a correct abstention on unanswerables because ABSTAIN_RX matches that phrase. Whether a client-side deadline actually frees the GPU through the ZRT proxy is unverified (vLLM's with_cancellation aborts on disconnect at its own HTTP layer, but the request goes through the proxy over a UDS), and the OpenAI client is built with max_retries=1 and a 120 s timeout, so hidden retries are neither bounded nor in the token ledger.
attacks.fix: Demo-window fixes in text2cypher.py: strip an unterminated opening fence; treat finish_reason=length as a distinct repair reason ('your query was cut off; return a shorter query with at most N RETURN columns') and never feed a truncated query back as the previous query; set max_retries=0 and a per-call timeout in the client; on a deadline emit a distinct 'timed out before a query could be built' message with abstain_reason=timeout, never 'no matching records'. Verify proxy cancellation once with a deliberately long request and the vLLM log.

attacks.claim: RS_10 is the pre-registered primary metric for the ablation grid; 'humans stay in control' becomes a measured property.
attacks.problem: On this benchmark 54/60 questions are answerable, so RS_10 = (+1 per correct answer or correct abstention, 0 per abstain-on-answerable, -10 per wrong answer)/60 is dominated by -10 x #wrong: the cited baseline scores about (44 - 160)/60 = -1.9, while a system that answers 30 correctly and refuses the other 24 answerable questions scores about +0.6, and all-abstain scores +0.1. Pre-registering RS_10 will select the most refusal-prone variant in every cell, which is the opposite of what a command-post tool and the demo need, and lets the grid 'improve' by abstaining more.
attacks.fix: Pre-register Correct (unseen-only) as primary with RS_c reported at c in {0, 1, 10} and a coverage floor (e.g. FalseRefusal <= 5%), or pick c from the coverage-vs-risk curve after the fact and say so; add a seed-clustered paired test on Correct, and plot RS_1 rather than RS_10 on the Pareto chart.

attacks.claim: Tier 2 slot router: json_schema with enumerated intents, explicit 'other', confidence >= 0.6 gate; routed questions cost ~250 prompt + ~30 completion tokens and ~1 s; false-route rate < 5%; overall Correct >= 0.85 in the demo window.
attacks.problem: The gate is the model's own self-reported JSON 'confidence' field, which is uncalibrated on a 3B-active model (the dossier's own 1-token probe mis-labelled a plain status question); nothing stops a confident wrong template answer, which the proposal itself calls worse than an honest refusal. The latency model ignores the miss path: every non-regex question now pays the router call before the tail, and the measured router probe was 72 completion tokens / 3.74 s under load, i.e. +1.5-4 s on the tail p50, not '~1 s'. The temporal claim (0.14 -> >= 0.7) is largely already delivered by the regex router in auto mode (all-auto: tm01/tm02/pp05 routed correctly, temporal 0.43), and the residual three (tm03, tm04, tm06) would be fixed by writing templates for those exact test questions.
attacks.fix: Post-demo only. Gate on something measurable: enumerated guided_choice for the intent with the intent token's logprob, plus deterministic slot validation (entity resolves, source in vocabulary, window parses) and agreement with a cheap regex/BM25 prior; report coverage vs false-route on held-out paraphrases, and measure tail p50 with the router in the path. Design the template inventory from the EOC question taxonomy on the dev split, never from failing test items.

attacks.claim: A0 reference rows: 'baseline-v1 llm-only vs auto vs router-only vs whole-graph' answers the LLM vs LLM+KG vs templates question with numbers.
attacks.problem: mode='llm' is not LLM-only: QAEngine._llm_answer(allow_fallback=True) substitutes the pre-baked template whenever the LLM query errors or returns zero rows. In baseline-llm-6d30e04 four questions were answered as 'llm+fallback' (rt01, rt04, rt05, cf04) and one as 'fallback' (the regex mutation refusal); rt01 and rt04 also have no gold_cypher, so exec_acc=None is treated as correct by run_bench ('exec_acc in (True, None)'). The route category's 0.8 is therefore the template's score, and the 'llm-only' row double-counts the template on exactly the questions where the model fails.
attacks.fix: Add a bench mode that calls _llm_answer with allow_fallback=False (pure tail) and report both; give rt01/rt04/pp03 gold rows (reachable flag + route list, or contains_any on the route ids) so exec_acc is never None on an answerable question; report per-mode_used counts in every summary.

attacks.claim: Resume framing: 'grounded-by-construction verbalisation (slots or Cypher + slot-bound answer template) is the defensible systems contribution; prior art templates the query, not the verbalisation'; 'a measured cost model (1 output token ~ 120 prompt tokens)'.
attacks.problem: Slot-filled answer templates rendered from query results are template-based data-to-text NLG (Reiter & Dale era), and letting the model choose the template is a plan-then-realise pattern; an AI-researcher reviewer will read 'novel slot-bound answer template' as a Jinja template. The 'cost model' is one division of two throughput numbers. The three-tier router is Neo4j's own published guidance. As written, contributions (1)-(3) read as engineering and will invite the 'prompt-tweaking' verdict the proposal wants to avoid.
attacks.fix: Lead the resume bullet with the benchmark and the measured, honest results: a provenance/time-first Text2Cypher benchmark with multi-snapshot EX, K-repeat paired statistics quantifying FP8/serving nondeterminism, coverage-vs-risk curves, and pre-registered ablations including negative results (grammar coercion, prompt compression, spec-decode corruption). Present the answer-template mechanism as an engineering pattern with a measured fluency/grounding trade-off and cite template-based NLG as prior art; drop 'cost model' as a contribution and keep it as a design rationale.

attacks.claim: Correct = EX_strict AND Grounded AND Facts AND HighlightAcc; ConsistencyRate over paraphrase groups; pass^3 and paired McNemar from K=3 with 'seen' flags; all part of S0 (3 h code).
attacks.problem: questions.json has only answerable, category, compare, gold_cypher, id, must_mention, must_not_mention, note, question: there is no gold highlight id, no seed_id/paraphrase_of, no phrasing tier, so HighlightAcc and ConsistencyRate cannot be computed for baseline-v1 without authoring 54 highlight golds and paraphrase links. The 'seen' flag is configuration-dependent (V0 bank: 1 verbatim; V2 bank: 6 verbatim), not a question property. run_bench's 'repairs' metric is 'non-json calls minus 1' and 'json' currently means compose; once S3 removes compose and S4 adds a json router, both counters become meaningless unless the role ledger lands first.
attacks.fix: S0 must ship the role ledger before any other change; compute 'seen' per run from the rendered bank; for the demo window define Correct without HighlightAcc (report highlight as secondary) and add the gold highlight/seed fields when authoring the held-out set.

attacks.claim: Memory headroom is 12-14 GB (proposal) or 19 GB (task context); S12 trains a 0.5-1.5B student (9.8 GB peak) and a resident Gemma-3-4B specialist 'barely fits'.
attacks.problem: free -g on 2026-09-25 shows 9 GB free / 11 GB available with only the llm (0.4) and vision (0.2) services resident (no ASR process). The PEFT smoke test's 9.8 GB peak plus a FlashInfer JIT spike does not fit reliably in 11 GB, and any 4B specialist or third ZRT label is impossible without stopping vision; the headroom number changed by 3-8 GB within a day, so every memory-based feasibility statement in the proposal is stale.
attacks.fix: Record free/available memory in the results fingerprint; make S12 and any specialist model explicitly conditional on stopping the vision service in an agreed window; train and serve sequentially with MAX_JOBS capped.

attacks.claim: Acceptance gate for S1-S4: 'abstain stays 6/6'; AbstentionRecall is a headline metric.
attacks.problem: The unanswerable set is six items and the metric is saturated at 1.0 in five of six existing runs: na04 is caught by the _MUTATION regex before any model call, na03/na05 (Building 99/500) produce zero rows and the canned 'no matching records' text, and ABSTAIN_RX also matches 'could not build' so an exception on an unanswerable question counts as a correct abstention (errors are rewarded). The gate cannot detect regressions and FalseRefusal is not gated anywhere in the demo window, although S2's deadline and S4's 'other' class both increase refusals.
attacks.fix: Gate on FalseRefusal (<= baseline) as well as AbstentionRecall; detect abstention from the explicit answerable/abstain_reason field once added and never count mode=error as an abstention; expand unanswerables to ~20 in the held-out set (false premise, stale, underspecified, out-of-schema property).

attacks.claim: S11: relaunch with --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 16 gives -0.4 to -0.7 s per LLM question.
attacks.problem: Verified that the flags exist in the installed vLLM 0.26.0 (arg_utils.py lines 698-699; CacheConfig.prefix_match_unit docstring) and that hybrid models are opt-in (arg_utils.py:2518). But prefix_match_unit only refines attention-KV matching; the Mamba SSM state is still checkpointed at mamba block boundaries (4,176 tokens with fp8 KV, ~2,176 with bf16 KV), so a 2,710-token shared prefix that then diverges has no stored SSM state to resume from, which is exactly the limitation PR #46384 lists. The expected saving is therefore unsupported unless the static prefix is padded past one Mamba block (which inflates reported prompt tokens) or bf16 KV halves the block and the prompt is arranged to exceed it.
attacks.fix: Keep S11 post-demo with the existing revert gate, but state the expected hit condition explicitly (static prefix >= one Mamba block after the chosen KV dtype), test both padded and unpadded layouts, and report computed tokens = prompt - cached only when usage.prompt_tokens_details is present.

attacks.claim: Recoverability: 'restore_state.sh baseline-v1 must reproduce the mean within the CI'; snapshot = git tag + graph dump + copies of results.
attacks.problem: With a +/-11 pp Wilson interval at n=60, 'within the CI' is satisfied by almost any run and does not test reproducibility. scripts/snapshot_state.sh copies every file in bench/results into every snapshot directory and commits them (features-v1 already carries 20k lines of baseline results), and restore_state.sh leaves the repo on a detached HEAD after stashing; results files record only the short git sha, not whether the tree was dirty (the all-*-8d1c86c files were produced from an untracked state).
attacks.fix: Define reproducibility as per-question majority-of-K agreement (e.g. >= 90% of questions identical) plus token counts within 5%; add a dirty-tree flag and the SCHEMA_TEXT/ANSWER_SYSTEM/bank hashes to the fingerprint; snapshot only the results produced at that tag; have restore create a branch from the tag.

attacks.claim: EX_strict (CypherBench semantics) becomes the headline text-to-Cypher metric.
attacks.problem: Several golds fix an answer shape that the question does not imply: ag03 'How many roads are blocked?' has gold count(r) with compare value=2, and the system's row-listing query (two blocked roads, answer 'Two roads are currently blocked') scores exec=False today and would still fail under EX_strict; conversely EX_key today passes pv05/tm03 with the right id and the wrong column. Moving to EX_strict without multi-shape golds will penalise correct answers on every aggregation question.
attacks.fix: Allow a list of accepted gold shapes per question (count or list; ordered or not) and score EX_strict as 'matches any accepted gold'; keep EvJ for partial credit and audit EX_strict/EX_key disagreements by hand once.

attacks.claim: Literature support: TeCoD 'up to 36% higher execution accuracy and 2.2x lower latency on matched queries' motivates Tier 2; Ozsoy 2026 confidence selection '77.6% -> 85.4%' motivates S9.
attacks.problem: Both TeCoD figures are in the arXiv 2604.28028 abstract (verified), but they come from mining templates out of historical NL-SQL pairs with a fine-tuned NLI matcher on BIRD with 1B-14B models, not from ~13 hand-written templates picked by an LLM slot router; the transfer of '+36%' to this setting is a hope, not evidence. The 77.6 -> 85.4 numbers are not in the 2605.10318 abstract (only qualitative statements), so they are unverified here; the 2609.02324 abstract does state 30.7% budget / 21-25% wall-clock / 0.2-0.5% loss (verified).
attacks.fix: Cite TeCoD as the closest prior art for template routing without quoting its gain as an expectation; mark the Ozsoy numbers 'from the paper body, unverified' or re-check them in the HTML version before they appear in any write-up.

final.decision: Keep LLM+KG via text-to-Cypher as the core (regex router -> parameterised templates first, text-to-Cypher tail second), but make the contamination-controlled benchmark the research object and the answer layer the engineering: a held-out test set with paraphrase/radio-speak tiers, ~20 categorised unanswerables, multi-snapshot execution accuracy, K-repeat paired statistics and coverage-vs-risk curves, with unseen-only Correct as the primary metric and a per-run 'seen' flag computed from the rendered few-shot bank. The answer layer moves the model out of the prose incrementally: deterministic row-only rendering (template-based NLG, cited as such) for known row shapes now, a slot-bound answer template and a logprob-gated Tier-2 slot router post-demo, each adopted only if it passes a pre-specified non-inferiority test on unseen questions. The demo window is cut to freezing baseline-v1 at HEAD 8d1c86c with a role/fingerprint ledger, fixing two real latency bugs in the Cypher parser, a renderer restricted to shapes the templates already render and reconciled with the grounding check, and rehearsing scripted Tier-1 questions in mode=auto.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: LLM-only: serialise the whole graph into the prompt and answer without Cypher
why_not_alternatives.reason: Measured 7.6-8.9k prompt tokens today (2x the baseline) and 15-60k at 100-500 events against max-model-len 32,768; the local probe got the aggregation wrong and invented an entity; there are no rows, so provenance, highlight ids and the fact-check cannot exist. Kept as one reference row (A0) only.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Vector RAG over event text / transcripts
why_not_alternatives.reason: Similarity retrieval cannot express 'last N minutes', sums, routes over blocked/conflicted roads or as-of semantics; a stale transcript can outrank the current node status. The one useful form (a fulltext clause inside Cypher) is already allowlisted via db.index.fulltext.queryNodes and needs no new architecture.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: GraphRAG family (Microsoft GraphRAG, LightRAG, HippoRAG, Think-on-Graph)
why_not_alternatives.reason: These build and index a graph from unstructured text; RescueGrid already has a typed, provenance-tagged property graph and an executed Cypher is exact and fresh. Community summaries go stale within seconds on a live graph; the RAG-vs-GraphRAG study and GraphRAG-Bench show graphs help multi-hop over large corpora, not fact lookups (arXiv 2502.11371, 2506.05690).

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Agentic ReAct / MCP tool loop
why_not_alternatives.reason: Needs a relaunch with a tool parser (tool calling 400s today), multiplies calls 3-4x at ~3 s each (10-15 s per question, unbounded worst case), and Neo4j's own MCP-Cypher agent scored 0.71 with 3.6 calls/question using Claude 3.7 Sonnet; Nemotron Nano's BFCL v4 is 53.2.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: DIN-SQL / MAC-SQL / CHESS-style decomposition and schema linking
why_not_alternatives.reason: The schema fits in 815 tokens (380 compact), where 'The Death of Schema Linking' shows linking costs 2.7-4.8 EX points; decomposition is 4-8 sequential calls at 45 tok/s (+10-20 s per question on this box).

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Adopting the existing entity_link + schema_check flags as the fix for the failing questions
why_not_alternatives.reason: Measured at HEAD 8d1c86c: entity_link alone 0.717 Correct with repairs 18 -> 24; entity_link+schema_check 0.717 with repairs 33, error rate 0.067, p95 13.55 s and prompt tokens 5,198 per LLM question. schema_check was written against the benchmark's own failures (its docstring says so), so any gain would be test-tuned anyway. Kept only as ablation cells on the held-out set.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Adopting fewshot_v2 + dyn_fewshot on the strength of the 8d1c86c all-flags run (0.733 -> 0.800)
why_not_alternatives.reason: EXAMPLES_V2 contains six benchmark questions verbatim (rt01, px04, cf01, tm07, un01, st01) plus near-duplicates of tm01/tm02/na03; three of the eight 'fixed' questions are leaked items, four questions broke (pv05, px02, rt02, ag03), and on the 51 uncontaminated questions the gain is one question (39/51 -> 40/51). The bank must be decontaminated and re-measured before any adoption decision.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: LoRA on the 30B Nemotron itself, or Mamba/GDN-hybrid students (Nemotron-3-Nano-4B, Qwen3.5) via Unsloth/GRPO
why_not_alternatives.reason: 16-bit LoRA of Nemotron 3 Nano needs ~60 GB (Unsloth docs) vs 9 GB free / 11 GB available today; the resident checkpoint is FP8; serving an adapter needs a restart of the shared service; hybrid students need mamba_ssm/fla kernels absent for sm_121a/aarch64 and a docker/NGC route not available to this user.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Speculative decoding now (ngram / suffix / EAGLE3 / MTP)
why_not_alternatives.reason: The FP8 Nano checkpoint has no MTP head and no public EAGLE3 draft; ngram on hybrid recurrent models has open silent-corruption PRs (vLLM #56531/#55504: Nemotron 12/60 correct before the fix) and was already reverted on this box. Post-demo only as a documented negative result with a greedy-equality test.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Learned prompt compression (LLMLingua-2 / Selective Context)
why_not_alternatives.reason: Prefill of the whole 2.8k prompt costs ~0.5 s of a ~5 s question, so the ceiling is ~0.35 s, and the compressors delete exactly the low-frequency schema identifiers Cypher must copy verbatim. At most one negative ablation row.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Schema-compiled grammar-constrained decoding as the headline thesis
why_not_alternatives.reason: The baseline has 0 guard rejections and its failures are semantic (value lookups, time-window idioms, projection omissions); three probes on this endpoint produced grammatical-but-wrong Cypher, and Ozsoy 2026 (verified in the paper body) shows grammar/schema filtering raises empty predictions 0 -> 24 -> 36 on Gemma-2-9B. Kept as one pre-registered ablation dimension, not the system.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: A client-side 8 s deadline that returns 'no matching records' (the original S2)
why_not_alternatives.reason: The worst outlier (px02, 21.7 s) is a parser bug (unterminated code fence + finish_reason=length fed to the guard three times), not a model limit; a deadline hides it, and 'no matching records' after a timeout is a false statement that ABSTAIN_RX would also score as a correct abstention. Replaced by the bug fixes plus a distinct 'timed out' message with abstain_reason=timeout.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Tier-2 LLM slot router shipped before the demo, gated on the model's self-reported confidence
why_not_alternatives.reason: A self-reported JSON confidence is uncalibrated on a 3B-active model (the 1-token probe mis-labelled a plain status question); the router probe cost 72 completion tokens / 3.74 s under load, so every non-regex question would pay +1.5-4 s on the miss path; and the temporal gain claimed (0.14 -> 0.7) is largely delivered already by the regex router in auto mode (temporal 0.43). Moved post-demo with a measurable gate (guided_choice intent logprob + deterministic slot validation + regex/BM25 agreement).

why_not_alternatives.alternative: RS_10 as the pre-registered primary metric
why_not_alternatives.reason: On a 54/60-answerable set RS_10 is dominated by -10 x #wrong: baseline RS_10 = -1.93 while all-abstain scores about +0.1 and answer-30-refuse-24 scores about +0.6, so the grid would select the most refusal-prone variant. Correct (unseen-only) is primary; RS_c is reported at c in {0, 1, 10} with a FalseRefusal floor.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Adding Neo4j's text-to-cypher-Gemma-3-4B as a resident specialist
why_not_alternatives.reason: ~8 GB BF16 plus KV does not fit in 9 GB free / 11 GB available next to Nemotron (47.5 GB) and Qwen3-VL (26.8 GB) without stopping the vision service; the model card publishes no accuracy numbers; a fourth model is a team decision.

why_not_alternatives.alternative: Relaunching the shared 'llm' server before the demo (prefix caching, bf16 KV, tool parser)
why_not_alternatives.reason: Upper bound ~0.5-0.7 s per LLM question and only if the static prefix exceeds one Mamba block (4,176 tokens with fp8 KV, ~2,176 with bf16) since --prefix-match-unit refines attention-KV matching but the SSM state is checkpointed at block boundaries (vLLM PR #46384 lists shared-prefix-then-divergent workloads as a limitation); it interrupts the vision/ASR teammates. Post-demo bundle only, verified by vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total > 0.

final.baseline: baseline-v1 = code at HEAD 8d1c86c of /home/hp2/kenil/rescuegrid-reasoning after committing the four untracked ladder result files (all-auto, all-llm, l1-entity, l2-entity-schema at 8d1c86c) and adding the role/fingerprint ledger to bench/run_bench.py, with QA_FEATURES unset (the verbatim pinned SCHEMA_TEXT: schema 815 + rules 304 + 11 V0 few-shots 1,591 = 2,710 tokens; ANSWER_SYSTEM 504 tokens), LLM_THINKING=false, temperature 0.0, call A max_tokens 320, call B json_schema with COMPOSE_MAX_TOKENS 320, max_repairs 2 + 1 zero-row retry, one fact-check regeneration, OpenAI client max_retries=1 / timeout 120 s (recorded; changed in D1); graph = private Neo4j bolt://127.0.0.1:7687 restored from bench/snapshots/baseline-v0/graph.json (sha256 7f101435..., 20 entities / 10 events / 36 rels) with RESCUEGRID_CLOCK=replay; questions = bench/questions.json (sha256 fea4829d..., 60 questions; 51 with gold_cypher; rt01/rt04/pp03 given gold rows in D0 so exec_acc is never None on an answerable item); server = vLLM 0.26.0 serving nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8 as 'llm' at http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 with only --max-model-len=32768 --trust-remote-code (enable_prefix_caching=False, attention block 4,176 tokens, kv_cache_dtype fp8_e4m3, no speculative config, gpu_memory_fraction 0.4) as in /opt/hp/zrt/run/vllm-llm.json. Three modes, K=3 each, on an otherwise idle box (vLLM running-request gauge and free/available memory recorded): --mode llm, --mode auto, and the new --mode llm-pure (QAEngine._llm_answer with allow_fallback=False, so template substitution on error/zero rows is off). Every results file carries: git sha + dirty-tree flag, sha256 of SCHEMA_TEXT, ANSWER_SYSTEM and the rendered few-shot bank, sha256 of questions.json and the graph snapshot, vllm-llm.json contents, vLLM version, QA_FEATURES, K, temperature, the per-run 'seen' ids (verbatim or token-Jaccard >= 0.7 against any bank question: for the V0 bank rt01 verbatim, tm01/tm02 near-duplicates), and per-call roles (cypher, repair_k, zero_row_retry, compose, compose_retry, router). Reproducibility = per-question majority-of-K outcome agreement >= 90% and token counts within 5% after scripts/restore_state.sh baseline-v1 (which creates a branch from the tag). Reference single-run numbers to land near (baseline-llm-6d30e04.json, llm mode): correct 0.733 (unseen-only 39/51 = 0.765), exec_acc 0.804, grounded 0.944, facts 0.741, abstain 6/6, 4,377 prompt + 221 completion tokens per LLM question over 2.14 calls, p50 5.08 s, p95 11.62 s, 18 repairs, 0 guard rejections; RS_0 0.73, RS_1 0.47, RS_10 -1.93; modes used llm 54 / llm+fallback 4 / fallback 1 / error 1. Auto mode (baseline-auto-6d30e04.json): correct 0.75, 17/60 routed by regex, p50 4.7 s, p95 7.05 s.

metrics.name: Correct (primary) and Correct_unseen
metrics.definition: Per question: for answerable items EX (EX_key in the demo window, EX_strict-any-shape once R1 lands) AND Grounded AND Facts AND mode != error (HighlightAcc joins the conjunction when gold highlight ids exist); for unanswerable items an explicit correct abstention (never mode=error). Correct_unseen restricts to questions not flagged 'seen' for that run's rendered few-shot bank and is the headline; on the held-out test set the two coincide. Reported as mean over K=3 with Wilson 95% CI and seed-clustered SE; deltas as paired mean-of-K differences with a 90% paired-bootstrap interval, plus exact McNemar on majority-of-K outcomes for significance claims on the held-out set only.

metrics.name: Non-inferiority acceptance rule (for adopting any change)
metrics.definition: A change is adopted only if the lower bound of the 90% paired-bootstrap interval on the mean-of-K Correct_unseen difference is > -3 pp, no category loses more than one question, repairs and p95 are not worse than the comparison run, AbstentionRecall is not lower and FalseRefusal is not higher. Stated limitation: n=51 unseen (n=60) cannot certify gains below ~10 pp; gains are claimed only on the ~100-question held-out set.

metrics.name: EX_strict (any accepted shape), EX_key, EvJ
metrics.definition: EX_strict = 1 iff multiset(rows_pred) equals any of the question's accepted gold row sets up to column permutation (ordered comparison when the gold Cypher has ORDER BY; floats 3 dp, ISO datetimes, nested lists sorted, empty==empty scores 1; CypherBench semantics). Each question may list several accepted shapes (count vs list, e.g. ag03). EX_key = today's set equality on declared key columns, kept as the lenient secondary. EvJ = Jaccard of entity-id sets in rows for partial credit. EX_strict/EX_key disagreements audited by hand once.

metrics.name: EX_multi
metrics.definition: min over S=4-6 replayed graph snapshots of EX_strict when the same predicted Cypher is re-executed on each snapshot with that snapshot's replay clock as $now; EX_strict - EX_multi measures queries right on one snapshot only (over-filtering).

metrics.name: Grounded (over answered questions with rows) and GroundedCoverage
metrics.definition: Grounded = 1 iff fact_check(answer, rows) returns no problem, computed only on questions that were answered with >= 1 evidence row and using the same inputs in engine and benchmark (evidence + conflicts + provenance in both); zero-row and error answers are excluded and reported as GroundedCoverage = fraction of answerable questions that were answered with rows. Deterministic renderers must pass the same check on their own rows (unit-tested), so 'by construction' is a tested property limited to the value classes the checker covers (sources, times, confidences, percentages), not a blanket claim.

metrics.name: Facts
metrics.definition: 1 iff every must_mention string appears (case-insensitive) and no must_not_mention string appears in the answer.

metrics.name: HighlightAcc (post-demo)
metrics.definition: 1 iff highlight.id equals the gold subject id (or one of the accepted ids); gold highlight ids are authored with the held-out set, so it is reported as secondary until then and joins Correct afterwards.

metrics.name: AbstentionRecall / FalseRefusal
metrics.definition: AbstentionRecall = explicit abstentions (answerable=false field with abstain_reason in {out_of_schema, no_records, timeout, mutation_refused, underspecified}) on unanswerable questions / unanswerable questions; FalseRefusal = explicit abstentions on answerable questions / answerable questions. mode=error never counts as an abstention. Regex ABSTAIN_RX only until the field exists. Gate: FalseRefusal <= 5% (and <= baseline) for every adopted change.

metrics.name: RS_c (reliability score, secondary)
metrics.definition: TrustSQL-style: mean over questions of +1 for a correct answer or correct abstention, 0 for abstaining on an answerable question, -c for a wrong answer or for answering an unanswerable question, reported at c in {0, 1, 10}; baseline RS_0 0.73, RS_1 0.47, RS_10 -1.93. RS_1 is the y-axis of the Pareto chart; RS_10 is reported, not optimised, because on a 90%-answerable set it rewards refusal.

metrics.name: pass^3 and ConsistencyRate
metrics.definition: pass^3 = fraction of questions correct in all 3 repeats (reliability under serving nondeterminism); ConsistencyRate = fraction of paraphrase groups (seed_id links authored with the held-out set) whose members all get the same Correct outcome.

metrics.name: Tokens per question by call role
metrics.definition: prompt_tokens and completion_tokens per question split by role (cypher, repair_k, zero_row_retry, compose, compose_retry, router) from the CALLS ledger, plus finish_reason=length count and guard rejections; cached_tokens reported once the server exposes prompt_tokens_details (null until then); 'repairs' redefined as the count of repair_k + zero_row_retry roles.

metrics.name: Latency
metrics.definition: wall p50 / p95 per question, LLM-seconds per question (sum of call durations), calls per LLM question, timeout count, and the vLLM running-request gauge and free/available memory at run time; LLM-seconds and tokens are primary, wall-clock secondary.

metrics.name: TokensPerCorrect / SecondsPerCorrect
metrics.definition: mean total tokens per question / Correct_unseen, and mean wall seconds / Correct_unseen (Cost-of-Pass with tokens as the currency since inference is local); every variant plotted on an RS_1-vs-tokens Pareto chart.

metrics.name: Router metrics (Tier 1+2)
metrics.definition: coverage = fraction of questions routed; false-route rate = routed questions whose template answer is not Correct; reported as a coverage-vs-risk curve across the gate threshold (intent-token logprob for Tier 2) on the held-out paraphrase/radio-speak tier, in the style of selective classification.

metrics.name: Seen flag and contamination audit
metrics.definition: Per run: ids whose question is verbatim or token-Jaccard >= 0.7 to any question in the rendered few-shot bank or template test corpus, with the bank hash; reported alongside every accuracy so a reader can recompute unseen-only numbers.

metrics.name: Error taxonomy histogram
metrics.definition: Each failed question (majority-of-K) gets one primary code: value_lookup_miss, time_window_semantics, projection_omission, entity_linking, over_filtering, wrong_pattern, wrong_aggregation, reversed_direction, invented_property, guard_rejection, syntax_error, truncation, compose_ungrounded, highlight_wrong, timeout; 20 labels double-checked by a teammate with agreement reported.

roadmap.step: D0. Freeze baseline-v1 at HEAD 8d1c86c: commit the four untracked ladder files; add the per-call role ledger, fingerprint block (git sha + dirty flag, SCHEMA_TEXT/ANSWER_SYSTEM/rendered-bank hashes, questions + snapshot sha256, vllm-llm.json, free/available memory, vLLM running-request gauge), per-run 'seen' ids, unseen-only rates, K repeats with Wilson CI, pass^3 and paired bootstrap/McNemar vs a named file, and --mode llm-pure (allow_fallback=False); give rt01/rt04/pp03 gold rows; run llm, auto and llm-pure at K=3; scripts/snapshot_state.sh baseline-v1 (snapshot only this tag's results; restore creates a branch)
roadmap.hypothesis: The committed numbers are single-run, the tree was dirty for the 8d1c86c runs, mode=llm silently substitutes templates on 4-5 questions, and 'seen' is a property of the bank not the question, so no option can be ranked without repeats, pairing and a per-run contamination flag
roadmap.expected_gain: A defensible baseline table: Correct ~0.70-0.75 (unseen ~0.77) with CI about +/-11 pp at n=60, pass^3 10-20 pp below the mean, ~4.4k prompt + ~220 completion tokens and ~5 s p50 per LLM question, a first llm-pure row that is expected to be lower than llm on route questions
roadmap.effort: ~2.5 h code + ~65 min box time (3 modes x K=3 x ~7 min)
roadmap.how_to_measure: bench/results/baseline-v1-{llm,auto,llm-pure}-<sha>-k{1,2,3}.json with fingerprint; restore_state.sh baseline-v1 reproduces majority-of-K outcomes on >= 90% of questions and tokens within 5%

roadmap.step: D1. Fix the two real latency bugs in rescuegrid/qa/text2cypher.py and the client: strip an unterminated opening fence in extract_cypher; treat finish_reason=length as its own repair reason ('your query was cut off; return a shorter query with at most N RETURN columns') and never feed a truncated query back as the previous query; OpenAI client max_retries=0 with a per-call timeout (~25 s); on a per-question deadline emit a distinct 'timed out before a query could be built' answer with answerable=false, abstain_reason=timeout, never 'no matching records'; verify once with a deliberately long request that the proxy cancels the vLLM request (log)
roadmap.hypothesis: The worst outliers are parser/loop artefacts: px02 hit finish=length at 320 tokens three times (21.7 s) with the leading ```cypher rejected twice by the guard; rt01 spent 3 x ~250 completion tokens (17.4 s) before falling back; hidden client retries are neither bounded nor in the token ledger
roadmap.expected_gain: p95 11.6 s -> ~9 s without touching accuracy; truncation cases become one short repair instead of three; every LLM second appears in the ledger
roadmap.effort: ~1.5 h + ~15 min box (--only px02 rt01 rt04 tm05 pp03 at K=3, then one full llm pass)
roadmap.how_to_measure: finish=length count, guard rejections, p95, paired Correct_unseen vs baseline-v1 (must be non-inferior), timeout count = 0 on the idle box

roadmap.step: D2 (optional if time allows). Deterministic renderer only for the two row shapes the pre-baked templates already render (single-entity status row, Event list), reconciled with the grounding check: print only values that are row cells (no window boundaries, no counts unless a count column exists), fix the tm07 window-boundary and route-renderer (rt01/rt04) fact-check failures, unit test that every rendered answer passes fact_check on its own rows; LLM json_schema compose (60-word cap) stays for every other shape
roadmap.hypothesis: Call B costs 842 prompt + 84 completion tokens and 2.13 s on 49/59 LLM questions; rendering the two most common shapes removes it on ~40% of LLM questions; the existing renderers are not yet grounded by construction (tm07 fails fact_check in auto mode), so reconciliation must precede any 'by construction' claim
roadmap.expected_gain: -2 s and -900 tokens on rendered questions; compose calls per LLM question ~0.85 -> ~0.5; Grounded (over answered-with-rows) not lower; Facts not lower
roadmap.how_to_measure: Grounded/GroundedCoverage, Facts, tokens by role, latency p50; paired non-inferiority on Correct_unseen; per-shape unit tests in tests/test_qa_fallback.py

roadmap.step: D3. Demo freeze demo-v1: mode=auto on the pinned prompt (QA_FEATURES unset, or compact_schema,dyn_fewshot only if a decontaminated-bank K=3 cell passes the non-inferiority rule in time); rehearse each scripted question 3x and record pass^3; scripted questions restricted to Tier-1 regex routes; no server relaunch, no T>0, fusion-agent LLM calls kept off the QA critical path; snapshot_state.sh demo-v1
roadmap.hypothesis: Under co-tenant load decode drops to 16-34 tok/s (probes 2026-09-25), so only Tier-1 answers are predictable; unscripted questions must degrade to an honest timeout, not a false 'no records'
roadmap.expected_gain: Every scripted question answers in < 2 s with pass^3 = 1.0; unscripted questions bounded by the per-call timeout with an honest message
roadmap.how_to_measure: bench --only <scripted ids> --mode auto at K=3; restore_state.sh demo-v1 reproduces it

roadmap.step: R1. Held-out test set and scorer: author ~100 new questions from the EOC category taxonomy by entity-swapped generation (never from failing dev items), including ~20 categorised unanswerables (false premise, stale, underspecified, out-of-schema property), short/radio-speak paraphrase tiers with seed_id links, gold highlight ids and accepted gold shapes; decontaminate EXAMPLES_V2 (drop or entity-swap the 6 verbatim + 3 near-duplicate entries) and pin V0 with its 3 seen ids; EX_strict/EvJ scorer (port CypherBench comparator), explicit answerable/abstain_reason contract fields, multi-snapshot EX over 4-6 replayed graph states, error taxonomy with a second annotator on 20 items; re-score the frozen baseline-v1 and demo-v1 files first (rows and gold_rows are stored)
roadmap.hypothesis: The existing 60 questions have been looked at during development (schema_check and the V2 bank were built from their failures) and are now a dev set; a single snapshot hides over-filtering (Zhong et al. 2020: 2.5% average / 8.1% worst-case false negatives); short NL drops accuracy sharply (Jackal: 86.0% long vs 35.7% short); the abstention gate is saturated at 6/6 and rewards errors
roadmap.expected_gain: A benchmark that survives review: CI half-width ~+/-8 pp at n=100, an honest EX_strict-EX_multi gap, FalseRefusal measurable, seen=0 by construction
roadmap.effort: ~1.5 days authoring + ~4 h code; no LLM cost for the snapshot loop
roadmap.how_to_measure: Re-scored baseline-v1/demo-v1 under the new metrics; annotator agreement on the taxonomy; contamination audit reports 0 seen

roadmap.step: R2. Flag sweep done properly: the 10-cell ladder (bench/ladder.sh) at K=3 on the held-out set with the decontaminated bank, reported against the 8d1c86c single runs as first data points (all-llm 0.800 vs baseline 0.733 but +1 unseen question, repairs 18 -> 29, calls 2.14 -> 2.42, p50 5.08 -> 5.79 s; l1-entity 0.717 / repairs 24; l2-entity-schema 0.717 / repairs 33 / error 0.067)
roadmap.hypothesis: compact_schema and dyn_fewshot cut call-A prompt tokens (2,818 -> ~1,300 measured) at no accuracy cost; entity_link and schema_check as implemented trade prompt tokens for extra repair rounds without rescuing questions; the earlier '+6.7 pp' was mostly contamination
roadmap.expected_gain: Prompt tokens per LLM question ~4,400 -> ~2,300 with Correct_unseen non-inferior; a documented negative result for static schema checking on this model
roadmap.effort: ~1 h wiring + ~3.5 h box (10 cells x 3 x 7 min), run overnight
roadmap.how_to_measure: Non-inferiority rule per cell; McNemar on majority-of-K for any claimed gain; tokens-per-correct Pareto

roadmap.step: R3. Repair budget ablation (A2): schema_check {off,on} x max_repairs {0,1,2} x zero-row retry {off,on}, with the structured truncation repair from D1
roadmap.hypothesis: The second repair round rarely rescues a question (tm05: 5 calls, 14.4 s, still wrong); adaptive budgeting literature reports 21-25% wall-clock savings for 0.2-0.5% loss (arXiv 2609.02324, verified abstract)
roadmap.expected_gain: p95 < 8 s and ~2.9k tokens saved per avoided round at no measurable Correct loss
roadmap.how_to_measure: p95, repairs, tokens by role, paired Correct_unseen, FalseRefusal

roadmap.step: R4. Projection macro + short few-shots: the model emits MATCH/OPTIONAL MATCH/WHERE/WITH/ORDER BY/LIMIT and a RETURN marker; code appends the canonical provenance projection per bound variable; explicit RETURN kept for computed values (danger, people, hops)
roadmap.hypothesis: RETURN..LIMIT is ~50% of few-shot Cypher tokens and the model copies that shape (116 completion tokens per call A; rt01 250 per call); at 45 tok/s decode vs 5.5k tok/s prefill one output token costs the wall time of ~120 prompt tokens; omitted-id failures (tm04, cf01, rt05) disappear when the projection is canonical
roadmap.expected_gain: Call-A completion 116 -> ~65 tokens (-1.1 s per call), prompt -700 tokens, truncations -> 0
roadmap.how_to_measure: completion tokens per call A, paired Correct_unseen, projection_omission and truncation counts

roadmap.step: R5. Slot-bound answer template in the same call (template-based NLG, cited as such): call A returns Cypher plus a template whose slots reference RETURN aliases; template text restricted to a closed connective vocabulary / per-shape phrase library; the validator rejects any token outside slots that matches an entity name, status value, relationship word, number or time; unit tests that every rendered answer passes fact_check on its own rows; blind 20-answer fluency rating by a teammate
roadmap.hypothesis: Grounding for the checked value classes can be enforced at the interface rather than checked after the fact; prior art templates the query (TeCoD, AWS parameterised templates) and template NLG realises text from data (Reiter & Dale), so the contribution is the combination and its measured fluency/grounding trade-off, not novelty of templating
roadmap.expected_gain: Compose call removed on most LLM questions (-2.1 s, -900 tokens), +30-50 completion tokens on call A; fluency loss measured, not hidden
roadmap.how_to_measure: Ablation A3 {LLM compose, LLM + 60-word cap, deterministic renderer, slot template}: Grounded, GroundedCoverage, Facts, tokens, latency, fluency rating

roadmap.step: R6. Tier-2 slot router with a measurable gate: guided_choice over enumerated intents with the intent token's logprob as the gate signal, deterministic slot validation (entity resolves, source in vocabulary, window parses), agreement with a cheap regex/BM25 prior; template inventory (7 -> ~13) designed from the EOC taxonomy on the dev split, one regression test per template; tail p50 measured with the router in the path
roadmap.hypothesis: EOC questions are recurrent shapes and TeCoD is the closest prior art for template routing (it mined templates from historical pairs with a fine-tuned matcher on BIRD; its gains do not transfer as an expectation); the router's miss-path cost (72 completion tokens / 3.74 s measured under load) must be paid by every non-regex question
roadmap.expected_gain: Reported as a coverage-vs-false-route curve on the held-out paraphrase tier; adopted only if the tail p50 including the router is not worse than without it
roadmap.how_to_measure: A4: router off/on x logprob gate thresholds; coverage, false-route rate, p50 with router, paired Correct_unseen

roadmap.step: R7. Execution-grounded best-of-4 on the tail: n=4 in one request at T=0.7 (n>1 with json_schema and EBNF verified on this endpoint), guard + schema filter, execute all candidates, select by result-set agreement, non-empty preference and mean token logprob
roadmap.hypothesis: Greedy decoding is already non-deterministic here; confidence-based selection lifted Gemma-2-9B from 77.6% to 85.4% execution success in Ozsoy 2026 (verified in the paper body); gains appear from 3 samples (arXiv 2503.24364); n=4 measured at 1.5x wall time on this box
roadmap.expected_gain: Tail EX +5 to +10 pp at ~3.5x call-A completion tokens; reported on tokens-per-correct, not as a free win; cannot fix unanimous semantic misreads
roadmap.how_to_measure: A5 selection-signal ablation on EX_strict, RS_1, tokens-per-correct

roadmap.step: R8. Schema-compiled typed EBNF for read-only Cypher via xgrammar structured_outputs.grammar with a coverage test that all gold queries parse
roadmap.hypothesis: Grammar removes structural error classes but not pattern choice; expected outcome is validity up, EX flat, empties up (Ozsoy 2026: 0 -> 24 -> 36 empties on Gemma-2-9B); beam beats sample+vote under constraints and a larger model beats more compute (arXiv 2608.25761, verified abstract)
roadmap.expected_gain: guard/schema rejections -> 0; EX within +/-5 pp; empties measured; a publishable negative/neutral result on a 3B-active hybrid
roadmap.how_to_measure: A6 2x2 {few-shots static/kNN} x {grammar off/typed}; EX_strict, coverage, RS_1, tokens

roadmap.step: R9. Team relaunch bundle: --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 16 --enable-prompt-tokens-details (optional --kv-cache-dtype auto); hit condition stated up front: the static prefix must be >= one Mamba block after the chosen KV dtype (4,176 tokens fp8 / ~2,176 bf16), tested padded and unpadded
roadmap.hypothesis: Caching is simply off and the flags exist in the installed 0.26.0, but prefix_match_unit refines attention-KV matching only; the SSM state is checkpointed at block boundaries, which is the limitation PR #46384 lists for shared-prefix-then-divergent workloads
roadmap.expected_gain: -0.4 to -0.7 s per LLM question only if hits occur; cached_tokens reported; possibly more output variance
roadmap.how_to_measure: vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total > 0, usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, latency and pass^3 before/after; revert if 0

roadmap.step: R10 (conditional on the team stopping the vision service in an agreed window). Pattern-first synthetic pairs (schema patterns -> deterministic Cypher -> 30B paraphrase x3 -> execute and filter, de-duplicated against both question sets) -> LoRA r=16 BF16 on Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B then 1.5B (PEFT smoke test 1,692 tok/s, 9.8 GB peak; MAX_JOBS capped), merged and served under a third ZRT label; data-size curve 250/500/1k/2k
roadmap.hypothesis: Small fine-tuned models approach frontier Text2Cypher (CYQUARK, arXiv 2606.14325; exact averages unverified) and pairs-per-fixed-schema is unpublished; the token win is the schema prompt (~2.8k -> ~300)
roadmap.expected_gain: Call-A prompt ~300 tokens; decode only 1.5-2x faster at 273 GB/s; tail EX reported as a data-size curve
roadmap.how_to_measure: A10 model-swap cell on the held-out set; memory recorded in the fingerprint

ablations: A0. Reference rows: baseline-v1 llm (with template fallback) vs llm-pure (allow_fallback=False) vs auto (regex router + llm) vs router-only vs whole-graph-in-context LLM-only (no Cypher), with per-mode_used counts - answers the 'LLM vs LLM+KG vs templates' question without double-counting the templates

A1. Prompt: {pinned 2,710-token prompt, compact_schema, dyn_fewshot k=3, compact+dyn, compact+decontaminated-V2+dyn} on Correct_unseen, EX_strict, tokens; the rendered bank hash and per-run seen ids are stored, and the 8d1c86c single runs are reported as first data points (all-llm: +1 unseen question, repairs +61%)

A2. Validation/repair: schema_check {off,on} x max_repairs {0,1,2} x zero-row retry {off,on} on repairs, p95, tokens, Correct_unseen, FalseRefusal (l1/l2 at 8d1c86c already show repairs 24/33 at 0.717)

A3. Compose: {LLM json_schema compose, LLM compose + 60-word cap, deterministic row-only renderer, slot-bound answer template} on Grounded, GroundedCoverage, Facts, completion tokens, latency, plus a 20-answer blind fluency rating

A4. Routing tier: Tier-2 router {off, on} x intent-logprob gate thresholds, reported as a coverage-vs-false-route curve on the held-out paraphrase/radio-speak tier, with tail p50 measured with the router in the path
A5. Decoding: n=1 greedy vs best-of-4 with selection signal {result agreement, mean logprob, non-empty preference, validator pass, combined} on EX_strict, RS_1, tokens-per-correct
A6. Grammar: {none, schema-compiled typed EBNF} x {few-shots static, kNN} with coverage (empty predictions) and a structural-vs-semantic error split
A7. Thinking: enable_thinking {off, on with max_tokens 2048} on the tail only, reporting AbstentionRecall, FalseRefusal and latency

A8. Serving: prefix caching {off, on (align, prefix-match-unit 16)} x static prefix {unpadded, padded past one Mamba block} on latency, cached_tokens and pass^3 - a systems note, not an accuracy claim
A9. Negative rows kept for honesty: LLMLingua-2 prompt compression on call A; ngram speculative decoding greedy-equality test on 60 prompts
A10. Stretch: student model {none, Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B LoRA, 1.5B LoRA} x training data {pattern-grounded, 30B self-instruct} x data size {250, 500, 1k, 2k} on the held-out compositional split

Statistics for every cell: K=3, mean +/- seed-clustered SE, Wilson 95% CI, pass^3, paired mean-of-K difference with 90% paired-bootstrap interval and the non-inferiority rule; exact McNemar on majority-of-K only for significance claims on the held-out set; Correct_unseen primary, EX_strict secondary, RS_c at {0,1,10} reported with a FalseRefusal floor; every results file carries git sha + dirty flag, prompt/bank hashes, questions/snapshot sha256, server fingerprint, memory and concurrent-load markers
final.resume_framing: Built RescueGrid-QA, a contamination-controlled, provenance- and time-first text-to-Cypher benchmark and evaluation protocol for an offline disaster-response command post, and used it to evaluate a three-tier answer layer running a 30B-A3B hybrid Mamba/MoE model (FP8, vLLM 0.26) on an NVIDIA GB10 edge box. Benchmark: a held-out test set with paraphrase/radio-speak tiers and ~20 categorised unanswerables, per-run few-shot contamination flags, multi-snapshot execution accuracy for a time-versioned property graph with an audit trail, penalty-scored abstention reported as coverage-vs-risk curves, and K-repeat paired statistics that quantify FP8/serving nondeterminism. Findings reported honestly: a feature bundle that read as +6.7 pp on the dev set was +1 question once six leaked few-shot items were excluded; static schema checking increased repair rounds by 61% without improving accuracy; the worst latency outliers were parser bugs, not model limits. Engineering: router/template/text-to-Cypher tiers with deterministic row-only rendering (template-based NLG) that removes the second LLM call on common shapes, with the grounding/fluency trade-off measured rather than assumed; pre-registered ablations of prompt layout, repair budgeting, best-of-N execution-grounded selection and schema-compiled grammar decoding, including negative results (grammar-induced empties, prompt compression, speculative-decoding corruption). Reproducible, hash-fingerprinted, snapshot-restorable experiment state. Framed as 'a benchmark, an evaluation protocol and measured results on edge hardware', never as 'prompt tuning raised accuracy from X to Y'.
risks: Benchmark contamination and test-tuning: EXAMPLES_V2 holds six dev questions verbatim, schema_check was written from dev failures, and the 60 questions have all been inspected; mitigation: per-run seen flag from the rendered bank hash, unseen-only headline now, a held-out ~100-question test set authored from the taxonomy (never from failing items) post-demo, and no template or few-shot is ever derived from a test item

Demo-window overload: ~8 h of code (D0-D3) plus ~2 h box time while the developer also builds the fusion agent; mitigation: minimum viable cut is D0-lite (fingerprint + K=3 llm/auto) + D1 + D3 (~5 h), D2 is optional, and nothing in D0-D3 changes the Tier-1 regex path the scripted demo questions use

Single-run baseline numbers are stale and non-reproducible (scoring changed between c3108e3 and 6d30e04; T=0 outputs differ between identical calls; 8d1c86c runs came from a dirty tree); mitigation: D0 re-baseline at HEAD with K=3, pairing, dirty flag and reproducibility defined as >= 90% majority-of-K agreement

Co-tenant load during the demo (vision, ASR, fusion agent) halves decode speed (16-34 tok/s vs ~45 idle); mitigation: scripted questions on Tier 1 only, per-call timeout with an honest 'timed out' abstention, load and memory recorded in every results file

A confidently wrong template answer is worse than an honest refusal; mitigation: Tier 2 is post-demo, gated on an intent-token logprob plus deterministic slot validation and regex/BM25 agreement, one regression test per template, false-route rate reported on the held-out paraphrase tier, and executed LLM queries are never auto-promoted to templates (exec_acc ~0.8)

'Grounded by construction' over-claim: the existing renderers fail fact_check on tm07/rt01/rt04, the bench and engine feed different rows to fact_check, and zero-row wrong answers scored grounded=True (st06, st07, pv03, px04); mitigation: Grounded scored over answered-with-rows only with GroundedCoverage alongside, identical fact_check inputs in engine and bench, renderers print only row cells and are unit-tested against fact_check, claims limited to the checked value classes

Metric mis-specification pulls the grid toward refusal: RS_10 scores all-abstain (+0.1) above the baseline (-1.93); mitigation: Correct_unseen primary, RS_c reported at {0,1,10}, RS_1 on the Pareto chart, FalseRefusal <= 5% floor on every adopted change

Non-inferiority at n=60 is weak (CI about +/-11 pp; 'not significantly worse' is vacuous); mitigation: pre-specified -3 pp paired-bootstrap margin plus category/repairs/p95 guards, explicit statement that gains < ~10 pp cannot be certified on 60 questions, significance claims reserved for the held-out set

Abstention metrics are saturated and reward errors (6/6 in five of six runs; na04 is caught by a regex; ABSTAIN_RX matches 'could not build'); mitigation: explicit answerable/abstain_reason fields, mode=error never counts as abstention, ~20 unanswerables in the held-out set, FalseRefusal gated

Client-side deadlines may not free the GPU through the ZRT proxy and hidden client retries were unbounded (max_retries=1, 120 s); mitigation: max_retries=0, per-call timeout, one verified cancellation test against the vLLM log

Few-shot leakage does not even guarantee a pass (rt01 is verbatim in the V0 bank and still failed 3 rounds), so decontamination may lower the seen-item score; that is the honest number and is reported as such

Grammar-constrained decoding can push the model into grammatical nonsense and raises empty predictions (0 -> 24 -> 36 in Ozsoy 2026); mitigation: coverage test over all gold queries, regex guard kept as defence in depth, ablation not product path
Best-of-N multiplies completion tokens 3-4x and adds sampling variance; mitigation: post-demo only, reported on tokens-per-correct, T=0 remains production

Prefix-caching relaunch may not hit for a shared prefix shorter than one Mamba block, may add variance, and interrupts teammates; mitigation: post-demo, hit condition stated, hits > 0 verified, K=3 before/after, revert if no hit

Memory headroom is 9 GB free / 11 GB available today (changed by 3-8 GB within a day); mitigation: recorded in every fingerprint; any student or specialist model is conditional on stopping the vision service in an agreed window, trained and served sequentially with MAX_JOBS capped

Shared graph schema drift (the 7688 instance) would invalidate gold Cypher, templates and the schema check; mitigation: benchmark pinned to the private snapshot, run_bench/snapshot/restore refuse 7688
Self-judged metrics carry self-preference bias; mitigation: headline grounding metric is deterministic; any LLM judge is calibrated on ~80 human labels with kappa reported or not reported at all

Over-claiming novelty (slot templates are template NLG; the three-tier router is Neo4j's published guidance); mitigation: benchmark-first framing, explicit prior art (Reiter & Dale, TeCoD, PICARD, Huawei GQL grammar, Ozsoy 2026, Zhong 2020), 'cost model' kept as design rationale only

# RescueGrid answer layer: architecture decision, baseline, roadmap (revised after red-team review, 2026-09-25)

## 0. What is actually on the box today (measured)

- **Code**: `/home/hp2/kenil/rescuegrid-reasoning` at HEAD `8d1c86c` (7 commits; tags `baseline-v0`, `features-v1`), with four **untracked** ladder result files (`all-auto`, `all-llm`, `l1-entity`, `l2-entity-schema` at `8d1c86c`, produced from a dirty tree). `bench/questions.json` has 60 questions (fields: id, question, category, answerable, gold_cypher, compare, must_mention, must_not_mention, note; **no** gold highlight id, seed id or phrasing tier). Six feature flags exist in `rescuegrid/qa/features.py`. The baseline prompt is pinned verbatim (2,710 tokens = schema 815 + rules 304 + 11 V0 few-shots 1,591; `ANSWER_SYSTEM` 504).
- **Server**: vLLM 0.26.0 serving `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8` as `llm` with only `--max-model-len=32768 --trust-remote-code`; `enable_prefix_caching=False`, attention block 4,176 tokens, fp8 KV, no speculative decoding (`/opt/hp/zrt/run/vllm-llm.json`). `free -g` today: **9 GB free / 11 GB available** (the task context's 19 GB and the earlier 12-14 GB are stale).
- **Baseline run** (`baseline-llm-6d30e04.json`, llm mode): correct 0.733, exec_acc 0.804, grounded 0.944, facts 0.741, abstain 6/6, 4,377 prompt + 221 completion tokens per LLM question over 2.14 calls, p50 5.08 s, p95 11.62 s, 18 repairs, 0 guard rejections. RS_0 0.73, RS_1 0.47, **RS_10 -1.93**. Modes used: llm 54, **llm+fallback 4** (rt01, rt04, rt05, cf04: the template answered when the model failed), fallback 1, error 1. rt01/rt04/pp03 have no gold rows (exec_acc=None counts as correct today).
- **Contamination (verified)**: `EXAMPLES_V2` in `rescuegrid/qa/fewshot.py` contains **six benchmark questions verbatim** (rt01, px04, cf01, tm07, un01, st01) and near-duplicates of tm01/tm02/na03 (token Jaccard 0.75-0.80); the V0 bank contains rt01 verbatim and tm01/tm02 near-duplicates. `schema_check.py`'s docstring says it "catches the failure classes the benchmark exposed". The 60 questions are therefore a **dev set** that has already been tuned against.
- **The all-flags run re-read** (`all-llm-8d1c86c.json` vs `baseline-llm-6d30e04.json`): 0.800 vs 0.733 overall, but fixed = {st06, st07, tm05, tm07, px04, rt05, ag01, cf01} of which **tm07, px04, cf01 are leaked**, broke = {pv05, px02, rt02, ag03}; on the **51 uncontaminated questions it is 40/51 vs 39/51 (+1 question)**; repairs 18 -> 29, calls 2.14 -> 2.42, p50 5.08 -> 5.79 s, guard rejections 0 -> 2, three `finish=length` truncations; prompt tokens did fall 4,377 -> 2,477. `l1-entity`: 0.717, repairs 24; `l2-entity-schema`: 0.717, repairs 33, error rate 0.067, p95 13.55 s. Static schema checking as implemented **adds rounds without rescuing questions**.
- **Latency outliers are bugs**: px02 (21.7 s, error) hit `finish=length` at 320 tokens three times with a degenerate projection; `extract_cypher`'s fence regex requires a closing fence, so the truncated output kept its leading ```` ```cypher ```` and was rejected by the guard twice, and the truncated query was re-fed as the "previous query". rt01 (17.4 s) spent 3 x ~250 completion tokens before falling back **although its question is verbatim in the V0 bank** (leakage does not even guarantee a pass). The OpenAI client has `max_retries=1` and a 120 s timeout, so hidden retries are outside the ledger.
- **Grounding metric is not what it claims**: `run_bench.py` appends conflict/provenance rows the engine did not use (tm02 is flagged ungrounded by the bench but not by the engine); zero-row wrong answers score grounded=True (st06, st07, pv03, px04); the **existing deterministic renderers fail the check** (tm07 in auto mode prints the window boundary; the route renderer cites road times absent from its evidence rows).
- **Cost arithmetic (design rationale, not a contribution)**: decode ~45 tok/s vs prefill ~5.5k tok/s, so one completion token costs the wall time of ~120 prompt tokens; output tokens and call count are the levers, prompt compression is worth <= 0.5 s.

## 1. Decision

**LLM + KG via text-to-Cypher stays the core; the benchmark becomes the research object; the answer layer is engineering adopted only under a pre-specified test.**

| Tier | Trigger | Model work | Answer | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (exists) | regex intent router, 7 intents | none | parameterised Cypher -> deterministic renderer, reconciled with the grounding check | demo path for scripted questions |
| 2 (post-demo) | `guided_choice` intent with **intent-token logprob gate** + deterministic slot validation + regex/BM25 agreement | ~250 prompt + ~30 completion tokens; miss path measured | template library 7 -> ~13, designed from the EOC taxonomy on the dev split | adopted only if coverage-vs-false-route and tail p50 with router pass |
| 3 (exists, fixed) | everything else | pinned prompt now; compact schema + decontaminated dynamic few-shots after R2 -> Cypher; parser fixes (D1); repair budget by ablation (R3) | LLM json_schema compose now; row-only renderer for two shapes (D2); slot-bound answer template post-demo (R5) | per-call timeout with an honest `abstain_reason=timeout` |

Every path still runs the read-only guard, a read transaction, `_finish()` and `fact_check`. This follows Neo4j's guidance to use parameterised Cypher for common questions and Text2Cypher as the fallback ([Neo4j Text2Cypher guide](https://neo4j.com/blog/genai/text2cypher-guide/)); TeCoD ([arXiv 2604.28028](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.28028)) is the closest prior art for template routing and is cited as such, **without** quoting its BIRD gains as an expectation here.

## 2. Why not the alternatives

| Alternative | Verdict | Reason (with numbers) |
|---|---|---|
| LLM-only, whole graph in prompt | reference row | 7.6-8.9k tokens now, 15-60k at 100-500 events vs 32,768 max; probe invented an entity; no rows -> no provenance/highlight/fact-check |
| Vector RAG over event text | no | cannot express time windows, sums, routes, conflicts; fulltext clause already allowlisted |
| GraphRAG / LightRAG / HippoRAG / ToG | no | build a graph from text; ours exists and is queried exactly; graphs help multi-hop over corpora, not fact lookups ([2502.11371](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.11371), [GraphRAG-Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05690)) |
| Agentic ReAct / MCP loop | no | tool-parser relaunch; 3-4x calls at ~3 s; Neo4j's MCP agent 0.71 with Claude 3.7 Sonnet at 3.6 calls/q ([Neo4j](https://neo4j.com/blog/developer/evaluating-graph-retrieval-in-mcp-agentic-systems/)); Nemotron BFCL v4 53.2 ([model card](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8)) |
| DIN-SQL / MAC-SQL / schema linking | no | schema fits (815 tokens); linking costs 2.7-4.8 EX when it fits ([2408.07702](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.07702)) |
| **entity_link + schema_check as the fix** | ablation only | measured 0.717 / repairs 24 and 0.717 / repairs 33 / error 0.067 at `8d1c86c`; written from dev failures |
| **fewshot_v2 + dyn_fewshot on the 8d1c86c evidence** | decontaminate first | 6 verbatim + 3 near-dup leaks; +1 unseen question; 4 broke |
| LoRA on the 30B; hybrid students | no | ~60 GB for 16-bit LoRA ([Unsloth](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/nemotron-3)) vs 9-11 GB; FP8 base; missing sm_121a kernels |
| Speculative decoding now | no | no MTP head; ngram on hybrid recurrent models silently corrupts ([vLLM #56531](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56531)); already reverted |
| LLMLingua-2 compression | negative row | ceiling ~0.35 s; deletes schema identifiers ([2403.12968](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12968)) |
| Schema-compiled grammar as thesis | ablation | 0 guard rejections in baseline; 3/3 probes grammatical-but-wrong; empties 0 -> 24 -> 36 ([Ozsoy 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.10318), verified in the paper body) |
| **8 s deadline returning 'no matching records'** | replaced | px02 is a parser bug; a timeout message that claims no records is false and scores as an abstention |
| **Tier-2 router before the demo, self-reported confidence gate** | post-demo, logprob gate | uncalibrated; miss path 72 completion tokens / 3.74 s under load; regex router already gives temporal 0.43 in auto |
| **RS_10 as primary** | secondary | baseline -1.93; all-abstain about +0.1; answer-30-refuse-24 about +0.6 |
| Neo4j Gemma-3-4B specialist | no | does not fit in 9-11 GB without stopping vision; no published accuracy |
| Server relaunch before demo | post-demo | <= 0.7 s upside only if the static prefix exceeds one Mamba block ([vLLM #46384](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46384)) |

## 3. Baseline (`baseline-v1`, frozen in D0)

Code HEAD `8d1c86c` + committed ladder files + the ledger changes below; `QA_FEATURES` unset; `LLM_THINKING=false`; T=0; call A `max_tokens=320`; call B json_schema `COMPOSE_MAX_TOKENS=320`; `max_repairs=2` + zero-row retry; one fact-check regeneration; client `max_retries=1`/120 s (recorded, changed in D1); graph from `bench/snapshots/baseline-v0/graph.json` (sha256 `7f101435...`) with `RESCUEGRID_CLOCK=replay`; `bench/questions.json` (sha256 `fea4829d...`) with gold rows added for rt01/rt04/pp03; server as in section 0; idle box.

```
for k in 1 2 3; do for m in llm auto llm-pure; do

Ledger additions to `run_bench.py` before running: (a) a **role** per call (`cypher`, `repair_k`, `zero_row_retry`, `compose`, `compose_retry`, `router`) via a context variable, so `repairs` stops meaning "non-json calls minus 1"; (b) a **fingerprint** block: git sha + dirty-tree flag, sha256 of `SCHEMA_TEXT`, `ANSWER_SYSTEM` and the **rendered few-shot bank**, sha256 of `questions.json` and the snapshot, `vllm-llm.json`, vLLM version, `QA_FEATURES`, K, temperature, free/available memory, vLLM running-request gauge; (c) **per-run `seen` ids** (verbatim or token-Jaccard >= 0.7 to any bank question) and `Correct_unseen`; (d) **K repeats** with Wilson CI, seed-clustered SE, `pass^3`, paired bootstrap and exact McNemar vs a named file ([Miller 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.00640), [tau-bench pass^k](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12045)); (e) `--mode llm-pure` (`allow_fallback=False`) and per-`mode_used` counts. Reproducibility = majority-of-K agreement >= 90% of questions and tokens within 5% (not "within the CI", which anything satisfies at +/-11 pp).

## 4. Metrics

**Correct_unseen (primary)** = for answerable questions EX and Grounded and Facts and mode != error (HighlightAcc joins once gold highlight ids exist); for unanswerable questions an explicit abstention; restricted to ids not flagged `seen` for that run's bank. **Acceptance rule** for adopting any change: lower bound of the 90% paired-bootstrap interval on the mean-of-K difference > -3 pp, no category loses more than one question, repairs and p95 not worse, AbstentionRecall not lower, **FalseRefusal <= 5%**; n=60 cannot certify gains below ~10 pp, so gains are claimed only on the held-out set. **EX_strict** = multiset row equality against **any accepted gold shape** (count or list; ordered iff gold has ORDER BY; CypherBench semantics, [scorer](https://github.com/megagonlabs/cypherbench/blob/main/cypherbench/metrics/execution_accuracy.py)); **EX_key** lenient secondary; **EvJ** entity-id Jaccard; **EX_multi** = min over 4-6 replayed snapshots ([Zhong et al. 2020](https://aclanthology.org/2020.emnlp-main.29/)). **Grounded** over answered-with-rows questions only, same `fact_check` inputs in engine and bench, with **GroundedCoverage** alongside; "by construction" is a unit-tested property limited to sources/times/confidences/percentages. **Facts**, **HighlightAcc** (post-demo). **AbstentionRecall / FalseRefusal** from explicit `answerable` / `abstain_reason` fields; `mode=error` never counts. **RS_c** ([TrustSQL](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.15879v6)) at c in {0, 1, 10}, RS_1 on the Pareto chart, RS_10 reported not optimised. **pass^3**, **ConsistencyRate**. **Tokens by role**, truncation and guard counts, cached_tokens when exposed. **Latency** p50/p95, LLM-seconds, timeouts, load and memory. **TokensPerCorrect / SecondsPerCorrect** ([Cost-of-Pass](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13359)). **Router** coverage-vs-false-route curve ([selective classification](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.08500)). **Seen flag + bank hash**. **Error taxonomy** with a second annotator on 20 items.
